The people of the Fire ask the people of Jannah for water
A bed of Jahannam and coverings of fire over them
Scorching wind, boiling water and a shade of black smoke for those who lived in luxury
Keepers ask each group whether a warner came; they admit it and say had we listened or reasoned
Disbelievers driven to Jahannam in groups, its gates opened as they arrive
The regret of the one who wishes he had sent ahead for his life, which disciplined worship now is meant to prevent.
Rivers of water, non-intoxicating wine, honey and milk in Paradise
They await only a single blast that seizes them while they dispute, with no chance to make a bequest or return to their families.
The first quake followed by the second: the two blows of the horn.
Taking one's desires as a god counts among the partners asked about.
Some love others as they should love Allah, while believers love Allah most.
The people of Paradise are joyfully occupied, so eternity there is never boring.
The Day every soul comes arguing for itself and is repaid for what it did; you stand alone with your choices.
The people of the heights between Jannah and the Fire
Enter among My servants and enter My Jannah
Their call in Jannah is glorification and praise of Allah
Praise to Allah who removed grief; no fatigue or weariness there
You recognise in their faces the radiance of bliss
They hear no idle or hurtful speech
No soul knows the joy hidden for them
Judged with truth and it is said: all praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds
Coming to Allah alone as He created you the first time.
Belief in the Day of Judgment is included among the traits of those who pray and give.
The garden owners finding their land burnt and passing through grief and denial
The wish to be turned into dust
Nuh called his people night and day, publicly and privately; he will present this case
When the soul reaches the throat, angels are closer than the onlookers; bring it back if you can.
When it reaches the collarbones and leg is wrapped with leg, the drive is to your Lord.
Angels extend their hands to take the souls of wrongdoers in humiliation.
The record of the righteous is in Illiyyin.
The record of the wicked is in Sijjin.
The gates of heaven are not opened for those who denied.
Who raised us from our sleeping place? This is what the Most Merciful promised
They ask about the mountains; say my Lord will blast them away
The seas set ablaze
That day you will be exposed; nothing of you hidden
Whoever is given his book in his right hand says come, read my book
The one given his book in his left hand wishes he had never lived; his wealth and authority are gone
No injustice today, Allah is swift in reckoning; warn them of the approaching day when hearts are at the throats
Nuh is told not to address Allah about the wrongdoers
Ibrahim is told to turn away from pleading for Lut's people
Those who cast accusations at chaste women
You are repaid only for what you did, except Allah's chosen servants: the recurring exception to strict recompense.
That Day you will not know your mother, father or children.
Repentance is not for those who wait until death comes.
Let every soul look at what it has prepared for tomorrow, meaning the life after the grave, not the next ten years.
The first command, qum, to stand in the night: taking a stand for yourself.
Qum and warn: taking a stand for the world, from the same root as Qiyamah.
Paradise promised to those who stay the course, recited as a sample of what Allah has prepared.
'What will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near': the 'ma yudrika' form for what we will not be told, contrasted with 'ma adraka' used here (33:63 has the same wording)
Al-Kawthar given to the Prophet, linked to his basin
Believers' light running before them and the good news of Jannah
Were we not with you? You deceived yourselves; no ransom accepted
Has the time not come for believers' hearts to humble themselves
The orchard owner's denial of the Hour, answered by 'you claimed We would not make an appointment'.
Musa swooned when he asked to see Allah, a possible reason he is spared at the blow.
People love the immediate and leave behind them a heavy day.
A day that turns children grey-haired.
The day secrets are laid bare.
People like scattered moths and mountains like carded wool.
The sky splits and the earth casts out what it holds, both obeying their Lord.
The earth quakes and throws out its burdens, man asks what is wrong with it, and it reports its news.
The sky breaks apart, the planets scatter, the seas erupt and the graves are overturned.
The sky sways and the mountains drift away.
Allah folds the heavens like a scroll and repeats creation as He began it.
The stars are extinguished and the sky is opened.
The cover is removed and sight is sharp that day.
The sky splits open with clouds.
The inevitable event lowers some and raises others, shakes the earth and crumbles the mountains to dust.
Which of your Lord's favours would you deny: the bounties we cannot repay
Few of Allah's servants are grateful, the reason to pray to be among the few
They swear to Allah as they swore to people, thinking they are on something; they are the liars
Those who restrain anger, to explain the meaning of ghayz.

hadith.gist: Allah has prepared for His righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard and no human heart has ever imagined.
Ihsan is to worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you.
After crossing the bridge over Hell, the believers are held at an arched bridge before entering Paradise.
Allah permits the believers who are saved to intercede for their brothers and bring them out of the Fire.
The first people the Fire is kindled with are a man who fought to be called brave, a man who gave to be called generous and a man who learned or recited the Quran to be called a scholar or reciter
On that day the prophets can only plead, O Allah, grant safety
Aisha asked whether people will remember their loved ones; there are moments when no one remembers anyone, including when the books fly and when the scales are set
Nothing is heavier on the scale than good character
A man brings ninety-nine scrolls of sins, each stretching to the horizon, and is saved by one card bearing the testimony of tawhid
The dead person hears the footsteps of those leaving after burial.
In the grave prayer stands at the head, fasting and charity at the sides and other good deeds at the feet, each blocking punishment's approach.

A man is thrown into the Fire, his entrails spill out and he circles them like a donkey at a millstone; the people of the Fire ask what happened and he says he commanded good but did not do it and forbade evil but did it.
hadith.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, from Usamah ibn Zayd

hadith.gist: The Prophet called his uncle Abbas, his aunt Safiyyah and his daughter Fatimah: save yourselves from the Fire, I cannot avail you anything against Allah
End-times narrations that a promised figure will come back before the Hour, which people cite as a reason to sit back and wait
A man asked the Prophet when the Hour would be; he replied by asking what he had prepared for it
The most luxurious person is dipped once in hell and forgets all good; the most miserable is dipped in paradise and forgets all hardship
On his journey the Prophet passed Malik, keeper of the Fire, who alone did not smile, and was told he has not smiled since he was created.
The fire of this world is a seventieth part of the fire of Hell.
The most miserable person of this world is dipped once in Paradise and the most comfortable once in Hell; each forgets every hardship or comfort.
The grave is the first stage of the hereafter; whoever is saved from it finds what follows easier, and whoever is not finds what follows harder.
The deceased hears the footsteps of the people walking away from the grave.
In the grave the believer's prayer comes to his head, his fasting to one side and his charity to the other to protect him.
The Prophet's dream in which two angels showed him punishments in the barzakh, including the head crushed with a rock, the river of blood and the burning oven, then explained the sin behind each.
How can I enjoy life when the angel of the horn has put it to his mouth and is waiting to be commanded to blow?

Paragraph seven: I am waiting for you at the basin and I will boast of your numbers before the nations; some I will try to save will be taken from me, I will say 'my companions', and be told you do not know what they changed after you; then he will say 'away with them'.
Paragraph eight: inheritance shares and lineage must be preserved; no one is cut out, no one takes more than his share, and no one claims a family that is not his.
For the believer the Day of Judgment will feel as short as the time of a prayer.
Every religion has its core ethic, and the ethic of Islam is haya
Allah has people He frees from the Fire every night of Ramadan.
Aisha said only the shoulder of the sheep remained; he said all of it remains except its shoulder.
Mus'ab ibn Umayr was shrouded in a cloth that could not cover both his head and feet.
No one with an atom's weight of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise.
Hell is brought forth on the Day of Judgment with seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels.
During the battle of Mu'tah the Prophet described the three commanders' deaths and saw them in Paradise, Ibn Rawahah slightly lower for a moment's hesitation.
The last man to leave Hell is restored in a river of life, asks for tree after tree, and is finally given ten times the dominion of the greatest king.
The highest people of Paradise look upon their Lord morning and evening.
The last person to leave Hell and enter Paradise is given a dominion many times the size of the world.
The highest people of Paradise look at the face of Allah morning and evening.
Some of this ummah will bring many deeds that carry no weight on the scale because they are empty inside.
A large man will come on the Day of Judgment and carry no weight at all.
A man with ninety-nine records of bad deeds is saved when a single card bearing la ilaha illallah is placed on the scale and outweighs them.
hadith.source: he names Muslim; it is recorded by al-Tirmidhi

hadith.gist: Allah folds the heavens in His right hand and the earth in His left and says: I am the King, where are the tyrants, where are the arrogant
Allah descends to the lowest heaven in the last part of the night saying: I am the King, who calls on Me that I may answer, who asks that I may give, who seeks forgiveness that I may forgive
Hell will be brought on the Day with 70,000 reins, each held by 70,000 angels
The sun is brought within a mile of people and they sweat according to their deeds, some to the ankles, knees or waist, and some bridled by it to the mouth.

Seven whom Allah shades on the day there is no shade but His: the just ruler, a youth raised in worship, a man whose heart is attached to the masjid, two who love each other for Allah, one who refuses a woman of status and beauty saying I fear Allah, one who gives charity so secretly his left hand does not know, and one who remembers Allah alone and his eyes flow with tears.
Every betrayer will have a banner on the Day of Judgment proclaiming his betrayal, and there is no betrayer worse than a leader of the public.
The last person to leave Hell keeps asking for a little more and is finally given ten times the dominion of the greatest king
hadith.source: Ahmad, Abu Dawud; part in Muslim

hadith.gist: At certain moments of the Day of Judgment no one remembers anyone else, not even children, parents or spouse.
They told As'ad to lower his hand, saying they would never abandon this pledge or ask to be released from it, and raced to pledge.
On the Night Journey the Prophet saw Adam with his descendants on his right, at whom he smiled, and on his left, at whom he wept
On the Day of Judgment people run to the prophets asking them to intercede
No one enters Paradise by his deeds alone
People cross the bridge over Hell at different speeds: like a blink, lightning, wind, a fast horse, running, walking or crawling.
At three moments no one remembers anyone else: when the books are distributed, at the bridge, and at the scales.
Companions said a fallen fighter was in Jannah; the Prophet revealed he had taken his own life and forbade such claims.
Allah frees people from the Fire every night of Ramadan
Three people Allah will not look at on the Day of Judgement, among them the one who mistreats his parents and those who fail their basic roles in the family
Three people Allah will not speak to or purify and who will have a painful punishment: an elderly fornicator, a lying king and an arrogant poor man
Those who have much in this world will have the least on the Day of Judgement, except one who spends it this way and that way (with a gesture of giving)
Jahannam will be brought on that Day with seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels
Jahannam will be brought with seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels

Whoever makes the hereafter his concern, Allah puts his richness in his heart, gathers his affairs and the world comes to him humbled; whoever makes the world his concern, Allah puts his poverty between his eyes, scatters his affairs and he gets of the world only what was decreed.
When you ask Allah for Jannah, ask for al-Firdaws, its highest part
Hadith qudsi: My servants, it is only your deeds that I count for you and then repay you; whoever finds good should praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise should blame only himself.
After the Prophet gave away a sheep, Aisha said only the shoulder was left; he replied that all of it remains except its shoulder.

Aisha asked whether people will remember their loved ones on the Day of Judgment; the Prophet said in three places no one remembers anyone, among them when the books fly, until one knows whether his falls in his right or left hand.
People are gathered barefoot, unclothed and uncircumcised; Aisha asked about men and women seeing each other and was told the matter is too severe for that.
Ibrahim is the first to be clothed on the Day of Judgment.
The Prophet saw people in shirts of varying length, some to the neck, some lower, one dragging his, interpreted as the deen.
The arrogant are gathered like ants in human form, trampled by people.
People are gathered in three groups: walking, riding, and on their faces.
Those who love each other for Allah's sake will be on raised places of light that the prophets admire.
For the believer the long Day will feel as short as an obligatory prayer.
The most miserable person of this world is dipped once in Paradise and asked if he ever saw misery; he says he never did.
The fasting person has two joys: when he breaks his fast and when he meets his Lord; the fasting enter by the gate of al-Rayyan.
Allah tells the servant in Paradise to wish, then reminds him of things he forgot until he says he is satisfied.
On the Day of Judgment Allah declares: I am the King, where are the kings of the earth? I am the Compeller, where are the tyrants?
Seven whom Allah shades on the day when there is no shade but His, among them the just ruler, the youth raised in worship and the one whose heart is attached to the masjid.
At the Basin some are driven away and the Prophet is told: you do not know what they introduced after you.
Asked what he saw on the Ascension, the Prophet said: light.
Whoever loves meeting Allah, Allah loves meeting him.
Hadith qudsi: whoever draws near Me a span, I draw near him an arm's length.
Allah frees people from the Fire every night of Ramadan
Jahannam will be brought on the Day of Judgment with seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels
The person who lived in the most luxury is dipped once in the Fire and asked if he ever saw any good; he says never
Hadith qudsi: every deed of the son of Adam is for him except fasting; it is Mine and I reward it
Seventy thousand angels enter the Frequented House each day and never return.
Ibrahim on the night of the ascension: Paradise has good soil and open land, its plants are glorifications of Allah.
No one enters paradise by his deeds alone.
The Hour will come while two men have spread a garment between them and not finished their sale, and a man raises food to his mouth and does not eat it.
Allah will fold the heavens and the earth and say: I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?
On the Day of Resurrection people will be in sweat according to their deeds, to their ankles, knees, waists or mouths.

Seven are shaded by Allah on the day there is no shade but His: the just ruler, the youth raised in worship, the one attached to the masjid, two who love for Allah, the one who refuses temptation, the secret giver and the one who weeps remembering Allah alone.
The first judged and thrown into the Fire are a reciter, a scholar, a martyr and a generous man who acted to be praised.
Jahannam is brought with seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels.
The Fire was kindled a thousand years until red, a thousand until white and a thousand until black.
The Prophet's basin is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey with cups as many as the stars; some will be driven away and he will be told he does not know what they changed after him.
On the bridge people pass like lightning, wind and swift horses, with hooks that snatch them.
Allah has a hundred mercies; He sent one to earth and kept ninety-nine for the Day of Resurrection.
Verse 2:281 was the last revelation the Prophet received
Some will stand before Allah so ashamed of their deeds that the flesh of their faces falls away
The great intercession: people go from prophet to prophet, each says Allah is angrier today than ever before or after and worries for himself
An angel is appointed to blow the trumpet; the first blast ends all life and the second brings it back
The Prophet likened himself to a man holding people back by their belts from a fire that moths keep flying into
I go ahead of you to the Basin; your appointment with me is at the Basin.
Asked whether anyone would be better than the companions, he spoke of people after them who believe in him without seeing him.
The great intercession: people go to Adam, Ibrahim, Musa and others, then to him; he prostrates and says my ummah, my ummah.
No one sends salam on me but Allah returns my soul to me so I reply.
Hellfire was kindled for a thousand years until it was red, a thousand until it was white and a thousand until it was black
After the first blast the angel of death takes every life, then the trumpeter's, then his own; Allah alone remains, then revives the trumpeter, who blows again
On the Day people go to the prophets for help and the prophets say: O Allah, grant safety
Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him
Hadith qudsi: it is only your deeds that I record for you and then repay; whoever finds good should praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise should blame only himself.
The angels kept shading Abdullah ibn Amr with their wings until he was carried away
Allah spoke to Jabir's father face to face and asked him to wish; he asked to return and be killed again, Allah said none return, and the verse 'do not think those killed are dead' was revealed
A man in Jannah asks his Lord to let him farm and is allowed
A man asked when the Hour is; the Prophet replied, what have you prepared for it?
The Hour will come while a man is repairing his basin, another lifting a morsel to his mouth, and two men spreading a garment they will never finish trading.
After the first blast only a few remain; the angel of death is commanded to take their lives and finally his own.
Allah created a hundred portions of mercy, sent one to the earth from which all creatures show compassion, and keeps ninety-nine for the Day of Judgement
So much mercy is spread that day that even Iblis raises his head hoping to receive some (he notes it has questions of authenticity)
A share of every unjust killing goes to the son of Adam who first committed murder, because he started the practice
A man whose minor sins are turned into good deeds begins asking about the major sins he cannot find, and the Prophet laughed
The first matter judged between people on the Day of Judgement is bloodshed
The first deed a servant is asked about is the prayer
Whoever is closely questioned in the reckoning is ruined
A person will be with those he loves on the Day of Judgment.
The Prophet will be the first to knock at the gate of Paradise and have it opened.
The Prophet visited a dying boy who used to serve him, invited him to Islam, and left praising Allah for saving him from the Fire.

The long hadith of intercession: people in distress go to Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and Isa, each saying 'myself' and citing a reason, until they come to Muhammad, who prostrates under the Throne, praises Allah, is told to raise his head and intercede, and asks for his nation.
What I fear most for you is two things: following desire, which turns you from the truth, and long hope, which makes you forget the Hereafter
hadith.source: Ahmad (he grades it hasan); also from Ali

hadith.gist: Ali: the world is departing and the Hereafter approaching, each has its children; be children of the Hereafter, for today is action without reckoning and tomorrow reckoning without action
Saying he cites with the name of Anas ibn Malik: procrastination is one of Satan's great soldiers, with which he has deceived many
There was Allah and nothing with Him
The Prophet said he had seen no sight more terrible than the grave.
Allah says He dislikes taking the soul of the believer because the believer dislikes death, and He dislikes grieving him.
The Hour will come while a man is mending his basin, two people have spread a garment to trade, a man carries home his milk and another raises food to his mouth, and none will finish.
Asked by Jibril about the Hour, the Prophet replied that the one questioned knows no more about it than the questioner.
Allah frees people from the Fire every night of Ramadan.
Jahannam will be brought with seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels.
Nations will call one another against the Muslims like diners to a dish; they will be many but like the foam on a flood.
On the Day of Judgment people go from prophet to prophet seeking intercession; each declines citing a lapse, and Isa declines too
The lowest dweller of paradise will have a dominion many times the size of the earth.
The believer is brought close to Allah and screened while Allah reviews his deeds privately with him
Some companions heard from the Prophet that they were in Paradise yet kept fearing standing before Allah
Allah frees people from the Fire every night of Ramadan, and more in the last ten
Jahannam will be brought with reins, each held by seventy thousand angels
Hadith qudsi: every deed of the son of Adam is for him except fasting; it is Mine and I reward it
The Prophet told his relatives: ask me whatever you want of my wealth and I will give it, but I cannot save you from the Fire; you must do that yourselves.

Allah asks the people of Paradise if they want anything more; they ask what could be better, then the veil is lifted and nothing they were given is dearer to them than looking at their Lord, seen as clearly as the full moon.
Every traitor will have a banner on the Day of Judgment proclaiming his betrayal
People will be raised barefoot and naked; when 'A'ishah asked about men and women seeing each other, he said the matter is too severe for that
Ibrahim will be the first to be clothed on the Day of Judgment
The Prophet saw people in shirts reaching the chest or lower, and 'Umar dragging his; he interpreted it as the deen
In Jannah a person looks at something he desires and it comes near him
On the Day of Judgment a prophet will come with no one who followed him
The grave is the first stage of the hereafter; whoever is saved from it finds what follows easier, and whoever is not finds what follows harder.
The grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of Hell.
If you knew what I know you would laugh little and weep much, and would not enjoy your spouses
Allah sent Jibril to look at Jahannam; he said no one would enter it, then it was surrounded by desires and he feared no one would escape it
If a tiny opening were made in Jahannam toward this world it would burn everything
The person who lived the most comfortable life is dipped once in the Fire and asked if he ever saw any good; he says never
The Prophet likened himself to a man holding people back by their waists from falling into a fire like moths
At Badr the Prophet addressed the fallen Quraysh, asking if they found their Lord's promise true
The people of the highest rank in Jannah look upon Allah's face morning and evening.
Asked how there is light in Paradise without a sun, the Prophet said its land gives light

The Prophet said he could not enjoy life knowing the angel of the horn was ready to blow; when the companions were distressed he told them to say: Allah is sufficient for us, the best disposer of affairs, and upon Allah we rely.
The first to hear the horn will be a man mending his camels' water trough; he will collapse, and then all the people.

The Hour will come while two men have spread a garment between them and never complete the sale or fold it, a man carries his milk and never drinks it, a man fixes his basin and never uses it, and a man raises a morsel and never eats it.
After the first blow Allah orders the angel of death to take the life of the angel of the horn and then his own; between the two blows is a span of forty.
Hellfire will be brought on that day with seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels.
Allah draws the believer close on the Day of Judgement, makes him acknowledge his sins, then says He concealed them in the world and forgives them today.
Death is brought in the form of a ram, placed between Paradise and Hell and slaughtered, and no one will die again.

Farewell Sermon: I will wait for you at the Basin and boast of your numbers, so do not disgrace me; some will be driven away and I will be told you do not know what they changed after you, and I will say away with them.
Whoever visits or cares for a sick person remains in the khurfah (harvest) of Paradise until he returns.
Whoever visits a sick person, a caller from heaven calls out: you have done well, your walking is good, and you have taken a dwelling in Paradise.
Paradise holds what no eye has seen, no ear has heard and no heart has imagined
Whoever drinks from the Prophet's basin will never thirst again
The Prophet is the first to knock on the door of Jannah; the keeper says he was told to open it for no one before him
The hearts of the people of Jannah are like the heart of one man, glorifying Allah morning and evening
Allah prepared for His righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard and no heart has imagined
The last man to enter Jannah keeps asking for one more tree, is let in, and is given the like of the world many times over
The lowest person in Jannah needs a thousand years to see what he owns; for the highest, Allah planted their honour with His own hand and sealed it
The people of Jannah gather each week, Allah addresses them and they return more beautiful
Allah asks the people of Jannah if they are pleased, then grants them His pleasure and will never be displeased with them
Death is brought in a living form and slaughtered, and no one dies again
The righteous, angels and prophets intercede and bring people out of the Fire, then the Most Merciful Himself brings out others
Hadith qudsi on Al-Fatihah: 'You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help' is between Me and My servant.
Hell will be brought on the Day of Judgement with seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels
Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it; when it shook, the Prophet told it to be still as a prophet stood on it
The Prophet named many mountains around Madinah
On the Day, prophets come with a group, with one or two men, or with no one at all
People cross the bridge over Hell at speeds matching their deeds: like the blink of an eye, lightning, wind, horses, running, walking and crawling.
The bridge over Hell is extremely narrow and hard to cross.
Hooks along the bridge snatch at people as they cross.
The long narration of al-Bara' ibn Azib describing the departure, ascent and grave of the believing and the disbelieving soul.
The Hour will strike while two men are agreeing a sale and a man is raising food to his mouth
Allah folds creation and says: I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?
On the Day of Judgment Allah's anger is such as never before and never after
The arrogant are gathered like ants and trampled
The sun is brought near and people stand in sweat according to their deeds, up to ankles, knees, waists or mouths
Seven are shaded by Allah's shade on the day there is no shade but His
Jahannam is brought with seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels
The first judged and thrown into the Fire are a martyr, a scholar and reciter, and a generous man who acted to be praised
The Fire was stoked a thousand years until red, a thousand until white, a thousand until black
The Prophet's basin is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, scented with musk, its cups like stars; whoever drinks never thirsts again
Some are driven from the basin and the Prophet is told: you do not know what they changed after you
People cross the bridge over Hell at different speeds, like a blink, lightning, wind or horses, with hooks snatching some
The Prophet prostrates under the Throne and is told: raise your head, ask and you will be given, intercede and it will be accepted
Allah made a hundred mercies, sent one to the world and will add it to the ninety-nine on the Day of Judgment
Allah conceals the believer while reviewing his sins and forgives them
No one's feet move on that day until asked about his life, youth, wealth and knowledge
Allah tells the people of Paradise He bestows His pleasure on them and will never be displeased with them
Allah frees people from the Fire every night of Ramadan.
Hell is brought on the Day of Judgement with 70,000 reins, each held by 70,000 angels.
Before his death the Prophet told people that anyone he had struck could take retribution from his back and anyone whose wealth he had taken could take it back.
No one did the Prophet a favour except that he repaid it, except Abu Bakr, whose favour Allah will repay; every door into the masjid was to be closed except Abu Bakr's.
Jibril told the Prophet to ask Abu Bakr, dressed in a sack after giving everything away, whether he was pleased with his Lord, for his Lord was pleased with him.
A poor man people would ignore is better than an earthful of the nobleman they honour.
A huge, fat man will come on the Day of Resurrection and weigh less than the wing of a mosquito.
People will come with deeds like mountains that Allah makes scattered dust; they pray at night like you, but when alone with Allah's prohibitions they violate them.
A man with ninety-nine scrolls of sins is saved by a single card bearing the testimony of faith, which outweighs them all.
Between the two blowings of the trumpet is forty; no one knows forty of what.
After the trumpet, the angel of death is commanded to take the life of the trumpet's blower, then of Jibril, then his own, until only Allah remains.
Allah has prepared for His servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard and no heart has imagined
Allah frees people from the Fire every night of Ramadan
Hadith qudsi: every deed of the son of Adam is for him except fasting; it is Mine and I reward it
Allah created a door of repentance, as wide as the distance between east and west, before creating the people, and it remains open until the sun rises from the west.
Allah made mercy in a hundred parts and sent one to earth, by which creatures show compassion, even an animal lifting its hoof from its young; the remaining ninety-nine are for the Day of Judgment.
Jibril came to the Prophet carrying Allah's salam to Khadijah and the glad tidings of a house of hollow pearl in paradise with no noise and no fatigue.
During the Ascension the Prophet met Ibrahim in the seventh heaven reclining against the Bayt al-Ma'mur.

Allah is happier with His servant's repentance than a man who lost his camel and provisions in the desert, lay down to die, and found it returned, saying in his joy 'You are my servant and I am your lord'.
Repentance is accepted until the death rattle and until the sun rises from the west.
Hold yourselves to account before you are held to account, and weigh your deeds before they are weighed for you (the saying usually attributed to Umar ibn al-Khattab).
The best thing I and the prophets before me said is la ilaha illa Allah
A man with ninety-nine scrolls of sins is saved when a card with the shahadah outweighs them on the scale
Allah moves the soil of Paradise and water springs out wherever He wishes.
The most pampered person of the world is dipped once in Hell and says he never saw any good; the most miserable is dipped once in Paradise and says he never knew any hardship.
The last person to enter Paradise receives a kingdom many times the size of the earth; the highest ranks see the face of their Lord morning and evening.
The Prophet died with his shield pawned; in his telling, he had pawned it to pay off someone else's debt.
The Prophet's basin is a month's journey across, whiter than silver, more fragrant than musk, and whoever drinks from it never thirsts again
The Prophet will push people from his basin as a man drives other people's camels from his trough
His ummah will be recognised by the shining marks of wudu
People will be driven away from the basin and he will be told: you do not know what they did after you
The bridge is finer than a sword's edge with hooks like the thorns of the sa'dan plant
Aisha asked whether people remember their loved ones; no one remembers anyone at the books, the scales and the bridge
People cross the bridge according to their deeds: like lightning, the blink of an eye, wind, horses, some crawling, some falling

A Muslim and a Jew argued over Muhammad and Musa and the Muslim struck him; the Prophet said not to prefer him over Musa, for he is first to wake from the blow and finds Musa holding the leg of the Throne, not knowing whether Musa woke first or was spared because of his swoon at the mountain.
No one should say that I am better than Yunus ibn Matta.
On that day people say 'myself, myself', which he explains as complete preoccupation with one's own fate.
People will be gathered on a white land like a loaf of pure bread, with no landmark on it.
The arrogant will be resurrected the size of ants and trampled by people
People will be resurrected barefoot and unclothed
On the Day of Judgment deeds take form and accompany their owner
Allah does not look at your bodies or forms but at your hearts and deeds
The Prophet told his companions their appointment with him is at the Basin
When wealth arrived from Bahrain the Prophet said it is not poverty he fears for them but that the world will be spread before them as for those before
The poor companions complained the wealthy earn more reward by giving; when the rich copied the dhikr he taught them, he said that is Allah's bounty given to whom He wills
You will see your Lord as you see the sun at midday or the full moon without clouds
When the people of Paradise enter, Allah asks if they want more, then lifts the veil, and nothing is more beloved to them than seeing Him
The lowest in Paradise and the highest who see Allah's face morning and evening

Every day the sky, the sea, the mountains and the earth ask permission to destroy the human who eats Allah's provision and serves others; Allah refuses, saying had you created them you would have My compassion for them.

maxims: It's not theater; this is actually your life
Don't overcomplicate your faith
Beware the wrath of the patient one
We fear His justice, not His mistreatment
Not to deserve His mercy, but to be worthy of it
Be greedy for your akhirah, not your dunya
Happiness from the inside out, not the outside in
Jannah is life with fear and grief removed
The truth is an expensive commodity
Be materialistic in the right way
The increase in provision is in meaning, not amount
The basic package of life

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance

lectures.title: The Quran's Outcomes for Character: Vanity and Arrogance

spans.note: Vanity is crediting yourself for what Allah facilitated; arrogance is seeing others as less, and toward a group it is racism. Both are the root of personal and communal evil and must top the list of what you cleanse from your heart.
Qarun's 'I was given it for my knowledge' is today's 'I worked hard'. Assume merit in others, never in yourself; the modern world has turned this upside down.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Value, Episode 42

spans.note: Vanity claims an unknowable share of credit; performed humility only feeds it.
Arrogance is the ranking we run against others; humility is acknowledging our weakness and equality.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Value #43 – Arrogance, Assumptions and the Fall of Iblis

spans.note: Arrogance toward others is built on assumptions and the ego's ranking system, and ends in dehumanization.
Abu Jahl's tribal pride and the exercise of serving a disliked person to break arrogance.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Value #44 — Arrogance and the Trap of Comparison

spans.note: Arrogance rests on comparison, which fails on every count: no metric, unknown starts and unknown endings.
Religious arrogance, wanting others to surpass you, and competing only with yourself.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surah Saba, Session 5 (34:22-26)

spans.note: Accept being a servant, you are not the centre of the story, and having more does not make you better.

lectures.title: Attributes of the Prophet: His Humbleness

spans.note: Humility as realism about oneself, not a performance, shown through many scenes.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Fussilat: Verses 49-54

spans.note: Claiming success as one's own and calling oneself a good person are arrogance; success is Allah's bounty.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat al-Hadid, Part 7: Verses 22-25

spans.note: Hold confidence and humility in the middle against vanity, worthlessness, arrogance and inferiority.

lectures.title: Quranic Stories: The Story of Qarun

spans.note: Qarun is the Quran's example of vanity: crediting himself and judging his own effort.

lectures.title: Outreach, The Way of Our Prophets: What If?
lectures.series: Outreach: The Way of Our Prophets

spans.note: Do not walk around thinking your faith is strong; you are only fortunate not to have been tested at your breaking point.

lectures.title: The Empty Space Ep. 6: The Sins and Solutions

spans.note: Vanity credits the self, arrogance compares; humility is realism about one's own sins and the unknown hands of others.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Jathiyah Summary

spans.note: The whole surah warns four groups against arrogance and ends with praise of Allah as its cure.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Pearls 7: Humbleness, Part 1 (Vanity)

spans.note: Humbleness as the master ethic and vanity as entitlement and expectation, with its antidote and Quranic example.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Pearls 8: Humbleness, Part 2 (Arrogance)

spans.note: Arrogance is self-worth built on comparison; humbleness is seeing reality and serving.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2025 Night 24: Arrogance and Humbleness

spans.note: Arrogance is the inner enemy; humbleness is seeing the reality of human weakness and turning to Allah at one's peak.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Yasin, Part 2 (13-19)

spans.note: Rejection of messengers and most human conflicts come from petty ego and envy, as with Pharaoh and Abu Jahl.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 8: Quranic Themes 2 - Demise of the Vain

spans.note: Vanity distorts judgment and leads to ruin, from Adam's slip to Thamud's destruction and the arrogant being denied guidance.

lectures.title: The Values of Islam: Humility and Etiquette (Tawadu' and Adab)

spans.note: Humility rests on the truth of human equality and leaving the judgment of one's deeds to Allah.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2026 Night 23: Arguing Against His Signs

spans.note: Arguing against the signs comes from arrogance, the wish to feel above others; humility is just knowing reality.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat An-Nazi'at, Part 2 (79:15-33)

spans.note: Pharaoh's arrogance can grow in anyone given power if the nafs is untamed.

lectures.title: Self-Value #39: Vanity ('Ujb)

spans.note: Vanity means claiming credit for outcomes; Qarun is the Quran's example.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Value, Episode 39

spans.note: Vanity is the reflection of low self-esteem and the claim to know what one deserves; humility opposes both vanity and arrogance.

lectures.title: Self-Value #40: Vanity, Entitlement, Expectations and Mediocrity

spans.note: Vanity as claiming credit for outcomes no one can apportion; humility as directing praise to Allah.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Value, Episode 40

spans.note: Vanity is claiming credit for outcomes we cannot measure; praise Allah and ask Him to credit us.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah #41: Self-Value Recap and the Essence of Vanity

spans.note: Vanity is claiming credit; the righteous credit Allah and fear for their endings.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Value, Episode 41

spans.note: Vanity is crediting oneself; no one knows their breaking point, so 'I would never' becomes a dua.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Value #42

spans.note: Vanity is taking credit, arrogance is ranking yourself above others, and humility is acknowledging reality.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Value, Episode 43

spans.note: Arrogance toward others rests on bad assumptions and the ego's ranking system, and it dehumanizes.

lectures.title: Descriptions of the Prophet #8: His Humility

spans.note: Humility is the master trait and the core of following the sunnah; false humility is a disease.

lectures.title: The Laws of Success and Victory 8: Genuine Connection to Allah
lectures.series: The Laws of Success and Victory

spans.note: Batar is arrogance born of confidence in wealth and power; believers must not set out to impress or intimidate.
Badr was won through inner humility; a touch of materialism among the companions was named a weakness and the ratio was eased.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Honesty, Episode 7

spans.note: Pharaoh shows how applause and self-deception can grow into claiming lordship.
Knowing your faults puts you before Allah with the humility of one at fault, which saves you.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Value, Episode 35

spans.note: Believing you are further ahead than others is a judgement of innate superiority, the root of arrogance.
Iblis and Pharaoh claimed essential superiority; the Quran uses 'better' only functionally.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Value #38

spans.note: Piety used to feel superior is the arrogance the Quran most warns about.
Vanity and arrogance are defences of insecurity, the subject of coming sessions.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Kahf, Session 8: The Ruin of the Orchard (18:40-44)

spans.note: Comparing oneself to others breeds arrogance and jealousy; assume everyone is better than you.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Kahf, Session 10: The Book That Leaves Nothing Out and Iblis's Entitlement (18:49-51)

spans.note: Iblis's sense of entitlement is the model of arrogance born of what one was given.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Kahf, Session 11: False Partners, No Way Out, and the Arguing Human (18:52-55)

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 11 (33:32-34)

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surah Saba, Session 7 (34:31-37)

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Saba, Session 10: The Five Narratives Muslims Carry

spans.note: Mistakes are ours; guidance is Allah's gift.

lectures.title: Surah Summaries: Surat Al-Muddaththir

spans.note: Refusing a recognised truth out of ego, as al-Walid did.

lectures.title: Surah Summaries: Surat An-Naziat

spans.note: Unattended arrogance grows into tyranny; we differ from Pharaoh only in opportunity.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Waqi'ah, Part 1: Verses 1-19

synth.summary: Sh. Adnan treats vanity and arrogance as the two largest character traits the Quran demands we change, and humility as the hidden law beneath victory, unity and faith itself. His core distinction, set out most fully in his October 2025 khutbah, is between vanity (ujb), crediting yourself for what Allah facilitated, even your good deeds, and arrogance (kibr), seeing others as less; aimed at a group, arrogance becomes racism. He leans on Az-Zumar 39:49-50, Qarun's claim in 28:78, Luqman's counsel in 31:18-19, Al-Isra 17:37, the hadith that an atom's weight of arrogance keeps a person out of Jannah, and the Prophet's fear of self-admiration more than sin. His distinctive angle is to find arrogance where religious people least expect it: explaining disasters as punishment, arguing with Allah's commands, the elitism of Quraysh's 'strict ones', false humility, institutional ego, superiority over less observant Muslims, and the line 'I would never be in that position'. His remedies are concrete: assume merit in others but never in yourself, remember that guidance was a gift and that you were once like those you judge, recall that Allah has veiled your breaking point, and let real knowledge expose your ignorance. He holds humility in balance with self-worth: the cosmic verses humble you while telling you everything was made for you, and knowing your shortcomings should push you toward Allah, not into self-flagellation. His models are the Prophet entering Mecca bowed over his camel, An-Nasr's command to seek forgiveness at the peak, Abu Bakr serving a blind woman, and Abu Dharr laying his head before Bilal. Over the years the theme moved from warnings tied to battles, outreach and community conflict (2023 to 2024) to a systematic Quranic treatment in the 2025 character series, and then to a tazkiyah framing of the ego in his 2026 tafseer.

sections.heading: Vanity and arrogance are two diseases the Quran puts at the top of the list
sections.intro: He separates crediting yourself (vanity) from looking down on others (arrogance), and argues both are part of human nature that must be cleansed first.

subs.heading: Vanity: taking credit for what Allah facilitated

points.text: Vanity is deciding you deserve praise for achievements that may be the natural result of the upbringing, people, intellect and wealth Allah gave you. Al-hamd is not yours; it belongs to Him because you and all you have are His.
Az-Zumar 39:49-50 shows the human who begs Allah in hardship and, once favoured, says he earned it by his own merit; earlier boasters said the same and their earnings did not save them.
Qarun's claim that he was given his wealth for his own knowledge (28:78) is the archetype, echoed today in 'I worked hard, I am smarter'. The Quran's answer to him is do not exult (28:76).
Hud 11:10 describes the person given ease after hardship who becomes exultant and boastful, and Al-Isra 17:83 the one who turns away and distances himself when favoured.
Gloating over blessings includes performing a perfect life online to make others feel like nothing, which he says worsens the mental health epidemic.
Arrogance is thinking others are beneath you. Toward one person it is arrogance; toward a group it is racism.

Al-Isra 17:37 forbids strutting on the earth, since you cannot tear it or reach the mountains in height. Luqman's counsel in 31:18-19 adds: do not turn your cheek from people, walk moderately and lower your voice.

The hadith that whoever has an atom's weight of arrogance in his heart will not enter Jannah means that considering yourself better than anything or anyone, without Allah's word for it, is enough to fail.

The Prophet said that if his companions did not sin he would fear for them something worse: self-admiration (al-ujb), narrated by Al-Bazzar. He pairs it with the three destroyers, the last being a person's admiration of himself.

Abu Bakr told Aisha that a servant who delights in worldly adornment displeases his Lord until he parts with it, and she gave it in charity (Hilyat al-Awliya). A father steeped in the Quran could not bear to see his daughter vain.

Al-Alaq 96:6-8 names arrogance and oppression born of feeling self-sufficient as the first traits that make a person incompatible with Islam; the remedy is not seeing yourself or your opinion as more important than others.

subs.heading: Part of our nature, so admit it

points.text: The Quran names these instincts not to shame us but to show what must change. There is no point knowing the whole Quran without knowing you are vain and arrogant by nature.
An-Nahl 16:3-4: the human created from a drop becomes an open disputant who stands yelling at God about His rulings, pain and death.

Humanity still does not see how weak and fragile it is, racing toward planet-destroying weapons and treating one another as enemies, while Al-Mursalat 77:38-40 dares all of it to plot against Allah. If that does not teach us, nothing will.

sections.heading: Where does arrogance hide in religious people?
sections.intro: His most distinctive move is to locate arrogance inside pious habits that feel like faith. The forms he names are rarely the obvious ones.

points.text: Claiming that earthquake victims or a toddler with cancer were punished for their sins is arrogance, speaking without knowledge, and it drives people away from faith.
Questioning Allah's commands as if negotiating with a peer is vanity. His commands benefit us only out of His compassion, and that should humble us.
Al-Walid ibn al-Mughira looked, frowned and turned away in pride (74:21-23), resenting that prophecy went to Muhammad and not to a great man of the two cities (43:31).
Each of them wanting scrolls of his own (74:52) is an inflated ego that wants Allah to address it directly and thinks itself the exception; it fails the test of whether it could work for everyone.
Bad religiosity breeds a feeling of superiority over non-Muslims and the less observant, even over people more advanced in every way, and then licenses judging them.

Quraysh called themselves the Hums, the strict ones, and never left the sacred boundary at Hajj. By riding past the Mash'ar al-Haram to Arafah (2:198-199) the Prophet ended their claim to be more religious than everyone else.
False humility assumes superiority and then claims moral credit for stooping, so it combines two faults where open pride has only one.

Never judge yourself better than a sinner: you do not know the hand he was dealt, more given means more expected, and only Allah weighs effort against the start (74:37). His mother explained it with the staggered lanes of Olympic races.
Taqwa has no barometer, so no one can rank another (49:13). Worry about your own taqwa on the day you die, not the non-Muslim's.
Being right is overrated and being wrong is easier. People who admit error keep growing; those who must win stop, which is why he refuses to judge 300-message phone fights.
Listening is part of humility: the Prophet let Utbah ibn Rabi'ah finish every offer before asking to be heard. Refusing to listen while expecting non-Muslims to listen to us is inconsistent.
Knowing what you do not know matters more than knowing what you know; from his clinic, patients who parrot googled terms make the worst encounters.
Stop comparing yourself and trying to prove your value. Humility lets you learn and frees you from outdoing people who are living their own story.
Never say you could never be in someone else's position; that is punishable arrogance, since Allah could put any of us there without effort. Be thankful He spared you and use it to care for others.
Racism is collective arrogance, arrogance times a million; a foundling left by a dumpster and a ruler's heir cannot be ranked against each other.
Institutional ego is personal ego hiding inside an institution. Institutions are vehicles, not ends; one that needs defending or would sacrifice a person for its own survival should be dismantled.

sections.heading: What arrogance costs: victory, unity and the truth
sections.intro: He ties the inner state of humility to the outcomes Muslims care about, from the battlefield to masjid politics.

subs.heading: Victory is given to the humble

points.text: Al-Anfal 8:47 warns believers not to march out like those who left home boastfully and to be seen. Batar is arrogance born of confidence in wealth and might, so no cause should set out to impress or intimidate.
Allah gave victory at Badr while the believers were humble inside (3:123). This law needs nothing but you, and without the inner connection everything else is useless.

The ratio was eased from one-to-ten to one-to-two (8:65-66) because a weakness, attraction to the spoils (8:1), had been exposed. Uhud, the one battle fought at that ratio, was nearly lost, while Mu'tah was won at impossible odds once the weakness was fixed.

There is room in the masjid for all our bodies but not all our egos. Arrogance, envy of successful Muslims and seeing fellow Muslims as the other side of the tracks block unity; only Allah joins hearts (8:63), so he asks Him for it.
Shaytan invests people's egos in petty controversies until communities split. Lowering your wing to the believers (15:88) means taking a blow to your pride to keep the community together.
Walid shows that when pride and personal interest outrank the truth, a person refuses what he knows. Practise admitting you are wrong on small opinions so you can do it when much is at stake.
The gravest denial (takdhib) is seeing the truth and refusing it, as Abu Jahl admitted he did out of tribal rivalry.
Al-Alaq lists rejecting something only because it is new (96:9-10) and prejudice against the speaker alongside arrogance. Accept the truth regardless of whose mouth it comes from.

subs.heading: Shaytan's poison at the top of the hill

points.text: At your best moment Shaytan tries to add a drop of poison, making you arrogant, vain and ungrateful for what you were given; at your lowest he feeds the 'why me' questions.
He also strikes at critical moments: at the Bay'ah of Aqabah he screamed to expose the seventy-two Ansar, yet the pledge on which all later good depended succeeded.

sections.heading: Humility at the peak: how the Prophet and his companions carried power
sections.intro: His models show that humility is tested most at the moment of success and authority, and in how one repents.

points.text: After twenty-one years of effort, the Prophet entered Mecca at sixty with his face bowed to his camel's neck, still the epitome of humility.
When Sa'd ibn Ubadah declared it a day of slaughter, the Prophet took the banner from him, declared a day of mercy in which Quraysh would find its honour, and handed the banner to Sa'd's son.
An-Nasr 110:1-3 is the instruction for the top of the mountain: at victory, glorify your Lord and seek forgiveness. He entered lying flat over his mount, not chest out as a gloating conqueror.

subs.heading: No title exempts you from service

points.text: As caliph, Abu Bakr secretly cleaned, mended and cooked for a blind old woman each week, as Umar discovered. No degree or title puts you above basic service; there is still a spot for you down in the mud.
The Prophet asked a young child about his pet bird that had died, while someone thought it a waste of time; basic presence with people is part of service.

He balances two roles: you are Allah's steward (khalifa), who takes responsibility, and His servant (abd), who has no ego, agenda or need to own. Drop service and you become a tyrant; drop responsibility and you become passive and oppressed.
People empowered him at fifteen or sixteen, letting him learn, teach and hold positions he did not deserve while protecting him. Leaders without ego see youth for what they can become.

subs.heading: Repentance that does not plead a record

points.text: When Abu Dharr alluded to Bilal's race, the Prophet told him he still had jahiliyyah in him. Abu Dharr lay with his head on the ground asking Bilal to step on his neck, with no appeal to seniority or service.

Contrast Musa throwing the tablets and seizing Harun's beard (7:150), which Allah overlooked because of his record. Abu Dharr's record did not spare him because a breach of humility and equality comes before background, colour, wealth and deeds.

sections.heading: How to build humility without crushing your self-worth
sections.intro: His remedies are mental habits grounded in verses, and he insists that humility should strengthen a person rather than shrink him.

points.text: Assume others deserve credit for their effort, and assume the opposite about yourself, since Allah never told you that you do. Today the tables are turned.

When you succeed, ask whether it is your credit or the natural result of what Allah facilitated, and mean it when you say alhamdulillah. Cleansing vanity and arrogance should top your list because they appear in forms you do not expect.

Even good deeds are not yours to take full credit for: the close of Al-Insan teaches that your will exists only by Allah's will, so your spirit and choice are His creation. The deen centres on intention because it is all you have; renew it every time you fall.

subs.heading: Remember you could have been them

points.text: An-Nisa 4:94 forbids telling one who offers peace in battle that he is not a believer: you were like that before Allah favoured you. Guidance is His gift, nothing you did.
The Prophet kept repeating 'after he said it?' to Usama ibn Zayd, who had killed a man after he said the shahada, until Usama wished he had only become Muslim that day.

Most of us were born into Islam rather than reasoning our way to it, and those who are lost may never have met someone who cared. Guiding one person is better than all worldly possessions, so approach the distant gently, like the man who ran from the farthest part of the city.

Do not walk around thinking your faith is strong. Had the Prophet been harsh even Abu Bakr and Umar would have scattered; Allah knows your breaking point and has drawn His veil over you, so be ashamed before Him and ask for safety.
The more you know, the more you see your own ignorance. Only the knowledgeable truly revere Allah (35:28), and knowledge is that reverence, not the count of memorized narrations.
You cannot see a shortcoming without knowing the metric. Knowing it humbles you, and he is explicit that this humility should push you closer to Allah and generate improvement, not self-flagellation.

In a lecture that reads Musa and Pharaoh as the story of an untamed ego, the cosmic verses of An-Nazi'at 79:27-32, the vast balanced sky, the smoothed earth, its water, pasture and mountains, each humble the listener and leave no room for arrogance.
The balance comes in 79:33: all of it was made as provision for you. Tazkiyah is accepting both truths, so you stop fighting to prove you are more or fearing that you are less.

Humility is not a pose for special occasions. An ethic is either consistent or non-existent, and your true colours show with those who can do nothing for you; Surah al-Balad, after Taif, asked the Prophet to feed the hungry while hungry himself.
Lower the wing of humility to your parents out of mercy and pray for them as they raised you (17:24), above all when they are elderly and you hold the upper hand.

khutbah_seeds.text: Who gets the credit? Vanity as claiming what Allah facilitated (39:49-50, Qarun in 28:78), applied through his two assumptions: credit others, never yourself.
The arrogance of the pious: the Hums, false humility and superiority over the less observant, grounded in the atom-of-arrogance hadith, applied to how we speak about sinners.
On top of the mountain: the Prophet entering Mecca bowed and An-Nasr's command, applied to what we do after a graduation, promotion or win.
Badr was won on the inside: 8:47 and 3:123 on why community projects fail when they set out to impress, and how to audit intention.
You were once like them: 4:94, Usama and the veiled breaking point, applied to how we treat Muslims far from practice.
Racism is arrogance times a million: Abu Dharr's head on the ground before Bilal and 49:13, applied to marriage choices and masjid circles.

hadith.gist: After Ta'if, Jibril came with the angel of the mountains, who offered to crush the two mountains on Quraysh; the Prophet said he hoped Allah would bring from their descendants people who worship Allah alone.
The Prophet remarked that pollinating palms might not help; they stopped, the harvest failed, and he said: you know the affairs of your world better.
Aisha said that if the Messenger had concealed anything of the Quran, he would have concealed the verse about hiding in himself what Allah would reveal.

Three things, whoever has them finds the sweetness of faith: Allah and His Messenger being dearer than all else, loving a person only for Allah, and hating to return to disbelief as one hates being thrown into fire.
The Prophet would tell Bilal to call the prayer so they could find rest in it.
None of you truly believes until I am dearer to him than himself, his family, children, wealth and all people; Umar's exchange with the Prophet about loving him more than himself.
Whoever has food for his day and a safe place to sleep has been given the world.
Aisha: a month would pass without a fire lit in the Prophet's house, only dates and water, and he never ate bread with oil twice in one day.
The Prophet's mat marked his body; asked to accept something softer he said: what have I to do with the world? I am like a traveller resting in a tree's shade.
Companions pledged to the Prophet to take from the world only a traveller's provision, and later regretted falling short.
The Prophet died with his armour pawned to a neighbour for a loan.

On the Day of Judgment the Prophet prostrates beneath the Throne and Allah tells him to raise his head: ask and you will be granted, intercede and your intercession will be accepted. No one else has been told in sujud that it is enough.

The Prophet laid his head in Aisha's lap and asked Allah to forgive all her past and future, open and hidden sins; when she laughed he asked if his dua pleased her, and said this is the dua he makes for his ummah every day and night.
The two best men nearly perished: Abu Bakr and Umar raised their voices in the Prophet's presence, and the verse on lowering voices was revealed.
A man said he loved his brother; the Prophet told him to let him know.
Aisha said she was jealous of no wife as she was of Khadijah, whom she never met, because he remembered her and sent gifts to her friends.
Allah never gave me anyone better than Khadijah: she believed in me when people disbelieved and supported me with her wealth.
Amr ibn al-As asked who was most beloved to the Prophet: Aisha, then her father.
The Prophet took Muadh by the hand and said he loved him, then taught him a supplication.
The Prophet wept holding his dying grandson and said this is the mercy Allah places in the hearts of His servants.
At the conquest of Makkah he told Quraysh: go, you are free.
Dua for the last nights: O Allah, You are the Pardoner and love to pardon, so pardon me.
His description in the earlier scripture: he does not repay evil with evil but pardons and forgives.
Abdullah ibn Ubayy insulted the Prophet over the dust of his donkey; Sad ibn Ubadah explained that Ibn Ubayy was about to be crowned.

Do not laugh much, for much laughter kills the heart.
I never saw anyone smile more than the Messenger of Allah.

He told an old woman that old women do not enter Paradise, meaning she would enter it young.
