A Bedouin urinated in the masjid; the Prophet told the companions to leave him, then taught him gently and had water poured over it
Zayd ibn Sa'na demanded his loan early and insulted the Prophet, who told Umar he should have urged good repayment and gentle asking
The Prophet told a servant girl that if not for fear of retribution he would have struck her with his miswak
The Prophet never struck anyone with his hand, not a woman, a servant or anyone, except in battle
A man took the Prophet's sword while he slept and asked who would protect him; he said Allah, the sword fell, and he pardoned the man
Accused of unfair division, the Prophet said: may Allah have mercy on Musa, he was harmed more than this and was patient
At Ta'if the angel of the mountains offered to crush its people; the Prophet hoped Allah would bring from their descendants people who worship Him alone
Abdullah ibn ash-Shikhkhir found the Prophet praying with a sound in his chest like a boiling pot from weeping
The Prophet asked Ibn Mas'ud to recite to him; at the verse on the witness from every nation his eyes overflowed
Thabit ibn Qays stayed home fearing his deeds were void because of his loud voice; the Prophet sent word that he was among the people of Paradise.
Two of the Prophet's wives told him his breath smelled of maghafir after he drank honey at Zaynab's, and he vowed not to drink it again.
The Prophet would not eat raw garlic or onion before meeting people, because the angels are bothered by what bothers humans.
Thabit ibn Qays feared that his deeds were voided after the verse on raising voices, and the Prophet told him he was among the people of paradise.
A man swore Allah would not forgive another; Allah forgave that man and voided the deeds of the one who swore.
Wealth is the wealth of the heart and poverty is the poverty of the heart; the poor man of the masjid is better than the earth filled with the noble one.
My example in this world is like a rider who rests under a tree, then gets up and leaves it.
Umar found the Prophet on a mat that marked his side, with almost nothing stored, and asked him to pray for wealth like Persia and Rome; he replied those people had their good hastened in this life.
Aisha said only the shoulder of the sheep remained; he said all of it remains except its shoulder.
Mus'ab ibn Umayr was shrouded in a cloth that could not cover both his head and feet.
He would ask whether there was food and, when told no, would say he was fasting.
The handkerchiefs of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in Paradise are better than this garment.
Offered to be a king prophet or a servant prophet, he chose to be a servant who eats one day and is hungry the next.
The Prophet, Abu Bakr and Umar left home from hunger and were hosted by an Ansari man; he said they would be asked about this bliss.
The family of Muhammad never ate their fill three days in a row until he died; months passed with no fire lit in his home.
He died with his armour pawned to a Jewish man.
Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah
Whoever does you a favour, repay him
A woman mocked the Prophet for eating like a slave as he sat with poor people; he replied that no one is more of a servant than he.
Women and perfume were made beloved to me, and the delight of my eye was placed in prayer.
When prayer time came the Prophet would say: stand, Bilal, and give us rest through it.
Umm Salamah and Aisha: when a matter troubled the Prophet he rushed to prayer as his refuge.

Anas: the Prophet was neither very tall nor short, neither stark white nor dark, hair neither curly nor straight; sent at forty, ten years in Makkah, ten in Madinah, died at sixty with fewer than twenty white hairs.
Recite to me. Shall I recite to you when it was revealed to you? I love to hear it from others.
Allah commanded me to recite to you, Ubayy. Did He name me? Yes.
Your love of it will enter you into Jannah (the man reciting al-Ikhlas).
You have been given a flute of the flutes of the family of Dawud (Abu Musa).
Beautify the Quran with your voices; whoever does not recite melodiously is not of us.
Allah has His own people among mankind: the people of the Quran.
His character was the Quran.
O Allah, I am Your servant, son of Your servant... make the Quran the spring of my heart.
O Allah, all praise is Yours; none can withhold what You extend... make faith beloved to us.
I bear witness that all servants are brothers.
I ask for Jannah and refuge from the Fire; around these we hum.
O Allah, around us and not upon us.
Make your food pure and your supplication will be answered.
O Allah, to You I complain of my weakness... if You are not angry with me I do not mind.
O Allah, to You belongs praise; You are the light of the heavens and the earth.
If the Hour arrives while one of you holds a sapling, let him plant it if he can.
Abu Bakr told departing armies, passing on what the Prophet taught: in Allah's name, do not burn a tree, flood land, kill an animal or destroy anything.
Who will buy this slave from me? ... but in Allah's sight you are valuable (Zahir).
The Prophet turned al-Fadl's face away from the woman questioning him at Hajj.
O Mu'adh, by Allah I love you.
Some eloquence is like magic.
Jabir sells his camel to the Prophet, who pays and returns it.
O Allah, I am pleased with him, so be pleased with him (at the grave of Dhul-Bijadayn).
What an excellent man Abdullah is, if only he prayed at night.
Ibn Mas'ud gave reminders on certain days only, as the Prophet did, to avoid boring people.
Umm Haram: people of my ummah sailing the sea in Allah's cause; you are among the first.
This prayer is not fit for people's speech; it is tasbih, takbir and Quran recitation (Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam).
The Prophet's address to the Ansar after Hunayn and his dua for them and their descendants.

A Bedouin grabbed the Prophet by his garment and twisted it until his face changed colour; the Prophet kept others back, gave him more until he was satisfied, and compared himself to a man calming a runaway camel
The Bedouin who urinated in the masjid was treated gently by the Prophet
Elderly servant women and young children could take the Prophet by the hand and he would go with them to help
A Bedouin urinated in the masjid; the Prophet stopped the companions, had water poured on it and gently taught him.
A man later recalled that the Prophet did not scold, shame or yell at him but simply taught him.

A man spoke rudely to the Prophet while he distributed wealth; the Prophet gave him more until satisfied, then compared himself to a man who calls back his runaway camel gently while others only drive it away.
The Prophet would repeat himself three times, but each repetition pushed people to think further rather than being identical
The Prophet could not hold back his tears when his son Ibrahim died
The Prophet sharply rebuked companions who fought using racist insults, telling them to leave it because it is rotten
On the minbar the Prophet's voice rose and he appeared angry, because he was addressing critical matters and wanted people ready to change
The companions said that listening to the Prophet they would laugh and they would cry
Umar: the Prophet would pray Isha and then stay up with Abu Bakr over some matter of the Muslims, and Umar was with them.
Aisha: he would go to one of his wives' houses where people gathered and he would talk with them, then retire to his bed in the first part of the night.
The prayer of Dawud, which he calls sahih: sleep half the night, pray a third and sleep a sixth; and Aisha's report that the Prophet never stood a whole night in prayer.
After Fajr the Prophet would go to the markets of the Muslims, commanding, forbidding, advising and settling their needs.
Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa: he made much dhikr and little idle talk, lengthened the prayer and shortened the khutbah, and did not disdain walking with a widow or a poor person to settle their need.
Aisha: he would visit the sick, milk his goat, mend his sandal, serve his family and patch his garment.
Aisha: none of you is capable of what the Messenger of Allah was capable of; hence partial imitation.
Abu Bakr and Umar told their daughters not to ask the Prophet for more provision but to ask them
Umar asked permission three times and found the Prophet on a coarse mat with almost no food stored, and wept
Are you not content that they have this world and we have the Hereafter?
The wolf only takes the sheep that is alone; the herd together cannot be eaten.
The Prophet wept reciting a verse about his nation; Jibril was sent to ask why and returned with the promise that Allah would please him concerning his ummah
When his people wounded him, the Prophet prayed that Allah forgive them because they did not know.
A narration that on Safa, as he made takbir and dua with the companions gathered at his feet saying amin, tears ran down his face.
There is no faith for one who has no trustworthiness, and no religion for one who does not keep his word
The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand people are safe, and the believer is the one whom people trust with their blood and wealth
The Bedouin who urinated in the masjid; the Prophet stopped the companions and gently taught him
The Prophet smiled the smile of an angry man
Khadijah reassured the Prophet after the first revelation by listing how he helped the poor, the weak and those in distress.
Umar found the Prophet on a mat in his upper room with an almost empty store and asked how long they would live poor while Persia and Rome lived in luxury; the Prophet rebuked him.
A man given great wealth by the Prophet went back telling people to accept Islam, because Muhammad gives like one who has no fear of poverty; he had hated him and came to love him.
The Prophet was more generous with good than the wind sent with rain.
The Prophet never struck anyone with his hand, not a woman, child or servant, except in battle.
The best of you are the best to their families (wives), and I am the best of you to mine.
At home the Prophet cleaned, mended his clothes and repaired shoes.
In his final days, carried to the minbar, the Prophet bequeathed that women be treated well.
Farewell sermon: wives are your helpers, you own nothing of them, you took them by Allah's covenant.
When Abu Bakr came to rebuke Aisha for raising her voice, the Prophet stood between them, then joked that he had defended her.
Young man, say Allah's name, eat with your right hand and eat from what is in front of you.
The Ash'aris pool their food when short and share it equally; they are of me and I am of them.
He never criticised food: if he liked it he ate it, otherwise he left it.
Offered roasted lizard he did not eat it, saying it was not forbidden but not found among his people.
He breathed three times while drinking.
The worst vessel a son of Adam fills is his stomach; a third for food, a third for drink, a third for breath.
I do not eat while reclining.
Anas saw him seeking out the gourd in the dish and loved it from that day.
He ate watermelon with fresh dates.
Allah is pleased with a servant who eats a meal or drinks and praises Him for it.
May the fasting break their fast with you, the righteous eat your food and the angels send blessings on you.
Wear white, for it is the best of your clothing.
A woman wove him a garment and a companion asked for it to be his shroud.
When the Prophet prayed, a sound like the boiling of a pot was heard from his chest from weeping.
When the Prophet said to tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer, Aisha said Abu Bakr is a tender man who would weep and not be heard.
Give us rest through it, O Bilal (said of calling the prayer).
The Prophet refused to have Ibn Ubayy killed so people would not say Muhammad kills his companions
Umar said revelation agreed with him on three matters, including not praying over the hypocrites
Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib: the Prophet was of medium height, broad-shouldered, with hair to his earlobes; in a red garment he was the most beautiful thing al-Bara' ever saw.
Ali: the Prophet had large sturdy hands and joints, a line of hair down his chest, walked as if descending a slope; Ali never saw his like before or after.

When Abdullah ibn Ubayy spoke insultingly on the return from a campaign, Umar asked to strike his neck; the Prophet said people must not say Muhammad kills his companions, and that they would treat him well while he remained with them.
The Prophet said he was sent to perfect noble character.
Aisha, asked about the Prophet's character, answered that his character was the Quran.
The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful; show mercy to those on earth and the One above will show you mercy. Traditionally the first hadith taught.
Description of the Prophet as constantly concerned and never at rest.
At Hudaybiyyah: war has exhausted Quraysh; by Allah I will keep striving for this until Allah makes it prevail or my neck is severed.
Abu Sufyan, urged to say la ilaha illa Allah, wept and said how forbearing, generous and kind to kin the Prophet was.
An envoy who watched the companions catch the Prophet's ablution water reported that he had seen kings but none revered like Muhammad.
When someone remarked that the Prophet sat and ate like a slave, he replied that he was a servant and ate as a servant eats.
The Prophet visited his dying Jewish boy servant.
O Abu Umayr, what happened to the little bird?
Anas served him for years and he never said why did you do this or why didn't you do that.
Whoever has three daughters or sisters, or two, and fears Allah regarding them and treats them well enters Jannah.
Whoever has a daughter and does not bury her, demean her or prefer his sons over her, Allah enters him into Jannah because of her.
A young woman married off by her father to his nephew was given the choice to end the marriage.
We have granted protection to whomever you granted protection, O Umm Hani.
Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from the masajid of Allah.
The Prophet raced Aisha twice and said this one is for that one.
Your mother became jealous; he gathered the food from the broken plate and replaced the dish.
Aisha found him prostrating at night praising Allah.
I know when you are pleased with me and when you are angry: you swear by the Lord of Muhammad or the Lord of Ibrahim.
Abu Bakr: let me into your peace as you let me into your war.
He was in the service of his family and would mend his shoe and sew his clothes.
He drank from the place on the cup where Aisha drank during her period.
My grandson rode on me and I did not want to rush him.
Get up, Abu Turab.
May Allah curse whoever branded this animal's face.
Do you want to kill it twice? Sharpen your blade before laying it down.
She is not stubborn; she was held back by the One who held back the elephant.
At Uhud, wounded, the Prophet prayed: O Allah forgive my people, for they do not know
The Prophet addressed the dead of Quraysh at Badr, asking if they found his warning true
At the conquest he took the banner from Sa'd ibn Ubadah: today is a day of mercy
O Allah, strengthen Islam with one of the two Umars
When Aisha asked why he stood so long in night prayer though forgiven, he said: shall I not be a grateful servant?
Abdullah ibn Salam came to test the Prophet, saw his face and said it was not the face of a liar.
A companion compared the Prophet's face with the full moon and found his face more beautiful.
The Prophet never struck anyone with his hand, not a woman nor a servant, except when fighting in the path of Allah.
I have several names: I am Muhammad, Ahmad, the obliterator by whom Allah erases disbelief, the gatherer at whose feet people are gathered, and the final one after whom there is no prophet.
Al-Nu'man ibn Bashir: do you not eat and drink as you please? I saw your Prophet unable to find enough poor-quality dates to fill his stomach.
The Prophet had braids on one occasion
He let his hair fall like the People of the Book, liking to agree with them where no command came, then later parted it
Salman brought charity which the Prophet did not eat, then a gift which he ate, then saw the seal of prophecy and believed
The Prophet planted the palms for Salman's freedom; Umar's palm alone failed until the Prophet replanted it
The seal of prophecy was a small cluster of hairs
Al-Hubab asked whether the camp site was revelation or strategy, and the Prophet adopted his plan.
It is not fitting for a prophet who has put on his armour to remove it before fighting.
Gentleness is not in anything except that it beautifies it, and it is not removed from anything except that it disfigures it.
The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful; show mercy to those on earth and the One above will show you mercy.
The angel of the mountains offered to crush the people of Ta'if; he hoped Allah would bring from them those who worship Him.
O Allah, forgive my people, for they do not know.
Go back to your families, teach them, pray as you saw me pray, and let the eldest lead.
Welcome, those the Messenger of Allah instructed us to care for (to young students).
Were it not hard on my ummah I would have commanded siwak at every prayer.
I begin prayer intending to lengthen it, hear a child crying and shorten it for his mother's sake.
What can I do if Allah has removed mercy from your heart.
The palm trunk wept when he moved to the minbar until he embraced it.
The Book of Allah is a rope extended from heaven to earth; hold to it and you will never go astray.
Al-Irbad ibn Sariyah: a moving admonition like a farewell; I have left you on a clear path whose night is like its day.
Whoever is struck by a calamity should remember his calamity in losing the Prophet, for it is the greatest.
He prayed for Aisha's forgiveness for all her sins and told her he makes that dua for his ummah in every prayer.
Every prophet had one answered dua; I have saved mine as intercession for my ummah on the Day of Resurrection.
Were it not hard on my ummah I would have commanded them to use siwak at every prayer.
He stopped leading the night prayer in Ramadan for fear it would become obligatory.
He recited the words of Ibrahim and Isa, raised his hands, wept saying my ummah, and Jibril was sent to say Allah will satisfy him regarding his ummah.
At the graves he wished to see his brothers, those who believe in him without having seen him, recognised by the light of wudu like white-blazed horses.
I go ahead of you to the Basin; your appointment with me is at the Basin.
Asked whether anyone would be better than the companions, he spoke of people after them who believe in him without seeing him.
The great intercession: people go to Adam, Ibrahim, Musa and others, then to him; he prostrates and says my ummah, my ummah.
No one sends salam on me but Allah returns my soul to me so I reply.
Perhaps Allah looked at the people of Badr and said: do as you will, I have forgiven you.
I asked permission to seek forgiveness for my mother and was not granted it; visit graves, for they remind you of death.
No one did me a favour except that I repaid it, except Abu Bakr; his reward is with Allah.
Close every door into the masjid except the door of Abu Bakr.
If I were to take a khalil I would take Abu Bakr.
Blood for blood, destruction for destruction: I am of you and you are of me (to the Ansar).
Whoever meets Abu al-Bakhtari, do not kill him.
The Prophet asked Ibn Mas'ud to recite to him and stopped him in tears at the verse about bringing a witness from every nation.
Aisha: the Messenger of Allah was neither obscene nor sought obscenity, nor loud in the markets, nor did he repay evil with evil, but he pardoned and overlooked.

Aisha: I never saw him avenge a wrong done to him unless one of Allah's limits was violated, then he was the angriest of them; and he was never given a choice between two things but he chose the easier, so long as it was not sinful.
Whoever turns away from my sunnah (refuses my way of life) is not of me.
Sawdah gave her turn with the Prophet to Aisha.
Umar urged the Prophet to screen his wives because all kinds of men entered his house.
A man asked the Prophet for money; he had him sell his household items, feed his family with half and buy an axe head with the rest, then cut and sell wood for a week
The Prophet was given concise comprehensive words
The minbar was made for the Prophet because the crowds grew so large that people at the back could no longer see his face
The Prophet would smile even while delivering Jumuah, despite his serious persona on the minbar
The Prophet gave most of his talks during his life sitting down, while Jumuah is given standing
When the Prophet turned to look at something he turned his whole torso rather than just his neck
Aisha said she was never jealous of any woman as she was of Khadijah, who died before her marriage, because the Prophet kept mentioning her and sent portions of meat to her friends.
The Prophet recognized someone approaching as sounding like Khadijah and was moved, years after her death.
When Aisha said Allah had given him better, he said Khadijah believed in him when people disbelieved and supported him when people rejected him.
The distance between two gateposts of Jannah is like that between Makkah and a distant city, yet it will be crowded.
The Prophet's instruction: saddidu wa qaribu, aim rightly and stay near the balanced middle.
Anas: the Prophet visited the sick, attended funerals, rode donkeys and accepted a slave's invitation; on the day of Banu Qurayzah he rode a donkey with palm-fibre reins
Anas: the Prophet would be invited to barley bread and stale fat and would accept
The Prophet died with his armour pawned to a Jewish man
Ali: when battle grew fierce we would shield ourselves with the Prophet, who was closest of us to the enemy.
At Hunayn he threw sand at the enemy and declared: I am the Prophet, no lie, I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib.
He walked among the mocking leaders of Quraysh at the Kaaba and warned them, and they feared him.
Ubayy ibn Khalaf said he fed his horse to kill the Prophet, who replied he would kill Ubayy instead.
Anas: the Prophet was the best, most generous and bravest of people; he rode out ahead of everyone on a bareback horse when Madinah was alarmed at night.
He told Abu Talib he could no more abandon his mission than they could light a flame from the sun; the sun-in-my-right-hand wording is weak.
Do not wish to meet the enemy; ask Allah for wellbeing, but if you meet them, be steadfast.
His first public call: say la ilaha illallah and you will succeed.
Whoever saw him unexpectedly was in awe of him, and whoever mixed with him loved him.
When the fighting grew fierce, the companions sheltered behind the Messenger, who was closest to the enemy.
Abdullah ibn Salam saw his face and knew it was not the face of a liar.
Among the people most loving of me are those after me who would give their family and wealth to see me.
Anas was overjoyed to hear that a person will be with those he loves, and said he loved the Prophet, Abu Bakr and Umar.
The Prophet would offer his hand first and not withdraw it until the other person did, and he turned his whole body toward whoever he spoke to.

A man complained he arrives late to Fajr because an imam prolongs it; the Prophet, angrier than ever seen, said some of you drive people away, so whoever leads should lighten it, for behind him are the elderly, the weak and those in need.
hadith.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, from Abu Mas'ud Uqbah ibn Amr

hadith.gist: When something distressed him he would pray.
Line up so I may praise my Lord (after Uhud).
Go back and pray, for you have not prayed; bow until you are at rest.
If a river ran by your door and you bathed in it five times a day, would any dirt remain?
Do you want to cause fitnah, O Mu'adh?
Shall I not be a grateful servant?
The time of sleep has passed, O Khadijah.
Ibn Abbas observed him pray thirteen rakat at night.
Help me against yourself with much prostration (Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b).
Shall I not tell you of the best of your deeds... the remembrance of Allah.
The mufarridun have gone ahead: those who remember Allah much.
Let your tongue stay moist with the remembrance of Allah.
My heart is sometimes clouded and I seek Allah's forgiveness a hundred times a day.
La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah is a treasure of Jannah.
How much of my prayer shall I make for you? ... If you add more, it is better.
On the Day of Judgment people go from prophet to prophet seeking intercession; each declines citing a lapse, and Isa declines too
Hadith qudsi: Allah has forbidden oppression for Himself and made it forbidden among His servants, so do not wrong one another.
Beware of oppression, for it will be darkness on the Day of Judgment.
Beware the dua of the oppressed, even a disbeliever, for nothing stands between it and Allah.
Riding to visit a sick person, the Prophet passed Abdullah ibn Ubayy, who complained of the smell of his animal; the Prophet ignored him and went on.

When Ibn Ubayy died his son asked for the Prophet's shirt to shroud him; the Prophet gave it and prayed over him though Umar pulled him back and reminded him of Ibn Ubayy's deeds, and then 9:84 was revealed.
An angel came with Jibril offering the Prophet the choice of being a king-prophet or a servant-prophet, and he chose servant

A man kept insulting the Prophet until the companions wanted to strike him; the Prophet held them back and said they should have told the man to ask more politely and reminded him to respond better; the man then testified that he was the messenger of Allah, saying his scripture foretold that mistreatment only increases his patience (the Zayd ibn Sa'nah narration).
The Prophet died with his war shield pawned to raise money for someone else's loan, leaving no inheritance at all.
His one request for himself: when you make dua for me, ask Allah to grant me al-wasilah, a rank given to only one person, which he hoped would be him.
When you ask Allah, ask Him for the highest point of Jannah, not just to be let in at the door.
Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah.
Aisha asked why he stood in prayer until his feet swelled when Allah had forgiven him; he replied: should I not love to be a grateful servant?
Shortly before his death the Prophet said no one had done him a favour he had not repaid except Abu Bakr, whose favour he could not repay and so left to Allah.
He ordered every private door opening into the masjid closed except Abu Bakr's.
Companions describe the Prophet as always smiling, including whenever he entered his home
Signs of the hypocrite: when he speaks he lies, when entrusted he betrays.
Jabir looked at the full moon and at the Prophet on a moonlit night and found him more beautiful.
Aisha told the Prophet that a poet's famous line on a radiant face fitted him better.
Hind ibn Abi Halah's long description of the Prophet given to al-Hasan ibn Ali.
The Prophet wrestled Rukanah and threw him repeatedly.
Umm Sulaym collected the Prophet's sweat as he slept, for perfume and blessing for her children.
I never touched silk softer than the Prophet's hand nor smelled anything better than his scent.
Ali's description: most generous of heart; whoever saw him suddenly revered him, whoever knew him loved him; I never saw anyone like him before or after.
Do not curse him, for he loves Allah and His Messenger; do not help Shaytan against your brother.
Thumamah ibn Uthal tied in the masjid and released, then accepting Islam.
A youth's pledge withheld until he promised to stop harassing women.
Adi ibn Hatim told a woman will travel alone in safety, wealth will find no taker, and the treasures of Kisra will be taken.
Would you like it for your mother? ... then he prayed for the youth's forgiveness and chastity.
The man who broke his Ramadan fast is given dates and told to feed his family.
That Allah guides one person through you is better for you than red camels.
Do not curse the dead, for it harms the living.
On the night journey, at each heaven the prophets learned that Muhammad had been sent.
At the Farewell Hajj the Prophet asked what people would say when asked about him; they said he had conveyed and advised, and he asked Allah to bear witness.
Aisha saw the Prophet at death with a cup of water, dipping his hand and wiping his face, saying: O Allah, help me through the agonies of death.
The Prophet said his fever was doubled, as prophets are tested more than others.
Anas: the day the Prophet entered Madinah everything in it lit up, and the day he died everything darkened; we had not dusted off our hands from his burial before we no longer recognised our hearts.
Fatimah cried out at her father's distress; he said there would be no distress for your father after today, and the meeting is on the Day of Resurrection.
Companions describe the Prophet as always smiling, especially on entering his home.
A bedouin with ten children saw the Prophet kiss his grandson and said he had never kissed any; the Prophet asked what he could do if Allah had removed mercy from his heart
At his son Ibrahim's death the Prophet wept, saying the eye sheds tears and the heart grieves but we say only what pleases our Lord
Hanzalah feared hypocrisy because his state with the Prophet faded at home; the Prophet said if it lasted the angels would shake his hand, but there is a time for this and a time for that
The Prophet stood in night prayer until his feet swelled; when Aishah asked why, since Allah had forgiven him, he replied: should I not be a grateful servant?
A man took the sleeping Prophet's sword and asked who would protect him; the sword fell and the Prophet spared him
At Uhud the Prophet prayed: O Allah, forgive my people, for they do not know
A rabbi tested the Prophet by demanding an unpaid loan early and insulting him, then accepted Islam on seeing forbearance increase with provocation
The Torah describes the final Prophet as one whose patience grows the more he is provoked
At the conquest of Makkah the Prophet pointed his stick at the idols around the Kaaba and they fell.
The companions pledged to hear and obey, and the Prophet would add: as far as you are able
What I command you, do as much of it as you can
The Prophet died with his shield pawned for a loan
Aishah was asked whether the Prophet prayed sitting; yes, after the people had worn him down, but he never stopped praying
At the death of his son Ibrahim, answering Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: the eye weeps and the heart grieves, but we say only what pleases our Lord, and we are saddened by your parting, Ibrahim
The Prophet died with his armour pawned to a Jewish man; he built no wealth for himself.

When the Prophet withdrew from his wives to an upper room, Umar was admitted, made him smile, saw the mat's marks on his side and wept over Khosrau and Caesar's luxury; the Prophet asked if he was not content that they have this world and we the Hereafter.

The Prophet recited the words of Ibrahim and Isa about their peoples, raised his hands and wept saying 'my ummah, my ummah'; Allah sent Jibril to tell him He would please him regarding his ummah and not grieve him.
hadith.source: Sahih Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As

hadith.gist: The Prophet was given sheep filling the space between two mountains and gave them all away.
He gives like one who has no fear of poverty.
The Prophet was more generous than the wind sent with rain.
Bedouins pressed him to a thorn tree; he said if he had livestock like these trees he would divide it and they would not find him stingy, a liar or a coward.
A woman gifted him a garment; a man asked for it and he gave it; the man wanted it as his shroud.
He would not want gold like Uhud to stay with him more than three days except something kept for a debt.
A hungry man was hosted by an Ansari couple who pretended to eat in the dark; Allah was pleased with what they did.
The Prophet gathered his clan and told each, down to Fatimah, to ask him for any of his wealth but save themselves from the Fire, since he could avail them nothing before Allah
Proofs of prophethood such as water gushing from the well at his touch and restored eyesight
Jabir ibn Samurah saw the Prophet on a bright moonlit night in a red-striped garment and found him more beautiful than the moon.
A man asked al-Bara' ibn 'Azib if the Prophet's face was like a sword; he said no, like the moon.
Khadijah reassures the Prophet after the first revelation: Allah will never disgrace you, for you carry the weak, give the destitute and honour guests
A visiting youth tugged a Madinan girl's trailing garment at night; next morning the Prophet withheld his hand from him at the pledge until he promised never to do it again.
At the Farewell Hajj the Prophet turned al-Fadl's face away from a young woman asking a question, saying he did not feel safe from Satan for a young man and young woman.
Aisha combed the Prophet's hair while she was menstruating
He loved to begin with the right in purification, combing and putting on sandals
He forbade combing except every other day
He forbade excessive indulgence in comfort
Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say good or remain silent.
A person's faith is not upright until his heart is upright, and his heart is not upright until his tongue is.
His strongest rebuke was to say: what is wrong with him, may his forehead be in the dust.
Aisha: if someone wanted to count his words, he could have counted them.
He would repeat a word three times so it would be understood.
When he gave a sermon his eyes reddened and his voice rose as if warning of an army.
He answered a tribe in their dialect that fasting while travelling is not part of righteousness.
At Ibrahim's death: the eye weeps, the heart grieves, and we say only what pleases our Lord.
When his toe was injured: you are but a toe that bled, and it was in the path of Allah.
Allah revealed to me that you must be humble so that no one boasts over another or transgresses against another.
He served his family, mended his shoes, milked his sheep and swept his house.
Do not exaggerate in praising me as the Christians did with the son of Maryam; say the servant of Allah and His messenger.
Julaybib was found martyred; the Prophet said he is of me and I am of him.
Take it easy, I am only the son of a woman of Quraysh who ate dried meat.
Every prophet herded sheep; he herded for the people of Makkah for a few coins.
If I were invited to a meal of trotters I would accept, and if given one as a gift I would accept it.
When fighting intensified, the closest of us to the enemy was the Prophet.
A Bedouin seized the Prophet's cloak demanding wealth; the Prophet gave until he was pleased and compared him to a runaway camel.
The Prophet let a Bedouin finish urinating in the masjid, had water poured on it and taught him gently.
Whoever eats garlic or onion should not come near the mosque; the Prophet avoided them because he conversed with those others do not.
Many men reached perfection but among women only a few, Khadijah among them; the best of the women of her time was Khadijah.
He stopped to sit with Khadijah's elderly friends and said they used to visit in Khadijah's days.
A woman offered herself to the Prophet; he married her to a man who had not even an iron ring, with the Quran he knew as her dowry.
A Bedouin pulled the Prophet's cloak hard enough to mark his neck and demanded from Allah's wealth; the Prophet smiled and ordered he be given
The Prophet never took revenge for himself, only when Allah's limits were violated
The Prophet warned the mocking chiefs of Quraysh that he had come with slaughter, and they fell silent
Tufayl ibn Amr of Daws put cotton in his ears, then chose to listen to the Prophet and accepted Islam.
Dimad came to treat the Prophet, heard his sermon opening, asked him to repeat it and accepted Islam.
Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt twisted a garment around the Prophet's neck while he prayed.
The entrails of a camel were placed on the Prophet's back in prostration until Fatimah removed them.
On the way to Badr he refused to ride more than his share, saying his partners were not stronger than him nor was he less in need of reward.
He insisted on paying Abu Bakr for his camel at the Hijrah.
He refused to kill Ibn Ubayy so people would not say Muhammad kills his companions.
I was made to fear for Allah when no one else feared, and harmed when no one else was harmed; thirty days passed with nothing for me and Bilal to eat except what Bilal hid under his arm.
Khadijah reassured him that Allah would never disgrace him because he kept family ties, carried the weak and helped those struck by hardship.
When the Prophet sought a loan to keep giving, Umar objected; an Ansari said 'give and fear no poverty from the Lord of the Throne' and the Prophet smiled.
The Prophet died with his shield pawned; in his telling, he had pawned it to pay off someone else's debt.
The Prophet told his companions their appointment with him is at the Basin
When wealth arrived from Bahrain the Prophet said it is not poverty he fears for them but that the world will be spread before them as for those before
The Prophet spread his cloak for the woman who had nursed him as a child
No one has done us a favour but that we repaid him, except Abu Bakr, whose favour Allah will repay
In his final days the Prophet offered anyone whose wealth he had taken or whom he had harmed to take their due from him.
During a dispute between Muhajirun and Ansar, the Prophet condemned the tribal rallying calls as foul.
Abdullah, son of Ibn Ubayy, asked to execute his father himself if ordered; the Prophet refused and told him to treat his father well, so people would not say Muhammad kills his companions.
Ibn Mas'ud joined the Prophet's night prayer, which was so long that he was tempted to sit down and leave him.
Ibn Mas'ud recited An-Nisa to the Prophet, who said he loved to hear it from another; at the verse of the witness he said 'enough' with tears flowing.
In one rakah the Prophet recited Al-Baqarah, An-Nisa and Aal-Imran slowly, asking for Paradise and seeking refuge from the Fire when they were mentioned.
At the Trench the Prophet struck the boulder three times and with each spark promised the conquest of Persia, Yemen and Rome.
When a man threw sand in his face, the Prophet told his weeping daughter not to cry because Allah would grant her father success.
The Prophet never filled his belly; a third is the maximum for food.
The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand people are safe, and the mu'min is the one around whom people feel safe.
No harm: the principle that a Muslim causes no harm to others.

After the first revelation the Prophet ran down the mountain to Khadijah fearing Allah's wrath; she answered that it could never be, because he keeps family ties, carries those who cannot carry themselves, helps the distressed, gives to the poor and stands beside anyone in difficulty.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Participation

spans.note: Participation is the community's second obligation in the covenant: belonging to the ummah is not optional, so everyone must put in time, wealth and presence and give more than they take.
The same few volunteers are recycled across every committee and institution while everyone else stays away; that is not how it should work.
Participation driven by the community itself, outside an institution's umbrella, lasts longer and goes farther.

lectures.title: From Populations to Communities: Political Centralization

spans.note: The series thesis: a population becomes a community by centralizing something, and a functional, self-sustaining local community is the biggest service to the ummah and the only base from which anything larger can be changed.
The freedom here gives Muslims a better chance than anywhere to build a functioning community; only their own lack of commitment stands in the way.
Caring for the ummah starts with building the local community properly: you cannot offer what you do not have.

lectures.title: The Five Categories of Community Investment

spans.note: The community lacks centralization, goals and vision; he proposes five investment categories so effort is channelled in one direction.
The five categories to invest in: education, mentorship, financial centralization, outreach and advocacy, with each person finding their piece.

lectures.title: My Maxims, Part 3

spans.note: The ummah's voice is ignored and Muslims have lowered their ambitions to comfort and a functional masjid.
Work with people you disagree with, bear their harm, and never withdraw from the community even after being burnt.

lectures.title: My Maxims, Part 6

spans.note: Communities must stand behind those who act even without full agreement; withdrawing because your request was not met is shameful.
Rare global Muslim unity over Gaza must be turned into organized work, advocacy and education before it fades.

lectures.title: Listening to the Divine: Aal-Imran 102-112

spans.note: I'tisam is collective: hold the rope and each other as one unit, remember the favour of enemies made brothers, and accept that protecting faith together is harder than alone but the only option the Quran gives.
Individual value exists within a group that sails together; the city's Muslims must organize to teach every child, strengthen the weak, treat the sick and find the lost, and turn numbers into output.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Our End of the Bargain

spans.note: Communities stagnate because no understanding exists between those who run masajid and those who attend; a covenant where everyone shoulders some weight is the only way forward, and the ummah's future is the sum of collective effort.
Every Jumuah attendee is party to the covenant, and the ummah's future is the sum of everyone's collective effort, one person at a time.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Summary

spans.note: Communities change only when members and their masajid agree on a clear covenant and stop working as scattered silos; a small, committed group is enough to start.
The written pledge spells out what the masjid and each member owe one another, with ways to hold each other accountable.

lectures.title: From Populations to Communities: Social Centralization

spans.note: A population becomes a community by centralizing something; socially that starts with geographic proximity, which London lacks, then a shared identity and equality among Muslims.
Norms protected by social reward and shame and marriage across ethnic lines complete social centralization; four of its five pieces can be built if people champion them.

lectures.title: From Populations to Communities: Financial Centralization

spans.note: A population becomes a community only by centralizing something; London's Muslims have grown in numbers but not in organization, unity or footing, and must centralize their interests to secure their future and serve the wider ummah.
Financial centralization is the most achievable step: the city has the money and numbers but no shared system, willpower or leadership to direct them.

cites.point: Hold on to the rope of Allah all together: collective i'tisam like drowning people sharing one lifeline.
Remember His favour: you were enemies and He joined your hearts so you became brothers, and saved you from the brink of the fire.
Hold fast to the rope of Allah and do not divide
The companions of the cave and the raqim, which he explains as a written document of vision and values.
The cave and the inscription as symbols of retreat and a charter
You are responsible for yourselves; Abu Bakr warned against reading it as permission to withdraw from the community
misused to justify detaching from the ummah
Do not be like those who split and disputed after clear proofs came
Do not be like those before you who divided and differed; division ruined them.
Allah has bought the believers' lives and wealth in exchange for Paradise.
Allah has bought from the believers their lives and wealth in exchange for Jannah: the covenant is a two-way contract you agreed to.
Hypocrites mocked believers who could give only a little, such as a date.
The hypocrites mocked poor companions who brought what little they had, like a single date, and Allah accepted it.
At Hunayn their numbers impressed them, the wide earth felt narrow and they turned back.
Hunayn, when the Muslims' great numbers pleased them but availed them nothing: the Quran's example of being fooled by numbers.
The youth of the cave: a few sincere people doing good briefly changed their people's fate
The people of the cave as the rock-solid idea that outlasted a king
Cooperate in righteousness and piety, not in sin and aggression.
Cooperate in righteousness and taqwa, not in sin and transgression: the basis for collective community work.
Let there be among you an ummah calling to good, commanding ma'ruf and forbidding munkar; read as all of you.
You were the best nation brought out for mankind: the goodness of this ummah is meant to reach others; you command good, forbid wrong and believe in Allah.
Harun feared Musa would say he had divided Bani Israel, so he held back
Those who split their religion: the Prophet has nothing to do with them and their affair is with Allah
Those who pledge to you pledge to Allah, whose hand is above theirs: the concept of the bay'ah is Quranic even though its points are not.
Ibrahim reasoning from the star, moon and sun: the one personal story in Al-An'am.
If believers ask for help you must give it; disbelievers ally with one another, and failing to do so brings fitnah and great corruption
Beware a trial that will not strike only the wrongdoers among you.
Fitnah is worse than killing, because it can destroy many.
People are led to Paradise in groups; rarely does anyone arrive alone.
The Prophet corrected for turning, even briefly, from the person in front of him
The overused ayah on change, read as a warning: Allah will not change a good state to a bad one unless the people change first.
Obey Allah and His Messenger and do not dispute, or you will fail and your strength will depart.
The first House at Bakka, with blessing, guidance, the station of Ibrahim, safety, and the duty of Hajj for those able.
Allah showed Ibrahim the site of the House, implying it existed before him.
those who maintain (make flourish) the masjids of Allah

The verse he opened with: earlier nations were destroyed because no one was left forbidding corruption and carrying the group, except the few Allah saved; a community dies when everyone becomes a selfish individual.
People given different ranks so they may make use of one another.
Asking forgiveness seventy times will not help those who lie, yet the Prophet did not know who was lying and accepted all excuses
Do not raise your voices above the Prophet's, contrasted with Khawlah's praised argument
Companions who argued about going out before Badr were blamed
Prepare strength against those hostile to you; wealth is part of that strength.
The Prophet's wives offered the choice to stay with his austere life or take a generous divorce, showing he kept nothing for himself.
The eight recipients of zakat, including those who collect it and those whose hearts are to be reconciled.
The Prophet was sent to all of humanity, so his ummah is everyone, not only those who believed.
The orchard owners who lost their garden and repented, unlike Saba
Allah strengthened the Prophet with the believers and united their hearts, which all the wealth on earth could not do.
The ratio eased from one-to-ten to one-to-two because weakness, a lack of togetherness, appeared.
The Israelites were told to enter the Holy Land and replied that Musa and his Lord should go and fight while they sat: a mentality problem.
The land was forbidden to them for forty years of wandering until a new generation came; this generation does not need forty years.
The owner of two gardens as the story about wealth
Musa's journey as the story about knowledge
Dhul-Qarnayn as the story about power

The transaction that saves from punishment: believe, then strive with wealth and lives; the reward is forgiveness, Jannah, victory and openings for those who follow. This is his definition of participation.

What happened at Uhud exposed the believers and the hypocrites, who were told to fight or defend and refused; they were nearer to disbelief than faith that day. Non-participation as the hypocrites' mark.
Nuh pleads for his son as family; Allah says he is not of your family and warns him against asking what he does not know; Nuh seeks refuge and forgiveness.
Work, and Allah, His Messenger and the believers will see your deeds.
Ibrahim's vision: a land of safety and security whose people are provided for.
'These, our people': they still saw the misguided as their own people, the basis of belonging.
Be mindful of your Lord and of kinship; Allah is ever Watchful over you
Hypocrites try to deceive Allah while He outwits them
Hypocrites in the lowest depth of the Fire with no helper

When the call to Friday prayer is given, leave trade and hasten; do not leave the Prophet standing to chase business. He reads the surah as the Quran's own description of what attendee and leader owe each other.
Every person carries his record on his own neck and will be handed a spread-open book: read your book, you are enough as an accountant against yourself today.
Let every soul look at what it has prepared for tomorrow, meaning the life after the grave, not the next ten years.
The same word for hateful, used for marrying a father's wife
Commanding righteousness while forgetting yourselves though you recite the Book
You thought it trivial but with Allah it is grave, about the slander
Allah and the believers who follow him are sufficient for the Prophet: the core group.
Helping one person live properly is like saving all of humanity.
Musa throws down the tablets and seizes his brother.

hadith.gist: The believer who mixes with people and bears their harm patiently is better than the one who does not mix with them
Abu Bakr: when people see an oppressor and do not stop him, Allah is close to punishing them all

Ka'b ibn Malik's hadith that the people of Madinah valued the night of the Bay'ah of Aqabah more than Badr, even though Badr is more celebrated, because that was when the relationship was established.

After the spoils were distributed following Hunayn the Ansar feared he would return to Makkah; the Prophet reassured them that his life and death were with them, that he was from them and they from him.
Yasin is the heart of the Quran; he notes the narration is weak though scholars accept the description.
Those who uphold Allah's limits and those who neglect them are like people on a two-deck ship; if the lower deck is allowed to drill a hole for water, all drown, and if stopped, all are saved.
Whatever befell the People of the Book before us will most likely befall us
Zaynab asked whether they would be destroyed while righteous people were among them; the Prophet said yes, when evil abounds.

Paragraph four: time has returned to its original form as on the day Allah created the heavens and earth, with the sacred months in their places; do not return after me to striking each other's necks.
After each statement the Prophet asked 'have I conveyed?', riders carried his words through the crowd, the people affirmed, and he said 'O Allah, be witness'.
Paragraph five: fear Allah regarding women; you took them by the trust of Allah and made them lawful by His word; they have rights over you and you over them; my advice is to treat them well.
Alluded to: the ummah is one body that feels the pain of any of its limbs.
Take from this world only the provision of a traveller.
Anas: the day the Prophet entered Medina everything was lit up, and the day he died everything went dark; the companions felt like strangers to one another after his burial
Mourning is limited to three days, after which one moves on carrying the lessons
The chance to repent and change remains as long as one breathes and until the sun rises from the west
Seven whom Allah shades on the Day when there is no shade but His, among them a man whose heart is attached to the masjid and a youth who grew up in the worship of Allah.
Ibn Mas'ud: in the Prophet's time only a hypocrite known for his hypocrisy missed the congregational prayer; a sick man would be carried between two men to be stood in the line.
Umar and an Ansari friend agreed to alternate attending the Prophet's gatherings while the other worked, each reporting to the other so neither missed anything.
A bedouin urinated in the Prophet's masjid
The Prophet taught people how to spit or clear their nose in the masjid and cleaned it from the floor himself
My Lord commanded me with five things, and the first was the jama'ah.

Two groups drew lots for the decks of a ship; the lower deck decided to drill a hole for water rather than disturb the upper deck. If the upper deck stops them, all are saved; if they leave them, all drown.
At the end of time a man will take his religion and flee to the mountains with his family and sheep.
Whoever leaves the jama'ah even a hand's span has removed the cloak of Islam from his neck.
The wolf only takes the sheep that is alone; the herd together cannot be eaten.
A famous saying of an early scholar: two groups decide a people's fate, the rulers and the scholars; if they are sound the people are sound, if corrupt the people are corrupt
The Prophet held the Eid prayer outdoors with women, children and whole families attending.
The scholars are heirs of the prophets, who left behind knowledge rather than wealth; whoever takes it takes an abundant share.

After an unusually long prayer the Prophet said he had asked Allah three things: that his ummah not be destroyed by a general punishment like earlier nations, granted; that no external enemy overpower them, granted; that they not fight among themselves, refused.
hadith.source: Tirmidhi and Muslim (as he names them)

hadith.gist: After Tabuk those who stayed behind came one by one with excuses; the Prophet accepted them outwardly, forgave them and asked Allah to forgive them, leaving their inner state to Allah
On campaigns the Prophet would ask about absent companions by name
Khawlah stops Umar as caliph and advises him at length; he says Allah heard her from above seven heavens, so Umar must listen
After the verse of the voices, Abu Bakr and Umar would only whisper near the Prophet
A companion who sought private counsel with the Prophet first gave charity
At the pledge with the people of Yathrib the Prophet set conditions; the second was to spend their wealth in ease and hardship.
The Prophet distributed even his own share of incoming wealth before entering his house.

A zakat collector said part of what he brought was a gift to him; the Prophet asked whether gifts would come if he sat at home, then raised his hands until his armpits showed, saying O Allah, have I conveyed.
Abu Bakr: by Allah, if they withhold even a cord they used to give the Prophet, I will fight them over it.
When the Prophet appealed for funds, those with nothing brought a date and hypocrites laughed at them.
There is to be no harm and no reciprocating harm
The Prophet foretold that the treasures of Kisra would come into the Muslims' hands, while people laughed at the idea.
Feed the hungry, visit the sick, and free the captive.
A believer does not mourn more than three days, except a widow for her husband.
Reading Surah al-Kahf every week.
The Prophet warned that the ummah's large numbers would fool it and would not protect it; referred to in passing, not quoted.
A believer to a believer is like a building, each part strengthening the other.
Everything of jahiliyyah is under my feet; the first blood claim and the first usury abolished are those of my own family.
Satan has despaired of being worshipped in your land but is content with what you consider minor deeds.
Do not return after me as disbelievers striking one another's necks.
Fear Allah regarding women; you took them as a trust from Allah.
The Prophet asked a young child about his pet bird that had died, taking children's concerns seriously; in his telling Umar objected that there was work to do.
Aishah was asked whether the Prophet prayed sitting; yes, after the people had worn him down, but he never stopped praying
A time will come when a man takes out his charity and finds no one to accept it.
A woman will ride her camel alone from al-Hirah to Makkah for Hajj fearing no one but Allah.
The day the Prophet entered Madinah everything lit up, and the day he died everything went dark; the companions felt like strangers to one another.
The worst of people is the two-faced one who comes to some with one face and to others with another
The Prophet would sometimes stand on the minbar and make the khutbah a recitation of Quran; some narrations say he recited Surah Qaf in full, others that he recited passages.
hadith.source: Sahih Muslim (Surah Qaf on the minbar)

hadith.gist: Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah
The Prophet paired newcomers in Madinah with established believers in brotherhood
At the second pledge of Aqabah the Prophet named five things he required: allegiance, wealth in ease and hardship, enjoining good and reform, standing firm in battle, and protecting him.
At Hunayn, when the Muslims fled, the Prophet had al-Abbas call out to those who had pledged allegiance to him, and they returned.
In his first years in Madinah the Prophet built the masjid, joined emigrants and Ansar in brotherhood, and had all parties sign the Constitution of Madinah.
Hold yourselves to account before you are held to account, and weigh your deeds before they are weighed for you (the saying usually attributed to Umar ibn al-Khattab).
The Prophet would walk the rows and align them by the shoulders before prayer
Straighten your rows or Allah will cause discord between your hearts
Sawad at Badr asked to retaliate for the Prophet's tap and instead embraced him
On Eid the whole community, women and children included, went out to pray in the open.
In his final days the Prophet offered anyone whose wealth he had taken or whom he had harmed to take their due from him.
A time will come when you are many but like the foam on the flood, numerous and weightless.

You don't have to agree with everything to support someone

You're either on the wagon or under it
Narratives change in academia, not from the minbar
Keep it moving; criticize later
The real problem we carry is internal
Taqwa is measured by Allah's status, not your ability
You don't know how graphs work
Hold on to the rope together, not each individually

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)

spans.note: The world follows the law of the strong, the law of the jungle; a Muslim with knowledge refuses to join or strengthen it and must not oppress the moment he gains power.

lectures.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Revelation to Ethics

spans.note: Humanity still lives by the law of the jungle where the bigger gun makes and breaks the rules; reforming that is one of the outcomes Islam exists for.

lectures.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Sunnah to Mindset

spans.note: The Prophet spent his life telling people to stand up to oppression, defend, speak up and die for justice; he would not care about beard length while his ummah starves and does nothing about its weakness.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Muzzammil, Part 3: Verses 10-19

spans.note: Muslims must still stand against oppression, but leaving oppressors to Allah relieves helpless anguish; every wrong will be paid for.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Muddaththir, Part 2: Verses 7-14

spans.note: When oppressors are honoured, leave their outcome to Allah rather than letting rage consume you.

lectures.title: Listening to the Divine: Al-Nahl 90-97

spans.note: Verse 90 commands justice, excellence and care for kin and forbids indecency, evil and oppression: the terms of the covenant every Muslim accepts.

lectures.title: Listening to the Divine: An-Nahl 90-97, Part 2

spans.note: Selling the covenant includes being just only to people you like and withholding fairness from a group that looks, smells or speaks differently.

lectures.title: Listening to the Divine: An-Nur 54-57

spans.note: The goal of engagement is a world without meaningless bloodshed, persecution and double standards, where the law of the jungle does not rule.

lectures.title: The Values of Islam: Introduction to Values, Principles and Ethics

spans.note: Truthful testimony against one's own parents shows justice outranking family loyalty.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 5: Quranic Themes 2 - Istiqamah and Moral Absolutism

spans.note: Islam's burden of proof and inheritance rules protected the weak, and people still try to evade them.

lectures.title: Promises (Ramadan 2026, Night 14: Quranic Themes 2)

spans.note: Oppressors' dominance is short and their fall certain, in this world or the next.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Participation

spans.note: The ummah's long-term goal is dawah, justice and the removal of oppression; keep the eye on that goal while taking the basic steps.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Initiative

spans.note: Evil individuals rule and imperial forces bomb the poor because people of good did not push back; the people of falsehood raised their banner while the people of truth were too busy or embarrassed to raise theirs.

lectures.title: Arabic Tafsir of Surat Yusuf: The Proof of His Lord

spans.note: Evidence-based judgment through the torn shirt.

lectures.title: Arabic Tafseer: Surah Yusuf (12:22-29)

spans.note: Wrongdoers never succeed, however long they rule.

lectures.title: From Populations to Communities: Religious Centralization

spans.note: Tyrants jail independent imams, script khutbahs, and in Syria shut the country on Fridays and bombed mosques because the uprising left from them; they understand the power of religious centralization better than Muslims do.

lectures.title: Bad Religiosity #2: Worship That Does Not Pass the Throat

spans.note: Even when criticising a group, the Prophet stayed fair and acknowledged their genuine qualities.

lectures.title: The Implications of Knowing: Moral Integrity (Part 1)

spans.note: Winning a dispute before the Prophet himself through a better argument does not make a right yours; taking what you know is not yours is eating a piece of the Fire.

lectures.title: Essentials and Pet Peeves: Indoctrination

spans.note: People devoted to truth resist oppression.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat 'Abasa, Part 2: Verses 17-32

spans.note: People tolerate injustice when it benefits them, as Quraysh did.

Stand firm for justice and testify truthfully even against yourselves and your parents.
Stand for justice even against yourselves

Badr is the Day of Criterion, separating truth from falsehood.

Allah promised one of the two parties and they wished for the unarmed one, but He willed to establish the truth; haqq recurs six times in these verses.
Good grieves them, harm delights them; with patience and taqwa their plots will not harm you; Allah encompasses what they do

Judgment of jahiliyyah: the political use.
Nuh's people despised the poor who followed him

Revelation defending a Jewish man falsely accused of stealing a shield.
The steep path of freeing captives and feeding the needy in hard times.
If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first worshipper: worship follows evidence
Muslims ask for a straight path rather than a destination
Had the Prophet fabricated anything, Allah would have seized him
Those who plot by night what Allah does not approve
Some believers disliked going out to Badr; Allah promised one of two outcomes
Salih's arrogant chiefs reject whatever the believers believed in
Leave Me with the deniers who enjoy luxury
Zayd and Zaynab, two righteous people whose marriage still did not work.
Those who take full measure when buying and give short when selling: respecting the scale.
Grant slaves who seek it an agreement to buy their freedom.
Allah does not wrong anyone an atom's weight and multiplies good deeds
In the scriptures of Musa and Ibrahim: no soul bears another's burden
They carry their own burdens fully and some of those they misled
Tell the believers to forgive those who do not hope for the days of Allah
That is Allah your Lord; His is the kingdom, so how are you turned away

Who owns hearing and sight and brings the living from the dead
They ask what to spend; say: the surplus
The amanah offered to the heavens, earth and mountains, refused, and accepted by man, who is zaluman jahulan; the verse that frames both traits.
Man transgresses when he sees himself self-sufficient: systematic oppression born of feeling that one needs nobody.
The earth will report what was done on it
Ears, eyes and skin testify, and the assumption about their Lord ruined them
the mosque built to cause harm; what is built on falsehood is false
Towns were destroyed when they did wrong, at an appointed time: the opening hook on oppression.
Ruined towns, abandoned wells and palaces; it is hearts, not eyes, that go blind when people look away from injustice.
The weak tell the arrogant they only followed them, an excuse Allah rejects

Allah may place love between believers and former enemies, once oppression is removed.
Did people think they would be left alone saying 'we believe' without being tested? Allah tests to make known the truthful and the liars.
Opening verse, recited then translated at 495: nations before you were destroyed for oppression after clear signs, then you were made successors on earth to see how you would act
Musa tells his people to seek Allah's help and be patient; the earth belongs to Allah; your enemy may be destroyed and you made successors, and then Allah watches how you act
The heir of the murdered must not exceed limits in retribution.
Nine men plot to kill Salih and his family by night
They argued with you about the truth after it was clear, as if being driven to death: the reluctance was fear of battle, not love of money.
Creation is founded on truth and admitting falsehood into it ruins it. Paraphrase only; the verse could also be one of the 'created with truth' verses.
The guilty would ransom children, spouse, brother, clan and everyone on earth to escape Hell.
The most honoured with Allah is the most righteous; quoted inside the sermon on equality.
Musa swooned when he asked to see Allah, a possible reason he is spared at the blow.

The father whose face darkens at news of a daughter, torn between keeping her in humiliation or burying her.

Help your brother whether he is oppressor or oppressed; you help the oppressor by holding him back from his oppression.
Whoever is slowed by his deeds will not be sped up by his lineage.
Leave tribal rallying cries, for they are rotten.
You are a man in whom there is still jahiliyyah, said to Abu Dharr after he insulted Bilal.
If Fatima the daughter of Muhammad stole, I would cut off her hand.
A man lashed for drinking was cursed by a companion; the Prophet forbade it, saying he loves Allah and His Messenger
Allah does not remove knowledge by plucking it from people's chests but by taking away the scholars, until people take ignorant leaders who misguide them
I am only human and judge by what I hear; one of you may argue more eloquently and win, but whoever I award his brother's right is being given a piece of the Fire
A dusty, dishevelled man raises his hands in humble supplication, but his food, drink and clothing are from haram, so how can he be answered
Support your brother whether oppressor or oppressed; when the companions asked how to support an oppressor, he said: hold him back from oppression.
Let no one be stopped by fear of people from speaking the truth when he sees it
O My servants, I have forbidden oppression for Myself and made it forbidden among you
If Fatimah the daughter of Muhammad stole, I would apply the punishment
A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim; he does not let him down or turn his back on him.
Support your brother whether he is oppressor or oppressed; you support the oppressor by stopping him.

Amr ibn Salim came pleading in verse after his tribe Khuza'ah, the Prophet's allies, were massacred in breach of the treaty, and the Prophet promised him support and moved an army.
The Prophet never became angry for himself, but when truth and justice were violated his anger did not subside until it was set right.
Near the end of time killing and chaos (harj) will spread among people.
I am only human; you bring disputes to me and one may argue better than the other; whoever I give something of his brother's right, I am giving him a piece of the Fire.
A man on a long journey, dishevelled, raises his hands saying O Lord, O Lord, but his food, drink and clothing are unlawful; how can he be answered?
The signs of a hypocrite: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, when entrusted he betrays.
Whoever unjustly takes another's right will be held accountable, even if it is only a twig of miswak.
Hasten to good deeds before trials come like pieces of dark night, when a man wakes a believer and sleeps a disbeliever, or the reverse, selling his religion for a bit of worldly gain.
Oppression will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection.
Allah says: O My servants, I have forbidden oppression upon Myself and made it forbidden among you, so do not oppress one another.
The just leader is among those shaded by the Throne and whose prayers are answered
Help your brother whether he is an oppressor or oppressed; help the oppressor by stopping him

In his final pilgrimage the Prophet annulled all riba, starting with that owed to al-Abbas
Hadith qudsi: Allah has forbidden oppression for Himself and made it forbidden among His servants, so do not wrong one another.
Beware of oppression, for it will be darkness on the Day of Judgment.
Beware the dua of the oppressed, even a disbeliever, for nothing stands between it and Allah.
The dua of the oppressed is answered even if he is sinful; his sin is upon himself.

The first matter judged between people on the Day of Judgment is bloodshed.
For Allah to guide one person through you is better for you than everything in the world.
Help your brother whether he is a wrongdoer or wronged; you help the wrongdoer by stopping him.
No obedience to any created being in disobedience of the Creator
All matters of jahiliyyah are under my feet; the first blood I abolish is Rabi'ah's, the first riba that of Abbas.
A man is brought and his deeds rise before him until he thinks he will be saved, then those he wronged take them all.

Those before you were destroyed because they let the noble thief go and punished the weak
