themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons

lectures.title: Prophet Muhammad's Final Sermon

spans.note: Walk through the Farewell Sermon at Arafah: its setting, the relayed crowd, the questions about the day, month and land, and the repeated 'have I conveyed?'.
Knowing his death was near, he stood among the Ansar and Muhajirun twenty years after being reviled, and chose the sanctity of blood as his will.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2025 Night 10: Quranic Themes, Courage

spans.note: The cave of the Hijrah retold as an act of courage by men who expected to die, not as a guaranteed rescue.
Tabuk: the excuse-makers, the weeping poor, and the companion who gave his honour.

lectures.title: Listening to the Divine: Aal-Imran 137-145

spans.note: Uhud was a felt defeat: the Prophet's grief and visits to the martyrs, Mus'ab's shroud, and the exposure of who had what it takes.
The rumour of the Prophet's death at Uhud and the verse that he is only a messenger: the deen was never tied to his presence.

lectures.title: Listening to the Divine: At-Tawbah 38-43

spans.note: Tabuk: the Roman threat, the Prophet's habit of concealing destinations and his decision to name this one openly, and the exhausted companions who hesitated.
The hijrah as a lesson in planning and courage: every precaution taken, pursuers at the cave mouth anyway, and the Prophet's calm 'do not be sad' when he did not know what would happen next.

lectures.title: Arafah Day Program: Workshop on the Farewell Sermon

spans.note: The whole program studies the Farewell Sermon paragraph by paragraph.

lectures.title: Saturday Seerah Halaqah: The Farewell Hajj and Sermon

spans.note: The Farewell Hajj and how the farewell sermon was delivered and transmitted.

lectures.title: The Expedition of Tabuk and the Story of Ka'b ibn Malik

spans.note: The Tabuk expedition and Ka'b's staying back, confession, boycott and forgiveness.

lectures.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: An Offering and a Return

spans.note: Detailed narration of the Second Pledge of Aqabah: its terms, the Ansar's questions, the Prophet's mutual pledge, and the warning about its cost.

lectures.title: Ramadan Reminders 1446: Part 2, Badr and Doing What Is Right

spans.note: Badr came in the first Ramadan ever fasted; comfortable companions resisted, Allah intended to establish truth, and the day of distinction secured Islam's future.

lectures.title: The Farewell Hajj and the Farewell Sermon

spans.note: The Farewell Hajj and Sermon as the Prophet's last address to his whole ummah.

lectures.title: The Final Sermon, Part 1

spans.note: The Prophet's farewell Hajj retold through Jabir's hadith: the years of being barred from Makkah, the patient clearing of the city, the first peaceful return, and the final public address of his life.

lectures.title: The Final Sermon, Part 2

spans.note: The whole lecture is a reading of the Farewell Sermon as the Prophet's chosen legacy statement, given publicly with no private context, three months before his death.

lectures.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Defining the Metrics

spans.note: The migration to Abyssinia as the first true test of Islamic character once oppression was removed, and Ja'far's speech to the Negus as a pure before-and-after of ethics with no mention of rituals.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Muzzammil, Part 1: Verses 1-5

spans.note: A detailed retelling of Hira, the first revelation and its aftermath as the key to understanding the surah.

lectures.title: Post-Fajr Quranic Story: The Martyrs of Uhud and Hamra al-Asad

spans.note: The martyrdom of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram at Uhud and the march to Hamra al-Asad as the background of the verses.

lectures.title: Third Week of Ramadan: Showing Commitment to Change

spans.note: Badr retold as the Sahabah's test of commitment in their first Ramadan: the reluctant response to the call, the escaped caravan, 313 men against a thousand, and the first army in Arabia bound by conviction rather than blood.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Summary

spans.note: The last Makkan years: refusing conditional support from tribes, the six youth of Yathrib, the demand for buy-in from both tribes, the five points of Aqabah, entering Madinah with fewer than a thousand Muslims, and his reassurance to the Ansar after Hunayn.

lectures.title: Fifth Annual Iftar: The Day of Arafah

spans.note: Jabir's narration of the farewell Hajj.

lectures.title: Building Adherence to Righteousness

spans.note: The first Ramadan and the companions' objection to pursuing the caravan, read through Al-Anfal's emphasis on haqq.
Badr's odds, the rank of the Badri companions, and how Allah tells the story through righteousness rather than narrative detail.

lectures.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The First Article, Adherence (Followship and Learning)

spans.note: The Ansar came to the Prophet and said 'take for yourself and your Lord what you want'; he asked for five things, the first being to hear and obey.
Those present at Aqabah considered it greater than Badr because it was the day they gave their word and then lived by it until death.

lectures.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The Second Article, Committing Wealth (Part 2)

spans.note: The Prophet sought no power or luxury and kept Madinah simple, asking only for a pledge that benefited those who gave it.
Tabuk: the poor brought handfuls of dates, a rich companion gave a fortune, and both mattered.

lectures.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The Fourth Article, Prioritizing the Message

spans.note: Yathrib before the Prophet was a city with no future; he reached it after many attempts with the tribes and only once its people offered the pledge.
Quraysh's negotiations sought a small compromise to empty the message of its authenticity, and their leaders asked him to dismiss the weak believers; he refused both.

lectures.title: Ramadan Reminders 1446: Victory Is Not a Handout

spans.note: The conquest of Mecca on the 20th of Ramadan 8 AH came after twenty-one years of work, and the Prophet entered with his head bowed and turned Sa'd's day of slaughter into a day of mercy.
The companions had to be pushed out of comfort through Badr, Uhud, the Trench, the murdered teachers and the obedience test of Hudaybiyyah before the conquest came.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Jinn, Part 1: Verses 1-10

spans.note: The surah's occasion: the Prophet's hardest day, walking aimlessly after Ta'if.
His lowest, planless night, with Khadijah and Abu Talib gone, when the jinn watched his character and listened to his prayer.

lectures.title: Listening to the Divine: Aal-Imran 102-112

spans.note: The aftermath of Uhud: prominent companions lost, the Prophet's wounds and headaches until his death, treaties broken by neighbouring tribes, and mutual blame; the verses were sent into that moment.
Arabic account of the companions' shame and confusion after Uhud and how the second half of Aal-Imran rebuilt them.

lectures.title: The Values of Islam: Righteousness, Justice and Refusing Oppression

spans.note: The Quran exonerating a Jewish man framed for a theft by Muslims.
Badr as reclaiming rights the emigrants had been robbed of.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 4 (33:7-9)

spans.note: Background and course of the Battle of the Trench, from the coalition to the wind.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 5 (33:10-12)

spans.note: Hunger, the Qurayzah betrayal, the scouts, the Prophet's exhaustion and Jabir's meal.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 9 (33:21-27)

spans.note: Qurayzah's betrayal, the two Sa'ds, Nu'aym's ruse, the withdrawal, and the siege of Qurayzah.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 12 (33:35-36)

spans.note: Zayd ibn Harithah's life, his choice of the Prophet, and his marriage to Zaynab.

lectures.title: Surah Summaries: Surat Al-Jinn

spans.note: The return from Ta'if and the night prayer the jinn overheard.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Fussilat, Part 1 (41:1-8)

spans.note: The Quraysh envoy's offers and the Prophet's patient listening.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Fussilat, Part 2 (41:9-14)

spans.note: Utbah's reaction to the recitation and his death at Badr.

lectures.title: Attributes of the Prophet: His Bravery

spans.note: Hunayn, the Kaaba confrontation, Uhud, the Hijrah and the Madinah night alarm.

lectures.title: Attributes of the Prophet: His Grit

spans.note: Makkan persecution, the Trench, Badr, the Hijrah, the slander and the boycott.

lectures.title: Attributes of the Prophet: His Loyalty

spans.note: Badr, Uhud, the boycott, the Ansar's pledge and Hudaybiyyah read through loyalty.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 20: Quranic Reflections (Al-Ankabut to Al-Ahzab)

spans.note: At the Trench the Prophet was named the best example and the believers' iman grew as the danger grew.

lectures.title: Attributes of the Prophet: His Ease, Tenderness and Flexibility

spans.note: Abyssinia, Badr, Uhud, the Trench, Hudaybiyyah and the brotherhood.

lectures.title: Facing Disbelief 7: Violence, Freedoms, Women in Islam, and the Fourth Source of Iman: You

spans.note: Executions, apostasy, the riddah wars and Banu Qurayzah read in political and historical context.

lectures.title: The Five Categories of Community Investment

spans.note: The pledge of Aqabah, Hunayn, and the first two years in Madinah show the Prophet working to clear, measurable goals.

lectures.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: The Compeller, Al-Jabbar

spans.note: Ta'if, the dua of complaint and the meeting with Addas.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Hashr, Part 1: Verses 1-4

spans.note: Banu al-Nadir's boulder plot and refusal of justice broke the constitution.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Mumtahinah, Part 1: Verses 1-3

spans.note: The broken treaty, the secret march on Mecca, Hatib's letter and his pardon for Badr.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Mumtahinah, Part 3: Verses 8-10

spans.note: The Hudaybiyyah clause, Umm Kulthum's emigration and Abu Basir's band.

lectures.title: The Laws of Success/Victory 1: Getting Our House in Order
lectures.series: The Laws of Success and Victory

spans.note: Madinah as a working society: migrants in Ansar homes, shared wealth, new political, social and financial models, and the explosive spread of Islam within thirty years.

lectures.title: The Laws of Success/Victory 3: Preparation
lectures.series: The Laws of Success and Victory

spans.note: The first and second pledges of Aqabah, with the second article of the pledge being to give what you have, whether much or little.

lectures.title: The Laws of Success/Victory 5: Righteousness
lectures.series: The Laws of Success and Victory

spans.note: Before Badr some believers resisted chasing Abu Sufyan's caravan out of comfort and fear; Allah's answer was that it was about haqq, not wealth.

lectures.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: The Almighty, Al-Aziz

spans.note: Badr, the Trench and the Hijrah each close with the name, since victory is from Allah alone.

lectures.title: The Laws of Success/Victory 6: Sparing No Effort
lectures.series: The Laws of Success and Victory

spans.note: A close reading of Badr through Al-Anfal: the race for the higher bank, Abu Sufyan's caravan diverting, the rain, the Prophet's dream of fewer enemies, and the nap before battle.

lectures.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Names of Divine Judgment, Al-Hakeem (The All-Wise)

spans.note: Hudaybiyyah as the clearest display of the Prophet's wisdom.

lectures.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Names of Support and Aid, Al-Wakeel (The Trustee)

spans.note: The Hijrah plan and the cave, and tying the Buraq on the Night Journey.

lectures.title: An Additional Three Ramadan Reminders

spans.note: The Quranic telling of how Badr began, with believers reluctant to pursue the caravan.

lectures.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Wadud (The Most Loving)

spans.note: Allah's love in the first revelation and in His consolations at the Prophet's hardest moments.

lectures.title: Final Three Ramadan Reminders

spans.note: The Prophet's last-hour meeting at Mina with the six from Yathrib after 26 rejections.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Munafiqun, Part 2 (Verses 4-7)

spans.note: The expedition, Ibn Ubayy's history and the Prophet's restraint.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Munafiqun, Part 3 (Verses 8-11)

spans.note: Events of the expedition and their aftermath.

lectures.title: Between June 6th and Rafah: The Day After

spans.note: Uhud's aftermath: the Prophet's curse answered by 3:128 and the verses revealed to steady the believers.

lectures.title: Arafah Program 2024: The Symbolism of Hajj

spans.note: The Farewell Hajj from Jabir's account to the final sermon.

lectures.title: Activism, Our Path Forward: The Pursuit of Guidance for All

spans.note: Thumamah ibn Uthal accepted Islam after three days observing the companions' devotion and compassion in the masjid.

lectures.title: Outreach, The Way of Our Prophets: Verbal and Practical
lectures.series: Outreach: The Way of Our Prophets

spans.note: The Prophet lived at the lowest point and built the ummah one person at a time; being Muslim in a dark time makes us closer to his experience, not further.

lectures.title: Outreach, The Way of Our Prophets: What If?
lectures.series: Outreach: The Way of Our Prophets

spans.note: Badr and the Trench as Allah's hypotheticals: a different dream or a different entry point would have broken the believers.

lectures.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: Why an Oath of Allegiance?

spans.note: From Mecca's rejection to the two meetings at Aqabah: the Prophet came to Yathrib only after its people pledged, and transformed it.

lectures.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The Second Article, Committing Wealth

spans.note: Yathrib was corrupt and low in status, but the Ansar's commitment and kept word made them the Prophet's choice and carried Islam to the world.

lectures.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The Third Article, Reforming Social Values

spans.note: The Prophet reformed slavery, domestic abuse and women's rights, and refused to drop equality to win over Quraysh's leaders.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Ahzab Summary, Part 1

spans.note: The Battle of the Trench is read as the hardest test the Muslims faced and the setting Allah chose to name the Prophet as the model.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Fath Summary

spans.note: Hudaybiyyah: the journey, the pledge, the treaty and its results.

lectures.title: Surah Al-Balad Summary

spans.note: The return from Ta'if and entry into Makkah under protection frame the surah.

lectures.title: Surah Ad-Duha Summary

spans.note: The months-long pause in revelation and Quraysh's mockery set the context.

lectures.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The Third Article, Reforming Social Values (Part 2)

spans.note: The Prophet kept good Arab values and removed racism, infanticide, usury and autocracy, consulting people himself and stripping status from those who resisted.

lectures.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The Fifth Article, Protecting the Message

spans.note: The fifth article of Aqabah, protecting the Prophet like one's family, read as a pledge to protect the message itself.

lectures.title: There Is God

spans.note: At the Trench the Prophet saw his companions' broken morale and gave them hope while working beside them.

lectures.title: Personal Reflections

spans.note: The hijrah as forced displacement: canvassing the tribes in years ten and eleven, leaving the city of his ancestors, calling Makkah the land he loved most, and never moving back out of loyalty to Madinah while building something greater.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 4: Quranic Themes, Avoiding Distractions

spans.note: The archers, those who fled, the rumour of the Prophet's death and the martyrs of Uhud.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Pearls 3: Reflection and Contemplation

spans.note: The Prophet's retreats in Hira and his year-round i'tikaf as models of contemplation.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2025 Night 11: Quranic Themes, Tawakkul

spans.note: The Prophet under Makkan pressure is told he is only a warner and should leave what he cannot change to Allah.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2025 Night 18: Companionship

spans.note: Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt lost the chance to be a companion of the Prophet because of his best friend.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2025 Night 20: Divine Hypotheses

spans.note: The Battle of the Trench was the community's hardest moment, ended by the collapse of the Confederates' plot and a fierce wind.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2025 Night 23: Sincere Da'wah

spans.note: The Prophet refused Quraysh's offers through Utbah, showing dawah with no personal agenda.

lectures.title: Pointing Out the Obvious 6: Tolerance

spans.note: The Constitution of Medina, the Khuza'a alliance, renewed treaties and the Roman victory show the Prophet allying with non-Muslims.

lectures.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Saffat, Part 9: Verses 171-182

spans.note: Abu Sufyan at the conquest of Makkah and the Prophet at Uhud show that knowing the ending makes mercy possible.

lectures.title: Ramadan Reminders 1446: The Last Hour of Ramadan

spans.note: The Prophet's twenty-six failed approaches in the tenth year and his final-hour meeting with six young men of Yathrib in an empty Mina show that persistence until nothing is left to do built the ummah.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Muddaththir, Part 2: Verses 7-14

spans.note: Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah's status in Mecca and Uthman ibn Maz'un's renunciation of his protection.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Muddaththir, Part 3: Verses 18-30

spans.note: How the leaders of Mecca struggled to answer the Prophet and turned to Walid for a line to repeat.

lectures.title: The Quran's Outcomes for Character: The Good News

spans.note: The Prophet's life as forty years of blows, then slander, persecution, bereavement, exile and war, ending in the conquest of Mecca; through it all he kept empathy and composure.

lectures.title: Listening to the Divine: An-Nahl 90-97, Part 2

spans.note: Uthman ibn Maz'un's conversion out of shyness, and the exhausting tour of twenty-six tribes in ten days in the tenth year that produced one reasonable hearing from Banu Shayban.

lectures.title: Ramadan Preparation: Taking Advantage of Opportunities

spans.note: Afif al-Kindi saw the first Muslim family praying at the Kaaba and let the moment pass; a lifelong regret about a closed door.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 4: Quranic Themes 2 - Accepting Mortality

spans.note: Uhud and the rumour of the Prophet's death expose a weak acceptance of mortality among some companions.

lectures.title: The Values of Islam: Incorruptibility and Moral Absolutism (Istiqama)

spans.note: The Prophet rejected kingship and segregated sessions for the elite.

lectures.title: Receiving Allah's Bounty (Ramadan 2026, Night 9: Quranic Themes 2)

spans.note: Badr as a battle arranged by Allah through terrain, rain, a dream and perception; Hunayn as a near-defeat caused by confidence in numbers.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2026 Night 21: Using Our Intellectual Faculties

spans.note: The Prophet's seclusion in Hira and the first coming of Jibril show revelation answering a mind fully engaged.

lectures.title: Fourth Week of Ramadan: Turning to Allah to Grant Success

spans.note: Shaybah ibn Uthman came to Hunayn hating the Prophet and intending to kill him; a touch and a dua turned him into a defender, showing Allah wanting good for someone who wanted evil for himself.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Initiative

spans.note: In Makkah the Prophet lacked numbers, wealth and status yet was never on the ropes; Quraysh were always reacting. He supported the seventy Qurra who built their own study and dawah circle and taught the people of Suffah trades.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Religious Adherence

spans.note: The siege of the confederates and the contrasting reactions of believers and hypocrites, then Bi'r Ma'unah and the martyrdom of Haram ibn Milhan.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Accountability

spans.note: The Trench, Abu Shahm's withheld bay'ah and the Mu'tah latecomer show that the Prophet gave no free passes and that his companions were used to being held accountable.

lectures.title: Hajj Lessons: The Attempts of Shaytan

spans.note: The Bay'ah of Aqabah with the 72 Ansar as the critical moment every later good depended on, and Shaytan's attempt to ruin it by screaming to the people in the tents.

lectures.title: Hajj Lessons: Knowing and Deciding

spans.note: The day of Taif as the Prophet's hardest day: humiliated, banned from Makkah, with no plan, yet he refuses to have his tormentors punished. Also the boycott decision, Abraha's elephant and the Ansar's bay'ah at Mina.

lectures.title: From Populations to Communities: Political Centralization

spans.note: The Prophet began with his family, worked locally in Medina, built brotherhoods and centralized the community's life so that it functioned after he was gone; Anas's description of the city lit on his arrival and darkened at his death.

lectures.title: From Populations to Communities: Political Centralization

spans.note: The Prophet built Madinah locally before looking outward.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Ankabut Summary

spans.note: The surah prepared the Prophet and companions for the pain of leaving Mecca in the hijrah.
The road to Madinah was the path Allah guided the strivers to.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2023 Night 26: Tahajjud

spans.note: The Prophet's dua on the night of Badr.

lectures.title: The Five Categories of Community Investment: Financial Centralization

spans.note: The pledge of the people of Yathrib included committing their wealth, which enabled the Prophet's state.

lectures.title: Ramadan Prep: The Philosophy of Fasting

spans.note: The companions' first Ramadan and Badr fought while fasting show Ramadan as a time of peak productivity.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2024 Night 10: Quranic Reflections on At-Tawbah and Yunus

spans.note: Repeated treaty betrayals and the Tabuk campaign explain At-Tawbah's tone.

lectures.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Ra'd, Part 3

spans.note: The Prophet's 23 years show success came through long struggle and setbacks.

lectures.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-'Aziz (The Unfathomable)

spans.note: Badr, the Trench and the cave as victories through Allah's unseen soldiers.

lectures.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-'Afuw (The Pardoner)

spans.note: The conquest of Makkah as the Prophet's supreme act of pardon.

lectures.title: End of Ramadan Reflections

spans.note: Badr took place in Ramadan because the struggle was outside Medina, not in the comfort of the masjid.

lectures.title: A Talk on Hajj: Walking in the Footsteps of Adam, Ibrahim and Muhammad

spans.note: The Farewell Hajj: completion of the religion and the end of jahiliyyah.

lectures.title: Activism - Our Path Forward: Answering the Why

spans.note: The Prophet left Makkah never to live there again and found his home torn down when he returned; he compares this to people whose homes are demolished today.

lectures.title: Activism, Our Path Forward: Companionship and Masajid

spans.note: Building the Prophet's masjid in Madinah: he carried stones himself, and the companions chanted as they worked.

lectures.title: Stages of the Hereafter 3: Death

spans.note: During years of Qurashi resistance, the reminder that his opponents would also die comforted the Prophet.

lectures.title: Towards a Modern Awakening, Ep. 3: Networking and Mentorship

spans.note: On the Ascension the Prophet met earlier prophets, and Musa advised him on the prayers.

lectures.title: Towards a Modern Awakening, Ep. 4: Efficiency and Effectiveness

spans.note: The trench as a model of organised, complete execution.

lectures.title: Pointing Out the Obvious 2: Conspiracy Theories

spans.note: The Prophet gathered intelligence and kept building despite plots.

lectures.title: The Spirituality of Hajj, Part 2

spans.note: The Prophet approaching six youths of Yathrib after rejection by every tribe.

lectures.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Rituals to Connection

spans.note: Al-Muzzammil returns the Prophet to the night he ran down the mountain asking Khadijah to cover him; Allah's answer to that fear was the command to stand at night and speak to Him.

lectures.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Sunnah to Mindset

spans.note: From one man, his wife, a ten-year-old and a friend to a faith spanning three continents in thirty years; how he did it should be the first thing we study.

lectures.title: The Quran's Outcomes for Character: Oppression and Ignorance

spans.note: During the rebuilding of the Kaaba, on the brink of civil war, Quraysh agreed to accept whoever entered next and welcomed the Prophet as the trustworthy one.

lectures.title: Listening to the Divine: Al-Nahl 90-97

spans.note: Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah's testimony that the Quran is not human speech, retracted under Abu Jahl's pressure, shows the power of these specific verses.

lectures.title: Listening to the Divine: Al-Isra 23-39

spans.note: The Prophet died thirty years before the ummah's expansion, yet in the middle of persecution he promised the treasures of Kisra, the gates of Mada'in and the Roman castles.

lectures.title: Ramadan Preparation: Focusing on One's Self

spans.note: The Prophet's first recorded public sermon: he could warn and teach people how to save themselves but could not save anyone, not even Fatima, from the fire.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Participation

spans.note: Preparing the army against the Romans, the Prophet saw that the wealth collected did not match the heads counted because half contributed nothing.

lectures.title: From Populations to Communities: Social Centralization

spans.note: The Makkan Muslims had religious leadership but could not centralize society, finances or politics, so they migrated; in Medina the Prophet gathered everyone in one place to build a culture, the model for social centralization.

lectures.title: From Populations to Communities: Social Centralization

spans.note: The hijrah was about gathering Muslims to build culture.

lectures.title: From Populations to Communities: Financial Centralization

spans.note: The Prophet never wanted to leave Makkah, his family's home for generations, but the ummah needed to organize; in Medina he centralized society, finances, politics and religion, which is why Islam spread within a decade of his death.

lectures.title: From Populations to Communities: Financial Centralization

spans.note: The hijrah was about organizing the ummah.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat 'Abasa, Part 1 (80:1-16)

spans.note: The early Makkan context of seeking freedom to preach and safety for converts.

lectures.title: Essentials and Pet Peeves: Community

spans.note: Life in the Prophet's masjid, its annoyances and its fruits.

cites.point: 'Today I have completed your religion for you' was heard on that day; no other faith has such a verse, so everything taught is handed forward with nothing to add.
'Today I have completed your religion for you' came down on Arafah during this Hajj; the Jew's remark to Umar and Abu Bakr's sobbing show it was understood as the peak and the farewell.
The completion of the religion revealed at Arafah, signalling his death was near.
Today I have perfected your religion.
The religion perfected at Arafah, signalling the end of the Prophet's mission.
This day I have perfected your religion, read as a sign the Prophet's mission was ending.
The completion of the religion, which Abu Bakr understood as the Prophet's approaching death.
Do not grieve, Allah is with us
In the cave the Prophet told his companion not to grieve, for Allah is with them.
The two in the cave; the verse ends with Allah Almighty, Wise
The Hijrah verse closing with Allah Almighty and Wise
Safa and Marwa are among Allah's symbols; begin where Allah began
'Safa and Marwah are among the rituals of Allah'; he began sa'i with Safa because Allah mentioned it first.
Safa and Marwah among the rites; begin with what Allah began with.
The noblest is the most God-conscious
The Prophet recites that the most honoured before Allah is the one with most taqwa, grounding the statement that no race or lineage carries merit.
The noblest is the one with most taqwa, the basis of human equality.
He says the Prophet had 'just received his obituary' and knew he would not live long; the surah is not named but this is the standard reference.
When victory comes and people enter Islam in droves, glorify your Lord and seek forgiveness: the instruction for the top of the mountain.
People entering Islam in crowds, a joyous sign that also signalled the end.
Badr is the Day of Criterion, separating truth from falsehood.
Badr as the day of criterion when the two groups met
Badr as the day of distinction between truth and falsehood, remembered until the end of time.
The angels were only good news; victory comes from Allah alone, so do not treat the means as the cause.
Angels were glad tidings; victory is only from Allah the Almighty, Wise
Victory is only from Allah, the Almighty, the Wise, after Badr
The drowsiness and the rain before Badr, details the Muslims could not have arranged.
Rain and drowsiness sent before Badr
The drowsiness and rain given before Badr
Those who pledge to you pledge to Allah, whose hand is above theirs: the concept of the bay'ah is Quranic even though its points are not.
Those who pledge to the Prophet pledge to Allah; the hand of Allah is over their hands.
The Prophet's prayer for hearts to come mirrors Ibrahim's call
Allah told Ibrahim to call to Hajj and people would come from every corner on foot and on lean mounts; the Prophet asks Allah to bring hearts to him the same way.
He recited it on reaching Maqam Ibrahim after tawaf
The Prophet recited 'take the standing place of Ibrahim as a place of prayer' before praying two rak'ahs behind the maqam.
Twelve months with four sacred
The twelve months and four sacred ones since the creation of the heavens and earth, behind 'time has returned to its original form'.
Yunus leaves in anger and calls out in the darkness.
Yunus leaving his people in frustration and his time in the whale
He who ordained the Quran for you will return you home
Allah's promise to return the Prophet to Makkah after he lost his home
Some believers disliked going out to Badr; Allah promised one of two outcomes

Your Lord brought you out of your home in truth while a party of believers were averse, arguing about the truth as if driven to death, after Allah promised one of the two groups. The Sahabah's reluctance before Badr.
Seeing the Confederates only increased the believers' faith and submission
When the believers saw the confederates they said this is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and it increased them in faith and submission.
You did not throw when you threw: human effort plus divine facilitation.
You did not kill them, Allah did; you did not throw when you threw. We act, Allah makes it land; the battle is space to prove ourselves.
Allah showed the enemy as few in the Prophet's dream; had He shown them as many, the Muslims would have lost heart.
Allah showed the enemy as few in the Prophet's dream; had He shown them many the believers would have failed and quarrelled.
Whether Allah punishes or forgives them is not your affair: the outcome is His, the effort is ours.
Not for you is the decision whether He forgives or punishes them; revealed after the Prophet cursed some after Uhud.
Believers disliked going out and argued about the truth; Allah willed to establish truth and abolish falsehood even if the criminals dislike it

Your Lord brought you out in truth while some believers were averse, arguing about the truth as if driven to death; Allah promised one of two groups and willed truth to be established even if the criminals dislike it.
The dream and each army seeing the other as few
The Prophet saw the enemy as few in his dream, and each army was made to see the other as small.
The confederates sent back in rage and the believers spared fighting
Allah turned back the confederates in their rage and spared the believers fighting; He is Strong, Almighty
Remember His favour: you were enemies and He joined your hearts so you became brothers, and saved you from the brink of the fire.
Arabic exposition: the verse every minbar opens with, revealed after Uhud to rebuild the individual and then the nation.
Do not drive away the poor believers to please the nobles
Bani Isra'il cursed on the tongues of Dawud and Isa because they did not forbid one another the wrong they did.
Remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram after leaving Arafah
The day of the greater Hajj
Believers are brothers, so their property is protected
The sermon's wording on separation in beds echoes this verse
Allah knows the stealing glance and what hearts conceal
Rabbaniyyun as a Quranic term for scholars to sit with
Another verse addressing what the Prophet held within himself and his concern about what people would say.
Pharaoh demanded gold bracelets or angels as proof from Musa, the same irrelevant demand the Makkans made.
Used to explain that 'naqdira' means to restrict provision.
The Quran told the Prophet to consult his companions, changing the Arabs' value of one-man rule.
Do not drive away those who call on their Lord morning and evening; Allah knows best who is grateful. Used against compromising the message to please the elite.
O you wrapped up, stand at night and recite slowly, for We will cast upon you a heavy word: night prayer and recitation are what make the burden carriable.
A people He loves and who love Him
Believers are stronger in love for Allah than idolaters for their idols
Eight beloved things must not outrank Allah, His Messenger and striving for Him
If you love Allah follow me and Allah will love you
Be patient for the decree of your Lord, for you are in Our eyes
After Uhud: do not weaken or grieve, you are uppermost if you believe
Your Lord has not forsaken you, and He will give you until you are content
Abu Sufyan repeats the brothers' admission that Allah preferred Yusuf over them
The Prophet's expected answer: no blame on you today
The mistake of saying 'we hear and disobey' and twisting words toward teachers.
Exception for polytheists who never broke their treaty: honour it to its term.
The Romans, defeated, will win within a few years and the believers will rejoice.
The cow of Bani Israil: any cow would have worked; they made it hard on themselves. Used to argue that room in practice is by design.
Remembering Allah at the Mash'ar al-Haram on leaving Arafah; cited to locate the boundary where the Hums used to stop.
His early warning of a severe punishment from Safa.
The three believers who stayed behind from Tabuk without excuse.
The command revealed after the Prophet prayed over Ibn Ubayy
Judge by the truth and do not argue for the traitors, revealed to clear the framed Jewish man
Those who plot by night what Allah does not approve
Musa throws the tablets and seizes his brother without being rebuked
Allah tells the Prophet that he will die and so will his opponents, as comfort.
Death will find you wherever you are, even in lofty towers.
The recurring phrase 'no fear upon them, nor will they grieve' shows that fear and sadness are distinct words.
None knows the forces of your Lord but Him
The prostration that sparked the rumour that Quraysh had accepted Islam
No human before the Prophet was granted immortality
Do not say of those killed in Allah's way that they are dead
No compulsion in religion: the Quran sets no penalty for apostasy.
The Prophet recited to Utbah up to the verse of prostration and prostrated
Allah brought them out for the truth while some believers disputed it as though driven to death: Badr was about haqq.
Yusuf's brothers' admission and his reply, 'no blame on you today'
Allah answered the Muslims' call at Badr with a thousand angels in succession.
The same statement repeated in Aal-Imran, which he returns to later to connect the Badr verses to Uhud.
The nearer and farther banks and the caravan below; had you arranged the meeting you would have failed, but Allah set it up so His decree would be carried out.
Each army was made to look fewer in the other's eyes so Allah's decree would be fulfilled; all matters return to Allah.
He paraphrases 'the ayah' about your capacity: run at full capacity; that is all that is asked. Could equally be 64:16.
Had you spent all the wealth on earth you could not have united their hearts, but Allah united them, even though uniting hearts was the Prophet's life work.
Explains the word aqabah as the steep obstacle: freeing a slave and feeding the hungry on a day of hunger; can you stand your ground when the obstacle appears?
The surah opens with the believers' dispute over spoils, a second lapse the Quran asks later Muslims to reflect on
To Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and earth
He grants victory to whom He wills; He is the Almighty
'O Musa, I am Allah, the Almighty, the Wise'
Allah raised Isa to Himself; Allah is Almighty, Wise
Isa questioned about his worship: 'if You forgive them, You are the Almighty, the Wise'
Musa arriving at the water of Madyan after fleeing Egypt, one of the prophets' migrations
Ibrahim's words 'I am migrating to my Lord', one of the prophets whose hijrah set the pattern
Hasten to forgiveness from your Lord.
You used to wish for death before you met it; now you have seen it.
Muhammad is only a messenger; no soul dies but by Allah's leave; whoever wants this world or the next is given of it.
The command to warn his closest kin, which prompted the Prophet's first public sermon.
He created death and life to test who is best in deed; He is the Almighty, the Forgiving
The hypocrites and the diseased of heart said Allah and His Messenger promised only delusion.
A group asked leave saying their homes were exposed when they were not; they only wished to flee.
You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help: a claim repeated 17 times a day that life will force you to prove.
Among the believers are men true to their covenant with Allah; some died, some still wait, and they changed nothing of what they agreed.
Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah's verdict under Abu Jahl's pressure: this is nothing but magic handed down, nothing but the word of a human.
Had the city been entered from all sides and they been asked to turn, the hypocrites would have done so almost at once.
Even if the Prophet sought forgiveness seventy times for the hypocrites, Allah would not forgive them.
The first five verses Jibril recited on the night of the first revelation.
Just as your Lord brought you out of your home with the truth while a party of believers was unwilling: the opening simile ties this lesson to the earlier one on wealth.
They argued with you about the truth after it was clear, as if being driven to death: the reluctance was fear of battle, not love of money.
Allah promised one of the two parties and they wished for the unarmed one, but He willed to establish the truth; haqq recurs six times in these verses.
Creation is founded on truth and admitting falsehood into it ruins it. Paraphrase only; the verse could also be one of the 'created with truth' verses.
The parallel passage also called the ten commandments of the Quran.
The believers spend from what We provide them: take what Allah gives and transform it into energy for His cause.
Allah bought the believers' lives and wealth in exchange for Jannah, so we are obligated to offer everything.

hadith.gist: On the Night Journey the Prophet tied the Buraq at the door of the mosque in Jerusalem
The leaders of Quraysh offered to accept Islam on condition that they not sit with the slaves and weak believers; the Prophet refused.

Ka'b ibn Malik's hadith that the people of Madinah valued the night of the Bay'ah of Aqabah more than Badr, even though Badr is more celebrated, because that was when the relationship was established.

After the spoils were distributed following Hunayn the Ansar feared he would return to Makkah; the Prophet reassured them that his life and death were with them, that he was from them and they from him.
Jabir's long account of the Prophet's Hajj, narrated to Muhammad al-Baqir
The miqats of each region, then the Prophet faced the horizon and asked Allah to turn people's hearts
Asma bint Umays told to bathe, protect herself and enter ihram after giving birth
On Safa the Ansar gathered at his feet saying amin to his dua
Had I known beforehand I would not have driven the sacrifice; umrah entered Hajj forever, said to Suraqa
Ali came to complain about Fatimah leaving ihram and the Prophet said she was right
To Mu'adh: perhaps you will pass my grave; my allies are the God-fearing wherever they are
Your blood, wealth and honour are sacred like this day, month and land
All matters of jahiliyyah are under my feet; blood feuds and usury abolished, starting with my own family
Shaytan despairs of being worshipped in your land but is content with deeds you belittle
Fear Allah regarding women; you took them by Allah's trust
Your Lord is one and your father is one; no Arab over non-Arab except by taqwa
I will precede you to the Hawd; some will be driven away and I will be told you do not know what they changed after you
Allah has given each heir his share; no bequest for an heir
I have left you what will keep you from straying: the Book of Allah
Let the present convey to the absent; perhaps the one told understands better than the hearer
When dirt was thrown in his face and his daughter wept, the Prophet told her not to cry, for Allah would give her father victory.
At Badr the Prophet pleads: O Allah, if this band perishes You will not be worshipped on earth; fulfil what You promised me. Abu Bakr tells him Allah will keep His promise.

At Aqabah the Ansar told the Prophet to take for himself and his Lord whatever he wanted; he praised Allah and asked them for five things, the first being to hear and obey in what they liked and what they disliked.
Farewell Sermon, paragraph one: your blood, wealth and honour are as sacred to one another as this day, this month and this land.
hadith.source: Farewell Sermon (he notes Imam Ahmad records it being delivered at least three times)

hadith.gist: Paragraph two: everything of Jahiliyyah is under my feet; its blood claims are abolished, the first I cancel is the blood of Ibn Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith; its riba is abolished, the first I cancel is the riba of al-Abbas, you keep only your capital.
Paragraph three: Shaytan has despaired of being worshipped in your land, but he is content to be obeyed in things you consider small; so be cautious of him for your deen.

Paragraph four: time has returned to its original form as on the day Allah created the heavens and earth, with the sacred months in their places; do not return after me to striking each other's necks.
After each statement the Prophet asked 'have I conveyed?', riders carried his words through the crowd, the people affirmed, and he said 'O Allah, be witness'.
Paragraph five: fear Allah regarding women; you took them by the trust of Allah and made them lawful by His word; they have rights over you and you over them; my advice is to treat them well.
Paragraph six: O people, your Lord is one and your father is one; you are all from Adam and Adam is from dust; no Arab over non-Arab, no red over black, except by taqwa.

Paragraph seven: I am waiting for you at the basin and I will boast of your numbers before the nations; some I will try to save will be taken from me, I will say 'my companions', and be told you do not know what they changed after you; then he will say 'away with them'.
Paragraph eight: inheritance shares and lineage must be preserved; no one is cut out, no one takes more than his share, and no one claims a family that is not his.

Paragraph nine: let the one present convey to the absent; perhaps one who is told will understand it better than the one who heard it, and many will carry knowledge to people more knowledgeable than themselves.
Hind bint Utbah, at her pledge, objected 'would a free woman commit zina?'; the Prophet smiled and told her to simply give the pledge, legislating for later generations.

Final paragraph: I have left among you that which, if you hold to it, you will never go astray, the Book of Allah; you will meet your Lord and be asked about me, what will you say? They said: you conveyed, fulfilled and advised; he raised his finger to the sky, 'O Allah, be witness'.

The articles of the Aqabah pledge: to hear and obey in energy and reluctance, to spend in hardship and ease, to command good and forbid evil, and to stand for Allah without fearing the blame of any blamer.

The Prophet kept visiting the martyrs of Uhud until he died, greeting them: peace be upon you, abode of believing people; peace be upon you Hamza ibn Abdul-Muttalib, Mus'ab ibn Umayr, Anas ibn an-Nadr.
Mus'ab ibn Umayr was killed at Uhud leaving only one cloth; when it covered his head his feet showed and when it covered his feet his head showed, and the companions wept.
At the Prophet's death Abu Bakr reminded the people that Allah is alive and does not die, and recited that Muhammad is only a messenger.
Anas: the day the Prophet entered Medina everything was lit up, and the day he died everything went dark; the companions felt like strangers to one another after his burial
A bedouin urinated in the Prophet's masjid
The Prophet taught people how to spit or clear their nose in the masjid and cleaned it from the floor himself
At the first revelation Jibril embraced the Prophet tightly three times
Leaving Makkah the Prophet said it was the most beloved land to him and he would not have left had its people not driven him out
Umar questioned whether the treaty was really a victory, and later said he did good deeds for the rest of his life in repentance for how he acted that day.

Terms of the pledge: hear and obey in energy and reluctance, spend in hardship and ease, command good and forbid evil, stand for Allah fearing no one's blame, and protect the Prophet as you protect your families and wealth.
Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur: by the One who sent you with the truth, we pledge to protect you as we protect our families; we are a people of war, inherited generation from generation.

Abu al-Haytham asked whether the Prophet would leave them after victory; he replied: blood for blood, ruin for ruin; I am of you and you are of me; I make peace with whom you make peace and war with whom you war.

As'ad ibn Zurarah: slow down, people of Yathrib; taking him means the enmity of all the Arabs, the killing of your best and the bite of swords; if you can bear it, take him and your reward is with Allah; if you fear, say so now.
When they asked what they would receive for this, the Prophet answered: Paradise.
Umar tells Abbas he was happier at his Islam than he would have been at his own father's, because the Prophet loved it
Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe, whoever stays in his home is safe
Wounded at Uhud, the Prophet prays: O Allah forgive my people, for they do not know
On the Ascension Musa repeatedly sent the Prophet back to ask for fewer prayers until five remained.
Aishah asked the Prophet whether any day was harder than Uhud; he named the day of Ta'if, when he walked aimlessly until he reached Qarn al-Tha'alib
The long hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah describing the Prophet's Hajj from Medina to its end; the frame for both nights.

Before Hajj the Prophet named the places where pilgrims enter ihram, then turned to the horizon and asked Allah to bring their hearts to him as He did for Ibrahim; narrated outside Muslim with a reasonable chain.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Husayn visited the blind Jabir, who felt for his chest, welcomed him as his nephew, led the prayer in a cloth too small for his shoulders, and then told the story of the Prophet's Hajj.
Asma bint Umays gave birth at Dhul-Hulayfah and sent to ask what to do; she was told to bathe, pad herself with cloth and enter ihram.
Jabir: I looked ahead, right, left and behind and saw only people on foot and riding; the Prophet was among us, the Quran descending on him, he knew its meaning, and whatever he did we did.
The Prophet said the talbiyah in his wording; people added other wordings and he did not object to any of them.

He touched the black stone, jogged three circuits and walked four, prayed behind maqam Ibrahim after reciting the verse, returned to the stone, then went out to Safa reciting 'Safa and Marwah are among the rituals of Allah' and saying 'we begin with what Allah began with'.
A narration that on Safa, as he made takbir and dua with the companions gathered at his feet saying amin, tears ran down his face.

At Marwah he said: had I known beforehand what I know now I would not have brought the sacrificial animals and would have made it an Umrah; whoever has no animal should exit ihram and make it an Umrah.
Suraqah ibn Malik asked whether this applied to that year only or forever; the Prophet interlaced his fingers and said Umrah has entered into Hajj forever and ever.

Ali returned from Yemen with the animals, found Fatima out of ihram in dyed clothes and kohl, and complained to the Prophet, who said she was right and asked Ali what intention he had made; since Ali had tied it to the Prophet's, he was to stay in ihram.
'Take your rituals from me', cited alongside the fact that he allowed two groups to do different things.

On the 8th they went to Mina and he prayed there; on the 9th, after sunrise, he ordered a tent at Namirah and rode on; Quraysh were sure he would stop at the Mash'ar al-Haram as they did in Jahiliyyah, but he passed on to Arafah.

A Jew said to Umar that if the verse of completion had come to them they would have made its day a festival; Umar said he knew the day and place it was revealed: on Arafah, a Friday, with the Prophet.
The sermon's opening: O people, listen and understand, for I do not know whether I will meet you after this year in this place.

Sending Mu'adh to Yemen, the Prophet said he might pass by his masjid and grave on return; Mu'adh wept, and the Prophet reassured him that those nearest to him are the pious whoever and wherever they are.

What day is this? What month? What land? asked three times each until they thought he would rename them; then: your blood, wealth and honour are as sacred to one another as this day, month and land, until you meet your Lord.
No father may transgress against his son nor son against his father; no one's wealth is lawful to another except what he gives with a glad heart.
Have I conveyed? The riders repeated his words and the people affirmed; he said, O Allah, be my witness.

A Companion would stand in tears on the last night of Ramadan calling out: which of us was accepted so we may congratulate him, and which was rejected so we may console him; good for you who were accepted, and may Allah make up the loss of the one rejected. The report is attributed to Ali ibn Abi Talib and, in this fuller wording, to Ibn Mas'ud.
Jabir's long description of the Prophet's farewell Hajj, narrated to Muhammad al-Baqir.
I stood here, but all of Arafah is a place of standing.
Umar told a man of another faith exactly when and where the verse of the completed religion was revealed.
O people, listen, for I may not meet you after this year in this place.

While building the masjid the companions chanted that sitting while the Prophet works would be misguided, and the Prophet chanted that there is no life but the life of the Hereafter, so forgive the Ansar and Muhajirun.

Ali recited a rhyme about those who build masjids standing and sitting and one who turns away from the dust; Ammar repeated it, Uthman took it as aimed at him and threatened Ammar, and the Prophet said Ammar is the skin between his eyes and nose.
During the quarrel at the well the Prophet condemned the calls of jahiliyyah: leave it, for it is rotten
Zayd ibn Arqam reported Ibn Ubayy's words and was later vindicated
The Prophet refused to have Ibn Ubayy killed so people would not say Muhammad kills his companions
Umar said revelation agreed with him on three matters, including not praying over the hypocrites
Before revelation the Prophet would seclude himself in the cave of Hira for a number of nights at a time, with Khadijah bringing him provisions.
Jibril first appeared to the Prophet filling the horizon between sky and earth.
At the pledge with the people of Yathrib the Prophet set conditions; the second was to spend their wealth in ease and hardship.
If Fatimah the daughter of Muhammad stole, I would apply the punishment
Perhaps Allah looked at the people of Badr and said: do as you wish, I have forgiven you
In Ramadan the doors of heaven are opened, the doors of Jahannam closed and the devils removed, and a night better than a lifetime is granted.
The best of the companions are those who were at Badr, and the Prophet said the best of the angels were those who helped at Badr.
Abu Bakr kept moving around the Prophet on the road, explaining that he feared an ambush from every side and that his own death mattered less.
During Tabuk the Prophet said there were people in Madinah who shared every valley crossed because only a valid excuse held them back.
A poor companion offered his honour in charity by forgiving all who had wronged him, and the Prophet announced that Allah had accepted it.
The Prophet secluded himself in the cave of Hira for long periods, with provisions brought to him, until revelation came.
The Prophet observed i'tikaf in the masjid behind a screen near his door.
Al-Hubab asked whether the camp site was revelation or strategy, and the Prophet adopted his plan.
It is not fitting for a prophet who has put on his armour to remove it before fighting.
Perhaps Allah looked at the people of Badr and said: do as you will, I have forgiven you.
I asked permission to seek forgiveness for my mother and was not granted it; visit graves, for they remind you of death.
No one did me a favour except that I repaid it, except Abu Bakr; his reward is with Allah.
Close every door into the masjid except the door of Abu Bakr.
If I were to take a khalil I would take Abu Bakr.
Blood for blood, destruction for destruction: I am of you and you are of me (to the Ansar).
Whoever meets Abu al-Bakhtari, do not kill him.
Do not wish to meet the enemy; ask Allah for wellbeing, and if you meet them, stand firm.
When the Prophet called for funds before Tabuk, one companion gave so much that the Prophet said nothing he did after that day could harm him.
The angels kept shading Abdullah ibn Amr with their wings until he was carried away
Allah spoke to Jabir's father face to face and asked him to wish; he asked to return and be killed again, Allah said none return, and the verse 'do not think those killed are dead' was revealed
After Uhud the Prophet called: whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, come out with me, and only those who were at Uhud may come
Ibn Abbas: 'Allah is sufficient for us and the best disposer of affairs' was said by Ibrahim when thrown into the fire and by Muhammad's companions when told people had gathered against them
Whoever changes his religion, read alongside narrations about leaving the community and fighting it.
A man asked the Prophet for money; he had him sell his household items, feed his family with half and buy an axe head with the rest, then cut and sell wood for a week
At Hudaybiyyah the companions hesitated to shave and sacrifice until Umm Salamah advised the Prophet to do it first
Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam has its reward and the reward of everyone who follows it afterward.

The seventy Qurra worked their trades by day, prayed most of the night, taught one another Quran, gave dawah and taught the poor of Suffah trades; when they were killed the Prophet prayed against their killers for a month until the Quran told him to stop.
Umm Kulthum emigrated after Hudaybiyyah and the Prophet refused to return her since the treaty did not cover women
Abu Basir, sent back under the treaty, formed a band on the coast that harassed Quraysh until they dropped the clause
The Prophet foretold that the treasures of Kisra would come into the Muslims' hands, while people laughed at the idea.
At Hunayn he threw sand at the enemy and declared: I am the Prophet, no lie, I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib.
He walked among the mocking leaders of Quraysh at the Kaaba and warned them, and they feared him.
Ubayy ibn Khalaf said he fed his horse to kill the Prophet, who replied he would kill Ubayy instead.
Anas: the Prophet was the best, most generous and bravest of people; he rode out ahead of everyone on a bareback horse when Madinah was alarmed at night.
At the conquest of Makkah the Prophet told the Quraysh to go, for they were free
Asked whether any day was harder than Uhud, the Prophet named the day he returned from Ta'if walking without direction
The dua of Ta'if: to You I complain of my weakness, my lack of means and my lowliness before people

On the day of the conquest Sa'd ibn Ubadah declared it a day of slaughter; the Prophet took the banner from him, declared it the day of mercy in which Allah honours Quraysh and the Kaaba, and handed the banner to Sa'd's son.

At the Bay'ah of Aqabah Shaytan screamed to the people of the tents that Muhammad and those who left their religion with him had gathered to fight them; the Prophet named him the enemy of Allah and promised to deal with him.
hadith.source: Musnad Ahmad; also in the seerah

hadith.gist: Jabir's long description of the Prophet's Farewell Hajj.
Let the present convey to the absent, for the one informed may understand better than the hearer.
You will be asked about me, so what will you say? They said you conveyed and fulfilled; he said, O Allah, bear witness.
Everything of jahiliyyah is under my feet; the blood and riba of my own family are abolished first.
Thumamah ibn Uthal was captured and tied to a pillar of the masjid; each day the Prophet asked him how he was; on the third he released him, and Thumamah bathed and returned to accept Islam.
Aisha asked if he had a day worse than Uhud; he named the day of Ta'if, when he walked on not knowing where he was going
Leaving Mecca, the Prophet said it was the most beloved land of Allah to him and he would not have left had its people not driven him out
The Farewell Sermon: 'Listen to me, for I may not meet you after this year in this place.'
The Prophet told Mu'adh when sending him to Yemen that he might return to find only his mosque and grave, and told him not to cry.
Your blood, wealth and honour are as sacred as this day, this month and this land.
All matters of jahiliyyah are under my feet; the first blood I abolish is Rabi'ah's, the first riba that of Abbas.
Shaytan has despaired of being worshipped in this land but is content with lesser sins.
No one with an atom's weight of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise.
Do not return after me as disbelievers striking each other's necks.
Fear Allah regarding women; I enjoin you to treat them well.
Abu Dharr insulted a man for his black mother and the Prophet told him he still had jahiliyyah in him.
Your Lord is one and your father is one; no Arab has superiority over a non-Arab except by taqwa.
I will be waiting for you at the Basin.
Let the present convey to the absent, for perhaps the one informed understands better than the one who heard.
You will be asked about me, so what will you say? They said: you conveyed and advised; he said, O Allah, bear witness.

Ja'far ibn Abi Talib's address to the Negus: we were a people of jahiliyyah who worshipped idols, ate carrion, were bad neighbours, severed kinship and let the strong devour the weak; a man of known lineage and integrity commanded us to worship Allah alone, speak truthfully, keep trusts, honour neighbours and kin, and forbade oppression, consuming orphans' wealth and false testimony.
The Prophet told some new converts from distant tribes to go home until they heard he had prevailed, since he could not yet protect them.
Take your rites from me.
Asked about rites done out of order, he said do it, there is no harm.
To the Ansar: I live with you and die with you.
I am only human; soon the messenger of my Lord will come and I will answer.
Zayd chose to stay with the Prophet rather than return with his father and uncle, and the Prophet declared him his son at the Ka'bah

Shaybah ibn Uthman's account of his Islam at Hunayn: the Prophet wiped his chest, prayed for his protection from Shaytan and told him Allah's intent for him was better than his own, then repeated it after the battle with a call to seek forgiveness.
The Prophet recited An-Nahl 90-91 to Uthman ibn Maz'un, who said that was the moment faith settled in his heart; he had accepted Islam earlier only out of shyness before the Prophet.

Allah commanded the Prophet to present himself to the tribes; he went to Banu Shayban, and when their leader Mafruq ibn Amr asked what he called to, he recited 16:90, and Mafruq said he was calling to noble character and good deeds and that those who denied him had wronged themselves.
The Prophet to Makkah: you are the most beloved land to me, and had your people not driven me out I would never have left
On the way back from Uhud the Prophet invoked curses on certain enemies by name and 3:128 was revealed.

When commanded to warn his family, the Prophet praised and exalted Allah, then said that one responsible for others does not lie to them and that he was warning them of a severe punishment; he called each tribe to save itself from the fire because he could not do it for them, and told Fatima she could ask for any of his wealth but he could not save her from the fire.

Hadith qudsi: My servant keeps drawing near to Me with extra acts of worship until I love him; when I love him he sees, hears and moves through Me, and if he asks Me I give him and if he seeks refuge in Me I grant it.
The day the Prophet entered Madinah everything lit up, and the day he died everything went dark; the companions felt like strangers to one another.

At Bi'r Ma'unah Haram ibn Milhan was speared from behind while explaining Islam to the chief and cried that he had won, by the Lord of the Kaaba; the Prophet mourned the group and prayed against their killers for a month until revelation stopped him; the killer later came to Madinah to ask what he had won and accepted Islam.
hadith.source: pieced together from the seerah and the books of hadith

hadith.gist: Sadaqah is a proof
Hadith qudsi: if all creation asked and were given everything, it would diminish Allah's dominion no more than a needle dipped in the ocean
Refusing to execute Ibn Ubayy so people would not say Muhammad kills his companions
Asked which day was the hardest of his life, the Prophet said it was not Uhud but the day he was driven out of Taif, stoned until his feet bled, and found he had been banned from Makkah too.

Jibril came with the angel of the mountains offering to crush the two mountains on the people of Makkah; the Prophet refused and hoped that from their progeny would come people who worship Allah alone.

The Prophet always concealed the destination of his expeditions and would hint at another direction, positioning the army one way and scouting another, except for Tabuk, which he named openly because of the distance and the season.
At the second pledge of Aqabah the Prophet named five things he required: allegiance, wealth in ease and hardship, enjoining good and reform, standing firm in battle, and protecting him.
At Hunayn, when the Muslims fled, the Prophet had al-Abbas call out to those who had pledged allegiance to him, and they returned.
In his first years in Madinah the Prophet built the masjid, joined emigrants and Ansar in brotherhood, and had all parties sign the Constitution of Madinah.
Walid, after hearing the Prophet, said the Quran was like a tree with fruitful top and deep roots, superior to all speech, and not poetry, sorcery or soothsaying.
Ka'b ibn Malik's long account of staying back from Tabuk, his confession, the boycott and the acceptance of his repentance
When someone criticised Ka'b on the march, a companion replied that they knew only good of him
Tufayl ibn Amr of Daws put cotton in his ears, then chose to listen to the Prophet and accepted Islam.
Dimad came to treat the Prophet, heard his sermon opening, asked him to repeat it and accepted Islam.
Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt twisted a garment around the Prophet's neck while he prayed.
The entrails of a camel were placed on the Prophet's back in prostration until Fatimah removed them.
On the way to Badr he refused to ride more than his share, saying his partners were not stronger than him nor was he less in need of reward.
He insisted on paying Abu Bakr for his camel at the Hijrah.
He refused to kill Ibn Ubayy so people would not say Muhammad kills his companions.
I was made to fear for Allah when no one else feared, and harmed when no one else was harmed; thirty days passed with nothing for me and Bilal to eat except what Bilal hid under his arm.

At the Trench the Prophet divided about 1,500 men into groups of 25 under leaders, told each group to defend what it dug, and inspected every group daily so the trench was complete before the confederates arrived.
Abu Shahm misbehaved toward a young woman the night before his tribe's bay'ah; the next morning the Prophet pulled his hand back from him, and he swore never to do it again.

Before Mu'tah the Prophet told the army to wait outside Madinah; a companion stayed to pray Jumuah with him instead and was told nothing on earth could make up for what he lost; he resolved only martyrdom could and died a martyr.
Khadijah reassured him that Allah would never disgrace him because he kept family ties, carried the weak and helped those struck by hardship.
When the Prophet sought a loan to keep giving, Umar objected; an Ansari said 'give and fear no poverty from the Lord of the Throne' and the Prophet smiled.
He saw Jibril in his true created form twice: on the first night and on the night of the Mi'raj.
Jibril told him to read; he said he could not read; Jibril pressed him three times before reciting the first verses.
Companions showed the Prophet the stones tied to their stomachs and he showed he had tied two
The Prophet sent leaders to confirm Banu Qurayzah's betrayal and asked them to report bad news in code
During the siege the Prophet slept briefly and was startled awake by a companion asking if he needed anything
Jabir's small meal of barley and meat fed all the diggers of the trench
O people, listen to my words, for I do not know if I will meet you after this year in this place again.
What day, month and land is this? Your blood, wealth and honour are sacred to one another like the sanctity of this day, month and land. Have I conveyed? O Allah, bear witness.

In the midst of the companions' fear and suffering, as at the digging of the Trench, the Prophet told them the day would come when they would bring back the treasures of Kisra, enter the gates of al-Mada'in and take the castles of the Romans, when some could not even relieve themselves safely.
The two Sa'ds asked whether giving dates to Ghatafan was a command from Allah or his own plan, then refused
Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud accepted Islam secretly during the siege and was told war is deception
From now on we go to them and they will not come to us
Jibril told the Prophet the angels had not laid down their arms and to march on Banu Qurayzah
I was given victory through fear cast into my enemies a month's distance away
While breaking the rock in the trench the Prophet saw the conquest of Persia and Rome

Afif al-Kindi, trading with Al-Abbas at the Kaaba, saw a man, a woman and a boy praying, was told it was Muhammad with Khadijah and Ali reviving the religion of Ibrahim, and after accepting Islam later wept that he could have been among the very first Muslims had he spoken to him that day.
At the second pledge of Aqabah one article was to spend in hardship and in ease, whether you have much or little, and the only promised return was Jannah.

maxims: Islam is an umbrella for life, not a category
Anything less than your whole life is real shortcoming
No one devotes himself to someone he does not love
Love is the first and last driver of this deen
Every decision is to get you across the finishing line
Allah initiated the conversation; you speak back
No one nails it every time and no one fails every time
What is not going well could always go worse
Brush off, get up and keep going
If the work stops when a man dies, what was the point?
Nothing is forever, especially not us
Ramadan is a launching pad

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Muddaththir, Part 6: Verses 42-56

spans.note: Two consecutive corrections show the real cause of turning away is not truly believing in accountability, and it applies to everyone.
He asks for a 100% honest yes on accountability and shows that the Arabs' core denial was resurrection, not God.
A claim to believe in judgment is empty unless one's choices show the fear of being asked.

lectures.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Goals and Accountability

spans.note: Trying hard is not enough; individuals, communities and the ummah must know the outcomes they are working toward, and he thinks the ummah has never defined them.
Sounds the alarm that the community has no defined goals and so nothing to be held to; proposes education, mentorship, outreach, financial centralization and advocacy as the objectives.

lectures.title: Listening to the Divine: An-Naml 82-93

spans.note: The question 'or what were you doing?' demands an account of a lifetime: what you spent your time on, what you learned, what conclusions you drew.
He imagines being handed his own book and told it has no plot and no beginning or end; the deniers fall silent because there is no answer.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Accountability

spans.note: The fifth communal commitment: hold yourself to a standard before Allah holds you to one, and build mutual accountability between masajid and their communities, negative and positive, because people without consequences inevitably deviate.
The Prophet gave no free passes, from the Trench to Abu Shahm and the companion who stayed for Jumuah; masajid must be transparent and members must not act like consumers.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surah Saba, Session 6 (34:25-33)

spans.note: Followers and leaders blame each other, but each answers alone for his own choices.

lectures.title: Surah Summaries: Al-Mutaffifin and Al-Inshiqaq

spans.note: Every choice is recorded in a numbered book; a short life is easy to document.

lectures.title: Surah Summaries: Surat At-Takwir and Al-Infitar

spans.note: Deen at root means accountability; people avoid it, yet every choice will be brought back.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Waqi'ah, Part 3: Verses 41-56

spans.note: Belief in resurrection means accountability shaping every decision; belief without conduct is hollow.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Fussilat, Part 3 (41:15-22)

spans.note: One's own senses testify on the Day, and everything is already recorded within.

lectures.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Ra'd, Part 3

spans.note: Angels preserve every deed so that, faced with the record, people accept the verdict and judge themselves.

lectures.title: Stages of the Hereafter: Receiving the Records (Day 20)

spans.note: Receiving the records, reading and judging oneself, with every thought and joke recorded.

lectures.title: Understanding Islam: Securing the Formula

spans.note: Without the conviction that we will be questioned, Islam and Iman are not worth investing in; Muslims should be the people who accept this most.

lectures.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Saffat, Part 3: Verses 28-50

spans.note: Followers cannot blame their leaders; both share the punishment.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 28: Accountability

spans.note: Being questioned about how we used our freedom is the real concern of the afterlife, and living with that concern is the way to be spared it.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ma'arij, Part 3: Verses 26-44

spans.note: Belief in the Day is proven by behaviour; you will defend every choice in the book you authored.

lectures.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Defining the Metrics

spans.note: Muslims must know what Islam is meant to achieve in this world and have metrics to judge whether they are succeeding; otherwise after a lifetime as a Muslim one has nothing to show.

lectures.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Goals and Accountability (Part 2)

spans.note: Allah judges effort, but effort toward the goals He set. 'I tried my best' without an object is a dodge; Muslims individually, institutionally and as an ummah do not know what they are trying to achieve, and that makes their best insufficient.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Muddaththir, Part 5: Verses 32-41

spans.note: Accountability is the third pillar of carrying Islam: each soul is held by its deeds and must own its choices, and no one else can care for you.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqa: Mortality, Episode 30

spans.note: Accountability before Allah gives morality its basis; at death the book is sealed and fate is fixed.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Mortality, Episode 31

spans.note: Conditions for accountability to work and why morality depends on it.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2026 Night 19: Difficult Questions

spans.note: The Quran gives us the questions of the Day of Judgment in advance; the hardest is how we spent our lives, and only lived answers will hold.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2026 Night 29 - Quranic Themes: Outcomes

spans.note: Every choice has an outcome you own; the worst and best of creation are defined by choices made against relentless time.

lectures.title: English Tafseer: Surat Al-Infitar 1-19

spans.note: Every choice is recorded by noble scribes, so claims about our deeds cannot be self-serving.

lectures.title: Listening to the Divine: An-Nur 54-57

spans.note: Beyond the shared individual duties there are communal obligations that depend on your circumstances; know exactly what you are required to do and put your shoulder under it.
Judgment is individual and private because each person is accountable for the hand he was dealt; a Sudanese mother and a Canadian professional will not face the same questions.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Kahf, Session 6: The Owner of the Two Gardens

spans.note: Doubting accountability is what lets people hoard wealth; hedging faith is self-deception.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Kahf, Session 10: The Book That Leaves Nothing Out and Iblis's Entitlement (18:49-51)

spans.note: Every blessing, including wealth no longer held, will be asked about.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 10 (33:26-31)

spans.note: Greater status brings greater reward and greater punishment, for the wives and for those born Muslim.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 19: Those Who Spread Fear, the Hour, and Blaming Our Leaders (33:60-69)

spans.note: Blaming leaders is no excuse; obedience belongs to Allah alone and no one will carry you.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Saba, Session 8: Wealth Is Not Proof of Allah's Love

spans.note: Followers carry their own choices and cannot plead ignorance or lies they chose to believe.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Saba, Session 9: The Angels Questioned and the Three Rejections

spans.note: Each person owns and answers for his choices; followers cannot blame leaders.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Saba, Session 10: The Five Narratives Muslims Carry

spans.note: Each person carries his own choices on the Day of Judgment.

Near the end of his life the Prophet said from the minbar that anyone he had struck or wronged could take their right from him, as he wished to meet Allah owing no one.
You will be asked about me, so what will you say? They said: you conveyed and advised; he said, O Allah, bear witness.
When the verse about being held to what is in the self was revealed, the companions were alarmed, and the Prophet reassured them and told them to hear and obey.
Shall I not tell you of a night better than Laylat al-Qadr? A guard keeping watch in a land of danger who may not return to his family.
The Prophet sought refuge in Allah from a sudden death.
Deeds are judged by their endings.
A man who killed ninety-nine, then a hundred, was told he could repent and must leave his land; he died on the way and the angels of mercy took him.
The Prophet's basin is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, scented with musk, its cups like stars; whoever drinks never thirsts again
Some are driven from the basin and the Prophet is told: you do not know what they changed after you
People cross the bridge over Hell at different speeds, like a blink, lightning, wind or horses, with hooks snatching some
The Prophet prostrates under the Throne and is told: raise your head, ask and you will be given, intercede and it will be accepted
Allah made a hundred mercies, sent one to the world and will add it to the ninety-nine on the Day of Judgment
Allah conceals the believer while reviewing his sins and forgives them
No one's feet move on that day until asked about his life, youth, wealth and knowledge
Allah tells the people of Paradise He bestows His pleasure on them and will never be displeased with them
The Prophet sought repentance from Allah a hundred times a day
On reciting 'what deceived you about your generous Lord', the Prophet said his ignorance deceived him; he notes it lacks some authenticity.
A man is shown ninety-nine scrolls of his deeds and asked whether the recorders wronged him; he admits they are accurate.
A person may say a word that pleases or displeases Allah without thinking much of it.
Allah says He will not combine for His servant two fears or two securities: whoever fears Him in this world is safe on the Day of Gathering, and whoever feels safe now will fear then.
Hold yourselves to account before you are held to account, and weigh your deeds before they are weighed for you (the saying usually attributed to Umar ibn al-Khattab).

At the Trench the Prophet divided about 1,500 men into groups of 25 under leaders, told each group to defend what it dug, and inspected every group daily so the trench was complete before the confederates arrived.
Abu Shahm misbehaved toward a young woman the night before his tribe's bay'ah; the next morning the Prophet pulled his hand back from him, and he swore never to do it again.

Before Mu'tah the Prophet told the army to wait outside Madinah; a companion stayed to pray Jumuah with him instead and was told nothing on earth could make up for what he lost; he resolved only martyrdom could and died a martyr.
