hadith.gist: After Ta'if, Jibril came with the angel of the mountains, who offered to crush the two mountains on Quraysh; the Prophet said he hoped Allah would bring from their descendants people who worship Allah alone.

When the Prophet called for charity Umar brought half his wealth, thinking he would surpass Abu Bakr; Abu Bakr brought everything and said he left his family Allah and His Messenger, and Umar knew he would never outdo him.
The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim; he does not wrong him or forsake him
Whoever supports a wronged Muslim, Allah will support him when he needs it; whoever forsakes him, Allah will forsake him when he needs support
Take from this world only the provision of a traveller.
Khabbab complained of persecution; the Prophet said believers before were sawn in half without leaving their faith, Allah will complete this matter, but you are hasty
When the Prophet appealed for funds, those with nothing brought a date and hypocrites laughed at them.
A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim; he does not let him down or turn his back on him.
Support your brother whether he is oppressor or oppressed; you support the oppressor by stopping him.
For Allah to guide one person through you is better for you than everything in the world.
Reading Surat al-Kahf every Friday is a sunnah.

When Quraysh asked through Abu Talib that he tone down his message, the Prophet said he could no more abandon it than they could light a flame from the sun, and Abu Talib pledged to keep supporting him.
The Prophet spoke of a time when the only way for a Muslim to survive would be to take his sheep and flee to the mountains; the sheikh says that time is not now, not even close.

In the midst of the companions' fear and suffering, as at the digging of the Trench, the Prophet told them the day would come when they would bring back the treasures of Kisra, enter the gates of al-Mada'in and take the castles of the Romans, when some could not even relieve themselves safely.
Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a smiling face.

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self

Restraining desire and ending the self's dictatorship.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions

lectures.title: My Maxims, Part 1: Communal Obligation, the Ummah as the Goal, Following Your Local Imam

spans.note: Institutions are vehicles for serving the community; when preserving the institution matters more than serving people, that is corruption and the vehicle should be dismantled. Islam is the only real institution.
Sub-groups inside Islam need a narrow, stated goal and must not act as substitutes for Islam (the group-within-a-group phenomenon); doing everything is elitism.

Leadership only works when people are willing to be led. Congregants who follow a YouTube or pocket sheikh against the local imam's vision are a severe hindrance; he never agreed fully with any of his teachers but kept working with them.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Jumuah, Part 1: Verse 1

spans.note: Jumuah was neutralized when the minbar went to hired or censored voices; the actual leader, or a scholar who truly advises him, should speak, and imams must be accountable.
The four names map onto a good leader's traits: ownership, a higher purpose, strength and wisdom; good intentions without wisdom run people into a wall.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Jumuah 62:9-11 (Part 4)

spans.note: Jumuah as an embedded leadership system, neutralized when the khatib is an employee with no vision.
Followship: being willing to be led, giving feedback and holding leaders accountable. Western masjids have the autonomy to do it.

lectures.title: Seeking Knowledge: Becoming Imams

spans.note: Allah made Ibrahim an imam: one who leads by example and paves the way regardless of who follows.
Imamate, for men and women alike, is sound judgment plus knowledge, and it must be built through mentorship that lets young people make decisions.

lectures.title: From Populations to Communities: Religious Centralization

spans.note: Religious leadership as the indispensable centralization: scholars as the social leadership and check on rulers, Jumuah as a God-installed leadership system, and councils of imams as protective institutions.
Imam means leader; regimes neutralize the imamate because they understand its power, and Muslims must coordinate humbly around their religious references.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat al-Kahf, Session 18: Dhul-Qarnayn Builds the Barrier

spans.note: Power exists to give others what they lack, not to take from them.

Allah's promise to believers who do good: stewardship on earth, establishment of the deen He approved, and security after fear, if they worship Him without shirk.

The eight recipients of zakat, including those who collect it and those whose hearts are to be reconciled.

Allah's word that He will fill Hell with jinn and people.

hardened hearts and Allah reviving the earth after its death

Shaytan's first success: he offered Adam the tree of eternity and kingship and swore to be a sincere adviser (also 7:20-21).
Thamud who carved out the rock: the same root as ijabah, used to show dua as hollowing the heart for Allah.

The Prophet would tell Bilal to give them rest through the prayer.
Fasting three days of every lunar month, best on the 13th, 14th and 15th.

Abdullah ibn ash-Shikhkhir found the Prophet praying with a sound in his chest like a boiling pot from weeping

The Prophet recited As-Sajdah in Fajr on Friday

lectures.title: Stages of the Hereafter: The Viewing of the Hellfire

lectures.title: Stages of the Hereafter: The Outcome of Punishment

spans.note: Fear of the Fire is a serious warning meant to change decisions, balanced by the coming talk on Jannah.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Haqqah Summary

spans.note: Hope and fear are motives that make obedience easier.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Qalam, Part 6: Verses 48-52

spans.note: Never decide people are beyond hope; the Prophet kept hoping for Quraysh, Umar and Abu Sufyan.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Haqqah Part 2: Verses 8-16

spans.note: Fear of Allah is fear of receiving exact justice, rooted in love, not fear of oppression.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Pearls 4: Four Daily Focuses

spans.note: Good assumption of Allah balanced by concern that any deed may be rejected.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Pearls 5: Deriving Self-Value

spans.note: Love, hope and fear as the healthy motivations, with feelings attached to deeds rather than to self-worth.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Pearls 19: Love

spans.note: Fear and hope of reward work as quick fixes, but not as the long-term engine of faith.

lectures.title: Night 27: Short Reminder and Tawahhum Exercise

spans.note: The hundred mercies and Allah's pleasure set against the terror of His wrath; the choice is still open.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ma'arij, Part 3: Verses 26-44

spans.note: Never feel safe from punishment; the companions' lifelong fear was healthy, motivating pressure.

lectures.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Ar-Rum (30:48-57)

spans.note: Despair, delight and ingratitude versus the believer's steady optimism and patience.

lectures.title: The Quran's Outcomes for Character: Greed, Desperation and Entitlement

spans.note: Desperation is the reflex of losing all hope the moment life withholds what you wanted; the Quran reserves despair of Allah's mercy for the misguided. The substitute is perseverance with hope, the exception named in Surah Hud.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqa: Mortality, Episode 24

spans.note: A healthy fear of accountability replaces the paralysing fear of nothingness.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqa: Mortality, Episode 26 (Q&A)

spans.note: Deeds never suffice; hold hope in mercy and fear of shortcomings, with healthy anxiety.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Insan, Part 1: Verses 1-4

spans.note: Reward and punishment always come together; with a logical reason, a reward and a consequence, the choice is easy.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Mortality, Episode 31

spans.note: Allah's love softens accountability but must not become an excuse for neglect.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Yasin, Part 1 (1-12)

spans.note: Allah revives dead hearts, so never lose hope; yet the shackles verses should bring some fear.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2026 Night 26 - Quranic Themes: Having Khushoo

spans.note: 57:17 is his most hopeful verse: the One who revives dead earth can revive any heart.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat An-Nazi'at, Part 2: Verses 15-33

spans.note: Khashyah combines respect, love and fear; with Allah we fear only getting what we deserve rather than His generosity.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat An-Nazi'at, Part 2 (79:15-33)

spans.note: Khashyah blends fear of just punishment, respect and love.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Value #38

spans.note: Relying on deeds breeds despair after sin; rely on Allah's mercy and act from fear, hope and love.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah #41: Self-Value Recap and the Essence of Vanity

spans.note: The companions feared their endings and whether their deeds were accepted.

lectures.title: Essentials and Pet Peeves: Acceptance of Deeds

spans.note: A believer must keep a measure of fear that his deeds may not be accepted, while hoping one deed saves him.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 7 (33:18-20)

spans.note: Deeds can be voided, so believers stay humble and anxious for acceptance.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 15: Witness, Bearer of Good News and a Radiant Lamp (33:45-48)

spans.note: Good news precedes warning; the stark contrast of Paradise and Hell makes the choice clear.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surah Fatir, Session 2 (35:3-7)

spans.note: Do not let anyone present Allah as only forgiving or only punishing.

lectures.title: Surah Summaries: Surat An-Naba

spans.note: Fairness requires warning before promising reward.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 13: Quranic Reflections (Ibrahim, Al-Hijr, An-Nahl)

spans.note: Only the misguided despair of Allah's mercy; Ibrahim corrected himself and was given a lineage of prophets.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2023 Night 27: Tahajjud Program

spans.note: Real hope in Allah's mercy is joined to belief and effort.

lectures.title: Five Additional Points to Consider During Difficult Times

spans.note: Like planting a sapling as the Hour arrives, Muslims do their part without deciding whether it will bear fruit; there is always hope.

lectures.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: The All-Encompassing, Al-Muhit

spans.note: The name both comforts, since nothing is lost, and makes one fear more.

lectures.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Ra'd, Part 5

spans.note: Reverence mixes fear, exaltation and love; fear of a bad reckoning makes people ask before they act.

lectures.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-'Aziz (The Unfathomable)

spans.note: Isa's plea gives hope that Allah can forgive even grave sins since no one questions Him.

lectures.title: The Empty Space Ep. 3: The Stages

spans.note: Punishment in the equation is what lets the short-sighted nafs choose rightly.

lectures.title: Surat Ghafir Summary

spans.note: Forgiver of sin and severe in punishment must be taught together; tilting either way distorts the deen.

lectures.title: Syria: A Personal Reflection

spans.note: He confesses he had accepted the regime as permanent and lost hope, something he says he is ashamed of.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 7: Quranic Themes, Knowing Allah

spans.note: Hold on to His mercy while fearing His punishment.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Pearls 11: Compassion (Rahma)

spans.note: No deed earns Paradise; our hope rests on Allah's mercy.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 28: Accountability

spans.note: Whoever fears Allah in this world is secure on the Day of Gathering, and whoever feels secure now will be afraid then.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ma'arij, Part 2: Verses 19-28

spans.note: A believer never feels safe from Allah's punishment; this fear motivates rather than paralyses.

lectures.title: Surat Nuh Part 2: Verses 10-20

spans.note: A healthy fear that avoids both false security and despair.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqa: Mortality, Episode 28

spans.note: Fear of not having done enough is healthy when balanced by knowing Allah does not want to punish.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2026 Night 28 - Quranic Themes: Insights

spans.note: Admit you have nothing to show and rely entirely on Allah's mercy, like Yusuf's brothers.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat An-Naba, Part 2: Verses 17-30

spans.note: Presenting Islam as only punishment or only reward misrepresents it; both wings are needed.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Value, Episode 37

spans.note: Reward, fear and love are the Quran's motives; disdaining them is arrogance.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat An-Nazi'at, Part 1: Verses 1-19

spans.note: Khashyah is reverence: respect of Allah's status, love of His essence and fear of just punishment, not fear alone.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Value, Episode 41

spans.note: Deeds are judged by endings and acceptance is unknown, so religiosity must never breed comfort.

cites.point: Only disbelievers despair of Allah's relief.
None despairs of Allah's mercy except the disbelievers; despair is forbidden.
Only the disbelievers despair of Allah's mercy, so losing hope is not permitted.
Only those astray despair of their Lord's mercy.
Who despairs of his Lord's mercy except the misguided.
Only the misguided despair of their Lord's mercy; he merges this with the Yusuf verse.
Only those with knowledge truly have khashyah of Allah
Those with knowledge truly revere Allah: khashyah is not mere fear.
Raising voices above the Prophet's voice voids deeds unnoticed.
Raising voices above the Prophet's can void deeds without one perceiving it.
The Prophet recites Allah's signs before teaching the Book, so people know Allah first
Prophets recite Allah's signs, purify and teach the Book and wisdom, so that people know Him.
Praise is the first word of the Quran.
Alhamdulillah as the Quran's first words
He has counted them all and each comes to Him alone
Allah counted it while they forgot it
Fasting is a limited number of days, now ending
Those who oppose the Messenger after guidance is clear will have their deeds voided.
Allah makes the deeds of those who disbelieve and obstruct go astray.
Deeds made into scattered dust, echoed in the Thawban hadith.
Hellfire made plain for whoever sees
Jahannam is brought and man remembers when it no longer helps
Jahannam displayed before the disbelievers
Every nation falls to its knees
Jahannam almost bursts with rage
When it sees them from afar they hear its fury and roaring
Humbled people looking at it with a furtive glance
Sparks like castles, like a line of camels
Those promised the best are kept far from it and do not hear its sound
Had the enemy entered at the Trench, many would have abandoned their faith
Allah does not forgive shirk but forgives anything else for whom He wills; it appears twice.
Isa: if You punish them they are Your servants, and if You forgive them You are the Mighty, the Wise.
Ibrahim: whoever disobeys me, You are Forgiving and Merciful.
Tell the disbelievers that if they desist, their past will be forgiven.
Tell the captives that if Allah sees good in their hearts He will give them better and forgive them.
Is there doubt about Allah, Creator of the heavens and earth? He calls you to forgive your sins.
Those who believe, emigrate and strive are the ones who hope for mercy.
The words of Yusuf to his brothers, recited at the conquest of Makkah so the Prophet would respond with the same forgiveness.
Yusuf's brothers bring goods of little value and ask him to be charitable; a model for asking Allah's mercy.
What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?
Peace, a word from a Lord most merciful, greeting the believers.
Your Lord has prescribed mercy upon Himself.
Your Lord is of vast mercy, yet His punishment is not turned from criminals.
Those whose deeds are void and given no weight on the Day of Resurrection
Keepers ask each group whether a warner came; they admit it and say had we listened or reasoned
Isa questioned about his worship: 'if You forgive them, You are the Almighty, the Wise'
Every soul tastes death and then returns to Allah.
Being told to read your own record on the Day of Judgment.
No injustice today, Allah is swift in reckoning; warn them of the approaching day when hearts are at the throats
What is this book that leaves nothing small or great unrecorded
Given a taste of mercy after hardship he says it is his due, doubts the Hour and expects good from his Lord; the ungrateful will be told what they did. Entitlement.
Favoured, man turns away and distances himself; touched by evil he is full of long prayer.
Mercy given then withdrawn leaves man despairing and ungrateful; ease after hardship makes him say the evils are gone, exultant and boastful.
Except those who persevere and do good: the one place he says the exception is spelled out.
Given a taste of mercy man exults in it, and when evil befalls him for what his hands did, he is ungrateful: the cycle in another surah.
Some rocks gush with rivers, split open or fall in awe of Allah, unlike hardened hearts.
Verses from Al-Hadid on punishment, recited as what the believer fears.
the most hopeful verse: Allah revives the earth and hearts
by the stars they find their way
Whoever thinks Allah will not grant victory should stretch a rope and see if it helps; the last verse of his opening recitation.

hadith.gist: Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him; Aisha's question about disliking death and the Prophet's explanation of the glad tidings at death.
Umm Habibah asked to enjoy long company with her family; the Prophet said terms are set and asking refuge from the grave and the Fire would be better.
Jibreel said: live as you wish, for you will die; the believer's honour is night prayer and his dignity is independence from people.
After 57:16 was revealed early on, the companions anxiously asked each other what they had done to deserve the rebuke
If the Hour comes while one of you holds a sapling, let him plant it.
Thabit ibn Qays feared that his deeds were voided after the verse on raising voices, and the Prophet told him he was among the people of paradise.
A man swore Allah would not forgive another; Allah forgave that man and voided the deeds of the one who swore.

People of my ummah will come with good deeds like the mountains of Tihamah and Allah will make them scattered dust: they are of your people and pray at night as you do, but when alone they violate Allah's limits.
The Prophet's supplication seeking refuge from committing a sin that voids deeds.
No one enters Paradise by his deeds alone, but by Allah's mercy.
A person may do the deeds of the people of the Fire until the end is near, then turn and be among the people of Paradise, and the reverse.
No one enters Paradise by his deeds, not even the Prophet, unless Allah covers him with His mercy
Jahannam will be brought on that Day with seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels
When you ask Allah, ask for al-Firdaws, the highest level of Paradise
Allah does not look at your forms but at your hearts
This religion is ease.
Allah is more merciful to His servants than a mother animal to her young
The Prophet tells companions he will meet them at the Hawd
The most beloved deeds to Allah are the most consistent.
The great intercession: people go from prophet to prophet, each says Allah is angrier today than ever before or after and worries for himself
Hadith qudsi: I will not combine two fears or two securities for My servant
While digging the trench the companions hit a boulder they could not break; the Prophet struck it three times, saying with each spark that Sham, Persia and Yemen would be conquered, and it crumbled.
Ibn Umar tells Abu Musa's son that Umar wished his deeds after the Prophet would merely break even, while Abu Musa hoped for reward; the son says Umar was wiser
A man told al-Miqdad how blessed his eyes were to have seen the Prophet; he grew angry, saying some who met the Prophet were thrown on their faces into the Fire
No one enters Paradise by his deeds alone, only by Allah's mercy.
A worshipper who claimed Paradise by his deeds found them outweighed by the single blessing of his eyesight, then entered by Allah's mercy.
His first public call: say la ilaha illallah and you will succeed.
Written on the Prophet's sword: pardon whoever wrongs you
When Allah decreed creation He wrote above His Throne: My mercy overcomes My anger.
On the Day of Judgment the prophets say their Lord is angry as never before nor after.
Allah created a hundred mercies, sent one to earth by which creatures show compassion, and will gather the ninety-nine on the Day of Judgment.
Would this woman throw her child into the fire? Allah is more merciful to His servants than she is to her child.
Hadith qudsi: I am the most free of need of partners; whoever does a deed for Me and another, I leave him with what he associated.
If a tiny opening were made in Jahannam toward this world it would burn everything
Deeds are judged by their endings.
No one enters Paradise by his deeds alone but by Allah's mercy.
Ibn Umar told Abu Burdah of Umar's wish that his deeds after the Prophet would just cancel out, while Abu Musa hoped for reward.
Salman wept at death because the Prophet made them pledge to take from the world only a traveller's provision.
The Prophet spent a whole night reciting one verse over and over: 'If You punish them, they are Your servants; if You forgive them, You are the Almighty, the Wise'
The wise one holds himself accountable and works for what comes after death; the incapable follows his desires and indulges in wishes about Allah.
Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him; asked about disliking death, the Prophet explained he meant the believer's state at death.
Allah says: I am as My servant thinks of Me.
Allah is more merciful to His servants than a mother is to her child, said while watching a mother animal feed her young.
In the last ten nights the Prophet strove as at no other time, kept the nights alive, woke his family and tightened his waist-wrap.
Allah made a hundred mercies, sent one to the world and will add it to the ninety-nine on the Day of Judgment
Allah conceals the believer while reviewing his sins and forgives them
No one's feet move on that day until asked about his life, youth, wealth and knowledge
Allah tells the people of Paradise He bestows His pleasure on them and will never be displeased with them
Allah says He will not combine for His servant two fears or two securities: whoever fears Him in this world is safe on the Day of Gathering, and whoever feels safe now will fear then.
Deeds are judged by their endings
Umar tells Abu Musa he hopes his deeds after the Prophet merely break even; Ibn Umar says his father was better
Salman weeps that the Prophet took a covenant that their provision be like a traveller's
If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much.
At the Trench the Prophet struck the boulder three times and with each spark promised the conquest of Persia, Yemen and Rome.
When a man threw sand in his face, the Prophet told his weeping daughter not to cry because Allah would grant her father success.

maxims: The battle begins on the inside
It's not over until it's over
It's not theater; this is actually your life
Don't overcomplicate your faith
Beware the wrath of the patient one
We fear His justice, not His mistreatment
Not to deserve His mercy, but to be worthy of it
We fly to Allah with two wings
Nowhere does the Quran mention Paradise without Hell
Fear is a good short-term motive, not long-term
We don't fear Allah's oppression; we fear His justice
Love is the strongest motive

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 13: Zayd, Zaynab and the Command the Prophet Found Hard (33:37-40)

spans.note: Al-Ahzab is about obeying uncomfortable commands; decisive rulings are followed even when their wisdom is unseen.
No prophet should feel distress at what Allah ordained; distress at a command means one's priorities are confused.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 22: Quranic Reflections

spans.note: Lays out the cluster as a study of obedience from difficulty, community, knowledge, life, unclear wisdom, returning and sincerity.
Ibrahim's sacrifice as the model of obeying a clear command without seeing its wisdom.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 21: Quranic Reflections on Al-Ahzab 35 to Ya-Sin 54

spans.note: The sixth cluster is about obeying Allah precisely when it is hard.
Once Allah and His Messenger decree, a believer has no option; 'it's my choice' cannot mean commands are optional, though no one may force religion.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 22: Quranic Reflections (Ya-Sin 55 to Az-Zumar 61)

spans.note: Seven angles on submission across al-Ahzab to az-Zumar, including obeying clear commands whose wisdom you cannot see.
Ibrahim's sacrifice as the clearest test of obeying without explanation; a believer has no option once Allah commands.

lectures.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The First Article, Adherence (Followship and Learning)

spans.note: Hearing and obeying in ease and hardship is the first article of the pledge: you will find wisdom in every command but may not condition obedience on it, Islam is not a buffet, and saying 'we hear and we obey' means no arguing, no defending sin and no reshaping the deen to fit you.
In Arabic: the Prophet is the scale by which everything is weighed; the ummah collapsed when it abandoned his sunnah and will only rise again by returning to it.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 6: Quranic Themes, Obeying Allah

spans.note: Bani Israel's refusal to enter the holy land cost a whole generation; obedience means acting even when afraid.
Those who turn back are replaced by a people whose love of Allah leads them to obey without fearing any blame.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Religious Adherence

spans.note: Allah's decrees are never optional for a believer; identifying as Muslim without adhering to the basic rulings does not work, and nothing in the community works without this piece. Obedience is demanded especially when it is difficult.
Hope for a better future for the ummah is empty without obedience; if Muslims turn away, Allah replaces them, so adherence is a privilege to seize.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 1: The Four Commands of Submission

spans.note: The cluster of surahs studies submission; Al-Ahzab focuses on obeying when it is hardest.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 4 (33:7-9)

spans.note: The surah's theme is submitting when obeying is hard; the heavy covenant of the prophets demands strong will.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 12 (33:35-36)

spans.note: Once Allah decides, believers do not choose; you may struggle with a ruling but must follow it.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 20: Review of the Surah, Words That Hit the Mark, and the Trust (33:70-73)

spans.note: A full review of Al-Ahzab as the surah of obeying when it is hardest, anchored in 33:36.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 21: Quranic Reflections (Al-Ahzab, Saba, Fatir)

spans.note: Obedience is required, is hardest when it matters most, and is not optional once Allah decrees; the difficulty lies in the nafs, not the command.

lectures.title: Surat As-Saff, Part 2 (Verses 5-6)

spans.note: Accept Islam as it is; struggle openly but do not haggle or rewrite the law.

lectures.title: The Laws of Success and Victory 7: Adherence
lectures.series: The Laws of Success and Victory

spans.note: Victory depends on following Allah's guidance exactly as taught and truly listening rather than merely hearing; each person must respond by capacity.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Ahzab Summary, Part 1

spans.note: Real submission means accepting revelation whole, with no exceptions, even when it is socially costly or personally painful.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Fath Summary

spans.note: The surah is the model of those who followed the Prophet even when they could not see his wisdom.

lectures.title: Surat Muhammad Summary

spans.note: Following the Prophet is the condition for accepted deeds and a functional life.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Ahzab Summary, Part 2

spans.note: The surah's thread is obeying when commands are hard: there is no choice once Allah and His Messenger decide.

lectures.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Saffat, Part 1: Verses 1-11

spans.note: Submission includes obeying commands whose wisdom we do not know, without demanding explanations.

lectures.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Saffat, Part 5: Verses 75-98

spans.note: Nuh obeyed commands he could not explain and understood them only later.

lectures.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Saffat, Part 6: Verses 99-113

spans.note: Ibrahim and Ismail submit fully to a command they could not understand, after making sure it was truly Allah's.

lectures.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Saffat, Part 7: Verses 114-148

spans.note: Submission means obeying Allah even when the wisdom of a command is hidden, trusting His knowledge.

lectures.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Saffat, Part 9: Verses 171-182

spans.note: Allah's soldiers take His commands without demanding reasons first, and victory is promised to them.

lectures.title: The Spirituality of Hajj, Part 2

spans.note: Ibrahim and Isma'il submit to a command without visible logic; every divine command is in our interest.

lectures.title: Hajj: Celebration of the Greatest Submission

spans.note: Ibrahim and Ismail model full submission to a command whose wisdom they could not see; that moment is when the word Muslim was coined, and it leaves us no argument for disobeying commands that plainly help us.

lectures.title: Arafat Lecture: The Day of Realization

spans.note: Ibrahim's submission when he saw no wisdom shows how small our own obedience is.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2026 Night 27 - Quranic Themes: Commands

spans.note: A Quranic command is binding unless evidence says otherwise, and obedience to commands is the core of what we will be asked about.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 14: Remember Allah Much (33:41-44)

spans.note: The surah's theme of obeying uncomfortable commands and avoiding distress at them.
Rulings shock those who never consulted Allah before acting; you need not like a command, but should not feel distress.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 10 (33:26-31)

spans.note: Accept rulings like the judgment of Banu Qurayzah even when they are uncomfortable; follow everything without having to enjoy everything.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 17: Fairness Among His Wives and the Etiquette of His Home (33:51-55)

spans.note: Permission and prohibition revealed together show that believers accept whatever Allah makes lawful or unlawful.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Saba, Session 1: Introduction, Praise, the Hereafter and Knowledge with Mercy

spans.note: Submission to Allah is total, and Saba extends it from the individual to society.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Saba, Session 8: Wealth Is Not Proof of Allah's Love

spans.note: Submission is giving up free will, tested when our wishes clash with Allah's.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Saba, Session 9: The Angels Questioned and the Three Rejections

spans.note: Islam asked Arabs who had nothing but free will to submit it to Allah.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 1: Quranic Reflections on Surat Al-Baqarah (1-153)

spans.note: Don't negotiate the commands down; accept Islam as it is while asking for time and help.

lectures.title: Attributes of the Prophet: Our Following of the Prophet

spans.note: Following the Prophet to his standard and putting nothing ahead of Allah and His Messenger.

lectures.title: The Journey of Hajj

spans.note: Ibrahim obeys a command he cannot rationalise.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Hashr, Part 2: Verses 5-7

spans.note: Take what the Prophet gives and refrain from what he forbids, revealed when companions resisted the fay' ruling.

lectures.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: The All-Subduer, Al-Qahhar

spans.note: All creation submits willingly; humans only choose when they will worship, and submission means giving up our will for His.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat As-Saff, Part 3: Verses 7-11

spans.note: Accept a command before understanding it; ask Allah for time and help, never for the rule to change.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2024 Night 7: Quranic Reflections on Surat Al-An'am

spans.note: Iman is proven by obeying even in food, and no one may add rulings of their own.

lectures.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Wahid Al-Ahad (The One, the Only)

spans.note: One God means one law without exemptions; shirk is attractive because it allows bargaining.

lectures.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Qahhar (The Subduer)

spans.note: Islam as submission, modelled by Ibrahim and enacted in the Hajj rites.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 24: Quranic Reflections (Ash-Shura 24 to the end of Al-Ahqaf)

spans.note: Respond to Allah as fully as you can, not flawlessly, and attend to your own response.

lectures.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Final Episode

spans.note: Knowing the One who commands makes obedience easy and every sin grave.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 30: Summary of the Quranic Clusters

spans.note: Obey when it is hard, as a community, through knowledge, even without seeing the wisdom, by always returning, and with sincerity.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Taghabun, Part 3 (Verses 9-14)

spans.note: Revelation and Sunnah are one source in two layers; the Messenger's duty was clear conveyance.

lectures.title: A Talk on Hajj: Walking in the Footsteps of Adam, Ibrahim and Muhammad

spans.note: Ibrahim obeyed without questioning, and the sacrifice celebrates that Allah commands only our good.

lectures.title: Arafah Program 2024: The Symbolism of Hajj

spans.note: Submission without questioning a clear command; letting go of what cannot be held.

lectures.title: Stages of the Hereafter: The Basin and the Bridge (Sirat)

spans.note: Those driven from the basin are those who changed his teaching, chose the parts they liked and did not walk his path.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Jathiyah Summary

spans.note: Following the whole shari'ah, not the parts we like, protects against arrogance.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Hujurat Summary

spans.note: Nothing before Allah and His Messenger; ask the shari'ah's view first.

lectures.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Saffat, Part 2: Verses 12-27

spans.note: Submission includes contentment with decrees whose purpose we never learn.

a day or part of a day; ask those who count
People asked how long they stayed on earth answer a day or part of a day, and are told they stayed only a little.
Asked how long they stayed on earth, people say a day or part of a day
A thousand months equals a full life of about 83 years, and one night outweighs it.

Within these ten nights is a night better than a lifetime, so seek it in all ten.
Humans are in loss except those who believe, do good and counsel one another: read as generational mentorship.
Humans are in loss except those who counsel one another to truth and patience.
On that Day people whisper that they stayed only ten days, or only a day

The Quran was revealed on the Night of Decree, better than a thousand months.

Angels and the Spirit descend that night.

The criminals whisper they stayed ten; the most accurate says only a day.

the best of them says you stayed only a day

The patient are given their reward without reckoning
A day of fifty thousand years

hadith.gist: Two blessings many people are cheated of: health and free time.
Allah boasts to the angels about His fasting servants and tells them He has forgiven them.

A Companion would stand in tears on the last night of Ramadan calling out: which of us was accepted so we may congratulate him, and which was rejected so we may console him; good for you who were accepted, and may Allah make up the loss of the one rejected. The report is attributed to Ali ibn Abi Talib and, in this fuller wording, to Ibn Mas'ud.
Saying he cites with the name of Anas ibn Malik: procrastination is one of Satan's great soldiers, with which he has deceived many

Saying of three things that make one laugh (the one hoping for the world while death seeks him, the heedless who is not overlooked, the one laughing unaware of his Lord's pleasure) and three that make one weep (parting from the Prophet and his companions, the terror of death, standing before Allah)
Asked by Jibril about the Hour, the Prophet replied that the one questioned knows no more about it than the questioner.
The Prophet came out to tell them the date of Laylat al-Qadr but two men were disputing, so it was taken up; seek it in the last ten nights.

There are no days in which good deeds are more beloved to Allah than these ten days; not even jihad, except a man who went out with himself and his wealth and came back with neither (narrated by Ibn Abbas).
In these days increase in tahlil, takbir and tahmid.
Remember often the destroyer of pleasures; remembering it in hardship eases it and in ease restrains it.
Fajr and Isha are the heaviest prayers, the ones that test commitment.
The Prophet prayed at night in i'tikaf, companions joined him, and he stopped coming out lest it become obligatory
Ramadan has come, a month of blessing in which Allah envelops you, sends mercy, removes sins, answers dua and boasts of you to His angels; the wretched is deprived of His mercy
Repentance is accepted until the soul reaches the throat or the sun rises from the west

The most beloved fast to Allah is the fast of Dawud, fasting every other day, and the most beloved prayer is his: sleeping half the night, praying a third and sleeping a sixth.
The Prophet secluded himself in the first, then middle, then last ten nights seeking Laylat al-Qadr.
The Prophet came out to tell its date, found two men quarrelling, and the knowledge was lifted; seek it in the odd nights of the last ten.

Seventy thousand of my ummah will enter Jannah without reckoning or punishment; Ukkasha ibn Mihsan asked to be among them and the Prophet prayed for him; when another man asked, the Prophet said Ukkasha had beaten him to it.
Your Lord has breezes (nafahat) during your days, so expose yourselves to them.

themes.label: The masjid: its role and etiquette

lectures.title: End of Ramadan Reflections

spans.note: The masjid is a launching point that recharges faith for work outside; full masjids that produce no action are worthless.
The masjid is where people return to refuel when the struggle outside wears them down.

lectures.title: Activism, Our Path Forward: Companionship and Masajid

spans.note: Every community needs a centre. The Prophet went to the masjid first and helped build it; Muslims have decentralized it and must make it welcoming, service-oriented and full.
In Muslim lands people spent, married, learned and were raised in the masjid; once that value was removed the ummah lost its way.

lectures.title: Muslim Wellness Network: Fourth Ramadan

spans.note: The masjid should welcome people and offer mentorship and companionship.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Our End of the Bargain

spans.note: What a masjid owes its congregation: the ten points, from balanced teaching to a welcoming space for all; masajid are vehicles to serve the community, not institutions to be defended.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Presence

spans.note: Presence in the masjid is the community's first obligation: attendance has fallen from most of the community to a few percent, dictators fear masajid because change happens there, and leaving because you dislike how they run fixes nothing.

lectures.title: Essentials and Pet Peeves: Community

spans.note: The masjid as a flourishing, safe, non-transactional space, to be cared for like one's home.

lectures.title: The Significance of Jumuah and Working Together

spans.note: Masjids exist to serve, not to treat worshippers as donors; the minbar is for sharing where the community stands.
An institution should serve first; a lack of support signals it is not offering value.

lectures.title: Beyond Ramadan: What We Need to Do to Be Well

spans.note: Full masjids have no innate value unless worship translates into action outside; the masjid is a training ground.
The masjid is where exhausted workers regroup and remember why; a new masjid is not an achievement in itself.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Accountability

spans.note: Nobody expects anything at the masjid, in the Middle East or the West, so masajid run like businesses and fundraise aggressively; instead the masjid should be the launching pad and measuring point of community progress.
Masajid must be transparent, answer questions, serve the right demographics and listen; members cannot treat them as another supermarket.

lectures.title: Fajr Dars: Az-Zukhruf, Verses 36-45

spans.note: A masjid is a house of service measured by people, not a business measured by money.

lectures.title: Attributes of the Prophet: How He Treated Children and Women

spans.note: Argues against barriers and exclusion of women in the masjid, calling for respectful conduct instead.

lectures.title: Tackling Contemporary Issues: Navigating Differences

spans.note: Masajid give the next generation social immunity; bring children through the week, not only on Jumuah, and revive mentorship there.

lectures.title: Three Ramadanic Reminders

spans.note: Masajid must be designed to embrace young people; the openness that matters is of mind and heart, and the annoying child who is unwelcome now will not return at fifteen.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 15: Quranic Reflections on Al-Kahf 27 to Taha 89

spans.note: A masjid without children and youth, and without a succession plan, should be worried; masajid should be busy and loud with the next generation.

lectures.title: Moral Collapse and State Failure (Reduced Concepts, Episode 1)

spans.note: Resistance to change, such as driving children out of the masjid, repels the next generation.

lectures.title: Islam, Tawheed and Following the Prophet (Reduced Concepts, Episode 2)

spans.note: The masjid is a training ground for practising Islam outside its walls.

lectures.title: Final Three Ramadan Reminders

spans.note: Full masjids mean nothing unless they launch people into work outside; the masjid is where Islam is trained.

lectures.title: Lessons Learned From Five Decades of Oppression

spans.note: Tyrants monitor masjids because they are the ummah's strength, while Muslims in the West have pushed them to the periphery and should restore them as the centre of community life.

lectures.title: Continuing After Ramadan

spans.note: Everyone must both give and receive at the masjid; it should be the umbrella under which the community lives as a family, as the Prophet's masjid was, not a place to step into for prayer and leave.

lectures.title: Surat Al-Jinn, Part 3: Verses 16-21

spans.note: Masjids are for Allah alone: places of equality without secondary gain, where people should give back rather than act entitled.

lectures.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Luqman (Introduction, verses 1-5)

lectures.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat As-Sajdah (verses 4-9)

lectures.title: Those Who Doom Themselves (Ramadan 2026, Night 11: Quranic Themes 2)

spans.note: Masajid should be lived-in, youth-welcoming spaces like the Prophet's, not quiet libraries.

lectures.title: Soft Speech (Ramadan 2026, Night 15: Quranic Themes 2)

spans.note: Masajid exist to serve and welcome; greet newcomers and learn the names of those you pray beside.

lectures.title: The Values of Islam: Brotherhood and Unity (Ukhuwwah and Jama'ah)

spans.note: Masajid exist to keep the jama'ah and must welcome everyone as guests of Allah.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Participation

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Summary

spans.note: What the masjid pledges: a welcoming space open equitably to men and women, education, mentorship, authentic teaching and no personal agendas; masajid must become the centres of society again.

lectures.title: Az-Zukhruf, Verses 11-19 (Fajr Dars)

lectures.title: A Ramadan Plan

lectures.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 28: Quranic Reflections (Nuh to Al-Balad)

lectures.title: The Five Categories of Community Investment: Outreach

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat al-Hadid, Part 6: Verses 20-23

spans.note: A mosque's value lies in service, education and mentorship, as with the Prophet's simple mosque.

lectures.title: Contemporary Issues: Principles of Gender Relationships

spans.note: He prefers an open masjid with men in front and women behind over full segregation, so people learn ethical conduct.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 17: Quranic Reflections on Al-Hajj 58 to An-Nur 64

lectures.title: Chastity, Love and Gender Relations (Reduced Concepts, Episode 5)

lectures.title: Outreach, The Way of Our Prophets: Verbal and Practical
lectures.series: Outreach: The Way of Our Prophets

spans.note: Bring people who never felt comfortable in the masjid and make sure they find something meaningful, so it becomes their community centre.

lectures.title: Seeking Knowledge: Fulfilling Our Purpose

spans.note: In the past no one sat in a masjid without an occupation of learning or teaching.

lectures.title: Seeking Knowledge: Becoming Imams

spans.note: A masjid's purpose is to educate and mentor; Islamic schools lack teachers more than buildings.

lectures.title: Stages of the Hereafter: The Shade of His Throne (Day 18)

spans.note: The masjid as the hub of service to Muslims and a compass for the heart.

lectures.title: Az-Zukhruf, Verses 46-56 (Fajr Dars)

spans.note: Imams should not be judged by voice alone; closeness to Allah matters more.

lectures.title: The Empty Space Ep. 4: The Strategies and Rules

spans.note: Good memories at the masjid create lasting love of worship; its tranquillity lifts the spirit.

lectures.title: Towards a Modern Awakening, Ep. 7: Service Mindset

spans.note: Masjids belong to Allah and exist only to serve people.

lectures.title: Ramadan 2025 Night 18: Companionship

spans.note: Older people whose friends are elsewhere struggle to enter the masjid, and parents must attend with their children rather than drop them off.

lectures.title: Pointing Out the Obvious 7: Cross-Gender Relationships

spans.note: Contrasts segregated Middle Eastern masjids with the Prophet's open masjid.

lectures.title: Surat Nuh Part 1: Verses 1-9

spans.note: Masajid should welcome and mentor through creative programmes and drop methods that fail.

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: The Rituals, Episode 16

spans.note: The ease of praying behind an imam and the habit of pressuring imams to shorten prayer.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Muddaththir, Part 5: Verses 32-41

spans.note: Masjids exist for youth to find comfort and mentorship; complaints about noise and schedules miss that purpose.

lectures.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat As-Sajdah (verses 10-16)

spans.note: Youth programmes aim to make children love the masjid.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Insan, Part 4: Verses 22-31

spans.note: Serving the masjid is an opportunity Allah can take away and give to others; ask Him to keep you in His house's service.

lectures.title: First Week of Ramadan: Taking Advantage of the Peace

lectures.title: The Values of Islam: Khidmah (Service) and Ithar (Selflessness)

spans.note: Masjids should see visitors as people to serve.

lectures.title: Receiving Allah's Bounty (Ramadan 2026, Night 9: Quranic Themes 2)

spans.note: Masajid wrongly measure their success by how many people show up.

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Yasin, Part 3 (20-32)

spans.note: Masjids should not charge for teaching the deen.

lectures.title: Our Communal Covenant: Your End of the Bargain - Initiative

spans.note: The masjid must be the Muslim's launching pad and reference point in a city; if people stop attending there is no point continuing the conversation.

lectures.title: Hajj Lessons: Knowing and Deciding

spans.note: Without a healthy dynamic between Muslims and their community centres there will be no masajid and no future.

Read Fatiha one way, every time
Leave people wishing for more, not less
Go back two or three words, never to the start
Mistakes don't bother me; unpreparedness does

themes.label: Respite and gradual luring (istidraj)

lectures.title: Surat Al-Qalam, Part 5: Verses 35-47

spans.note: Allah usually leaves wrongdoers to drift and grants them time; a sudden loss can be a mercy that wakes one up.

maxims: You can't be a Muslim and a mujrim at the same time
It just doesn't happen on your schedule
You only know something by knowing its opposite
Allah defines the list of what is good

themes.label: Clergy, claimed spiritual powers and cults

lectures.title: Surat Al-Jinn, Part 3: Verses 16-21

spans.note: No imam has special powers or a seat at the table; claimants are liars, and cult-like and papal structures have no place in Islam.

cites.point: The Prophet owns no benefit or harm for himself and does not know the unseen; he is only a warner and bringer of good news
Intercession only with Allah's permission
Warning his nearest kin: the gathering of his family
Quraysh demanded signs like those given to Musa
The splitting of the moon was not a challenge miracle

hadith.gist: You will follow the ways of the Jews and Christians before you
The Prophet gathered his clan and told each, down to Fatimah, to ask him for any of his wealth but save themselves from the Fire, since he could avail them nothing before Allah
Proofs of prophethood such as water gushing from the well at his touch and restored eyesight

maxims: You are the fluid; take the shape of the Quran
It's only a rule if you follow it when it's hard
You're not generous if you're only generous when wealthy
Anyone who claims special powers is a liar for claiming it
That's your cue to look for the exit
The only one who can't be questioned is Allah

themes.label: Softness of heart and expressing emotion

lectures.title: Ramadan 2026 Night 26 - Quranic Themes: Having Khushoo

spans.note: Men especially hide love behind a hard exterior; the Prophet's ready tears and empathy are the model of a softened heart.

maxims: Standing before Allah is an absolute bargain
The nafs loves things that are unearned
Knock on the door long enough
Every heart is the same on the inside
Ramadan is the launching pad

themes.label: Divine wisdom in what Allah conceals

lectures.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 24: Tahajjud

spans.note: He lists what Allah keeps hidden (His pleasure, His greatest name, the middle prayer, the hour of death) and shows that each concealment keeps people striving across all of the options.

cites.point: To Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call on Him by them: the setting for the hidden greatest name.
Guard the prayers and the middle prayer: the middle prayer is left unspecified so all are guarded.
No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow or in what land it will die: the hidden hour of death.

themes.label: Understanding vs agreeing vs accepting

lectures.title: Essentials and Pet Peeves: Understanding, Agreeing and Accepting

spans.note: Understanding is empathy and comprehension, distinct from legal agreement or moral acceptance.

hadith.gist: A Bedouin urinated in the masjid; the Prophet stopped the Companions and taught him gently
Ka'b ibn Malik's long account of staying behind from Tabuk and his repentance
Umar asking Hudhayfah whether he was named among the hypocrites
None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself

maxims: Understanding, agreeing and accepting are not the same thing
Any solution that lacks empathy is not a solution
Judging something follows from conceiving it

themes.label: Salawat: sending blessings on the Prophet

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 18: Salawat on the Prophet, the Sin of Harm, and the Jilbab (33:56-59)

spans.note: Salah as connection, verbal salawat and its barakah, living his way, and taslim as submission.

cites.point: Allah and His angels bless those who remember Him, parallel to 33:56.
The angels' salah is their prayer for the believers.

hadith.gist: Ubayy asked how much of his prayer to devote to salawat; told more is better each time, he said all of it and was told his worries would be removed and sins forgiven.
The Ibrahimi salawat taught for the prayer.

maxims: It counts when it is hard
His consistency made us miss his circumstances
Salah means connection
You may not do good, but do not do harm
Every verse can apply to me

themes.label: Islam as an ideology and worldview

lectures.title: The Philosophy of Islamic Thought 1: Introduction to Understanding Ideologies

spans.note: Deen as a coherent way of life analysed through the questions that define any ideology.

maxims: Academia is where public opinion begins
Ideologies are diagnoses, not prescriptions
Ideologies function like immune systems
What does an ideology distrust? The million-dollar question
Philosophy is the programming, the code
Utopias are very revealing

themes.label: Not judging where people will end up

lectures.title: Surah Summaries: Surat Al-Muddaththir

spans.note: Warn about actions but never declare anyone's final destination.

maxims: The Quran is not a catalogue of where people are going
I'm not a bookkeeper for Allah
Do your good deed and walk away
People judge an ideology by those who follow it
Take a stand

themes.label: Protecting and preserving the message of Islam

lectures.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The Fifth Article, Protecting the Message

spans.note: Every Muslim must keep Islam from being manipulated, from outside and from within; earlier messages were lost exactly this way.

cites.point: Allah's promise to preserve the Quran does not excuse us from the effort through which He preserves it.
After a defeat the believers asked why; the answer: it is from yourselves. Muslims are the main threat to Islam.
The trumpet is blown and everyone dies except whom Allah wills; our behaviour may hasten that end.

hadith.gist: Allah promised the Prophet that his ummah would not be wiped out by famine or by an external enemy, unless they kill, plunder and ruin one another.
hadith.source: Sahih Muslim and Musnad Ahmad (as he states)

hadith.gist: Between the two blowings of the trumpet is forty; no one knows forty of what.
After the trumpet, the angel of death is commanded to take the life of the trumpet's blower, then of Jibril, then his own, until only Allah remains.

maxims: Protecting him was protecting the message
We continue to be the biggest threat to Islam
Protecting Islam protects your family
The corrupt hand of man always finds its way
Deep down we are still the grade six kid

themes.label: Blindly following forefathers and inherited tradition

lectures.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 22: Quranic Reflections (Ya-Sin 55 to Az-Zumar 61)

spans.note: Sift what you inherit respectfully, keeping the good and letting go of the rest, as medicine does with Ibn Sina.

maxims: Sincerity is the mother of all good deeds of the heart
Cook the idea, marinate it, let it brew
Allah requires lifetimes of contemplation
A true believer sees no options when Allah commands
Letting go safely does not mean disrespecting those before us

themes.label: Immigration and welcoming newcomers

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Hashr, Part 3: Verses 8-9

spans.note: Most Muslims in Canada are immigrants; the Ansar's love for newcomers stands against today's anti-immigrant narratives.

cites.point: The hypocrites' toxic narrative against the emigrants

hadith.gist: The Ansar refused land in Bahrain unless the Muhajirun were given the same

maxims: Dangerous people are those who have nothing to lose
Less law, more values among Muslims
Be selfless now so you can be selfish later
Paradise is the ultimate selfishness
You cannot remove selfishness, only protect yourself from it

themes.label: The relationship between preachers and their congregation

lectures.title: London Muslim Survey (Part 1)

spans.note: Listeners accept Allah's law unconditionally and voice their struggles. Preachers listen, give time and never judge. Pandering and harshness both fail.

cites.point: The verse he recites: what some People of the Book said to their prophet vs what they should have said. The model of hearing, accepting and asking for time.
'O you who believe, do not say ra'ina': where the relationship is first introduced.

hadith.gist: When a companion punished for public drinking was cursed, the Prophet forbade it, saying he knew only that the man loved Allah and His Messenger.

maxims: Come to Islam as you are, to Islam as it is
Accept unconditionally, then ask for time
We must change to fit Islam, not the reverse
It's a two-way road
Show me the money

themes.label: Strength and power in every domain

lectures.title: The Values of Islam: Strength and Forbearance (Quwwah and Hilm)

spans.note: Strength protects truth and prevents moral collapse; weakness comes from loving this life above one's values.

cites.point: Prepare against your enemy whatever strength you can
The best to hire is the strong and trustworthy
Shu'ayb's people: were it not for your clan we would have stoned you
Sulayman's letter: do not be arrogant, come to me in submission
Sheba's chiefs boast of their strength and might
The queen submits with Sulayman to Allah
Nine men plot to kill Salih and his family by night

hadith.gist: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and in both there is good
Those before you were destroyed because they let the noble thief go and punished the weak
Nations will invite one another to devour you as diners to a dish, not because you are few but because of wahn: love of the world and hatred of death

maxims: Laws are written for the weak
Bring the strength out, then restrain it
If living comes first, you sell out everything else
Strength protects from moral collapse; hilm protects from moral corruption
A weak Muslim today helps no one

themes.label: Similes and examples in the Quran

lectures.title: Ramadan 2026 Night 25 - Quranic Themes: Similes and Examples

spans.note: He presents the Quran's similes as a teaching method whose accuracy and timelessness preserved its credibility, then decodes three of them.

hadith.gist: A person who keeps praying (at night) will have its blessing show in his face.

maxims: If you can't give an example, don't teach it
A bad example makes you question the point
We are planting seeds of iman
Every kid in this masjid is my child
They'll become their crop, not yours

themes.label: Truth and falsehood (haqq and batil)

lectures.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Ra'd, Part 4

spans.note: Falsehood is froth that rises first and vanishes; what benefits people stays, so do not be fooled by its apparent dominance.

maxims: My job is to offer knowledge, not exemptions
Everyone wants a guy; the prophets were never that guy
That's their sujud: doing what they were created for
Falsehood is froth: first on top, first thrown away
What benefits people stays
We're just shadows, here for a little bit

themes.label: Creation, time and science

lectures.title: Tafseer of Surat al-Hadid, Part 2: Verses 4-10

spans.note: The six days are periods creatures need; creation unfolding over billions of years is more impressive than instant magic and does not diminish 'Be and it is'.

cites.point: Creation of the heavens and earth caused Allah no fatigue, so there was no day of rest.
'Be and it is' signals that His will is certain, not that things happen instantly.

maxims: Materialism and spirituality are not opposites
The worse things are for you, the more you give
Tawakkul only exists after you have done your best
Take off the masks and speak to Allah
Dua is not Aladdin's lamp

themes.label: Respect in relationships and reverence of Allah

lectures.title: Surat Nuh Part 2: Verses 10-20

spans.note: No relationship survives without respect; Allah honoured humanity and asks for reverence in return.

cites.point: The angels commanded to prostrate to Adam as a sign of respect
Allah has honoured the children of Adam

maxims: Science explains the how; we already know the who
Never refuse a scientific theory because of religion
The more you understand the how, the more you respect the who
Love without respect is possession
Don't be happy with the numbers; look at the percentages

themes.label: Desires of the self (hawa) and resisting them

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Pearls 10: Principles and Tools of Tazkiyah

spans.note: Following desire as worship of the self, even distorting one's image of Allah.

cites.point: The one who takes his own desire as his god
The second occurrence of the same wording, read also as shaping one's god to fit desire

hadith.gist: What the Prophet feared most for his ummah: greed obeyed, desire followed and everyone admiring his own opinion

maxims: You'll be surprised what you can live with
The goal is not to break the self
Allah is not who you want Him to be
Consider your nafs a child
Leaving a sin leaves a void; fill it

themes.label: Lifestyle, sleep, diet and physical health

lectures.title: Tazkiyah Pearls 10: Principles and Tools of Tazkiyah

spans.note: Sleep, eating, routine and fitness as foundations of spiritual work.

hadith.gist: The son of Adam fills no vessel worse than his stomach; a third for food, a third for drink, a third for breath

maxims: You'll be surprised what you can live with
The goal is not to break the self
Allah is not who you want Him to be
Consider your nafs a child
Leaving a sin leaves a void; fill it

themes.label: Fulfillment and living well (hayat tayyibah)

lectures.title: Understanding Islam: The Outcomes (Part 1)

spans.note: Islam promises a good life here as well as Paradise; inner fulfillment from Allah fills the void nothing else can and frees you from others' leverage.

cites.point: The believer lives a good life, at ease, finding a paradise in this life before the next.

maxims: The goal is not to live with wealth, it's to live well
No one has leverage on you
Islam is highly functional in its simplest form
Get the recipe right and you get the cake
Selflessness now in order to enjoy selfishness later
Someone who learned from someone who learned from Muhammad

themes.label: Harmony with creation and sense of direction

lectures.title: Understanding Islam: The Outcomes (Part 1)

spans.note: The believer feels part of one family and one creation, speaks kindly to it as the Prophet did, and always knows where he is facing and why.

hadith.gist: On seeing the new crescent the Prophet would address it: my Lord and your Lord is Allah, a crescent of goodness and guidance.

maxims: The goal is not to live with wealth, it's to live well
No one has leverage on you
Islam is highly functional in its simplest form
Get the recipe right and you get the cake
Selflessness now in order to enjoy selfishness later
Someone who learned from someone who learned from Muhammad

themes.label: Muru'ah: nobility, dignity and chivalry

lectures.title: The Values of Islam: Nobility and Generosity (Muru'ah and Karam)

spans.note: Muru'ah is the full realization of humanity, shown by the Prophet and by a non-Muslim's noble escort of Umm Salamah.

hadith.gist: Khadijah: Allah will never disgrace you; you keep ties of kinship, carry the burdens of the weak, give to the destitute and help in hardship

maxims: Muru'ah is being truly human
Do what adorns character; leave what dents it
Half of muru'ah is generosity
Islam only purified the intention

themes.label: Physical health and the body as a trust

lectures.title: The Philosophy of Islamic Thought #6: Psychology, Physical Health and the Lifestyle of Wellness in Islam

spans.note: The body is entrusted: avoid harm, excess and neglect, and eat lightly.

hadith.gist: Cleanliness is half of faith
No vessel is worse to fill than the stomach; a third for food, a third for drink, a third for breath

maxims: Garbage in, garbage out
You cannot change human nature, only human behaviour
The nafs is your best cheerleader
The more you eat, the more you sleep
Balance is harder than extremism
Heal a suffering soul by healing another

themes.label: Hindering others: discouragement and false ease

lectures.title: Surat Al-Ahzab Summary, Part 2

spans.note: People are held back both by those who crush their resolve and by those who promise victory without sacrifice.

maxims: Servants tested by kindness, not by trial
Hard circumstances expose people
When Allah chooses, we do not choose with Him

17:23.ar: ۞وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنًاۚ إِمَّا يَبۡلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلۡكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوۡ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفࣲّ وَلَا تَنۡهَرۡهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوۡلࣰ ا كَرِيمࣰ ا
17:23.en: Thy Lord hath decreed, that ye worship none save Him, and (that ye show) kindness to parents. If one of them or both of them attain old age with thee, say not "Fie" unto them nor repulse them, but speak unto them a gracious word

17:24.ar: وَٱخۡفِضۡ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحۡمَةِ وَقُل رَّبِّ ٱرۡحَمۡهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرࣰ ا
17:24.en: And lower unto them the wing of submission through mercy, and say: My Lord! Have mercy on them both as they did care for me when I was little

70:21.en: And, when good befalleth him, grudging

18:10.ar: إِذۡ أَوَى ٱلۡفِتۡيَةُ إِلَى ٱلۡكَهۡفِ فَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحۡمَةࣰ وَهَيِّئۡ لَنَا مِنۡ أَمۡرِنَا رَشَدࣰ ا
18:10.en: When the young men fled for refuge to the Cave and said: Our Lord! Give us mercy from Thy presence, and shape for us right conduct in our plight

18:16.ar: وَإِذِ ٱعۡتَزَلۡتُمُوهُمۡ وَمَا يَعۡبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ فَأۡوُۥٓاْ إِلَى ٱلۡكَهۡفِ يَنشُرۡ لَكُمۡ رَبُّكُم مِّن رَّحۡمَتِهِۦ وَيُهَيِّئۡ لَكُم مِّنۡ أَمۡرِكُم مِّرۡفَقࣰ ا
18:16.en: And when ye withdraw from them and that which they worship except Allah, then seek refuge in the Cave; your Lord will spread for you of His mercy and will prepare for you a pillow in your plight

18:9.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبۡتَ أَنَّ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡكَهۡفِ وَٱلرَّقِيمِ كَانُواْ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا عَجَبًا
18:9.en: Or deemest thou that the People of the Cave and the Inscription are a wonder among Our portents

9:128.ar: لَقَدۡ جَآءَكُمۡ رَسُولࣱ مِّنۡ أَنفُسِكُمۡ عَزِيزٌ عَلَيۡهِ مَا عَنِتُّمۡ حَرِيصٌ عَلَيۡكُم بِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ رَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
9:128.en: There hath come unto you a messenger, (one) of yourselves, unto whom aught that ye are overburdened is grievous, full of concern for you, for the believers full of pity, merciful

10:26.ar: ۞لِّلَّذِينَ أَحۡسَنُواْ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ وَزِيَادَةࣱۖ وَلَا يَرۡهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمۡ قَتَرࣱ وَلَا ذِلَّةٌۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلۡجَنَّةِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
10:26.en: For those who do good is the best (reward) and more (thereto). Neither dust nor ignominy cometh near their faces. Such are rightful owners of the Garden; they will abide therein

7:156.ar: ۞وَٱكۡتُبۡ لَنَا فِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةࣰ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ إِنَّا هُدۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَۚ قَالَ عَذَابِيٓ أُصِيبُ بِهِۦ مَنۡ أَشَآءُۖ وَرَحۡمَتِي وَسِعَتۡ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۚ فَسَأَكۡتُبُهَا لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
7:156.en: And ordain for us in this world that which is good, and in the Hereafter (that which is good), Lo! We have turned unto Thee. He said: I smite with My punishment whom I will, and My mercy embraceth all things, therefore I shall ordain it for those who ward off (evil) and pay the poor-due, and those who believe Our revelations

6:12.ar: قُل لِّمَن مَّا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ قُل لِّلَّهِۚ كَتَبَ عَلَىٰ نَفۡسِهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَةَۚ لَيَجۡمَعَنَّكُمۡ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ لَا رَيۡبَ فِيهِۚ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
6:12.en: Say: Unto whom belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth? Say: Unto Allah. He hath prescribed for Himself mercy, that He may bring you all together to the Day of Resurrection whereof there is no doubt. Those who ruin their souls will not believe

4:76.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱلطَّٰغُوتِ فَقَٰتِلُوٓاْ أَوۡلِيَآءَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۖ إِنَّ كَيۡدَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ كَانَ ضَعِيفًا
4:76.en: Those who believe do battle for the cause of Allah; and those who disbelieve do battle for the cause of idols. So fight the minions of the devil. Lo! the devil's strategy is ever weak

23:115.ar: أَفَحَسِبۡتُمۡ أَنَّمَا خَلَقۡنَٰكُمۡ عَبَثࣰ ا وَأَنَّكُمۡ إِلَيۡنَا لَا تُرۡجَعُونَ
23:115.en: Deemed ye then that We had created you for naught, and that ye would not be returned unto Us

51:56.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡتُ ٱلۡجِنَّ وَٱلۡإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُونِ
51:56.en: I created the jinn and humankind only that they might worship Me

11:118.ar: وَلَوۡ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ لَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰۖ وَلَا يَزَالُونَ مُخۡتَلِفِينَ
11:118.en: And if thy Lord had willed, He verily would have made mankind one nation, yet they cease not differing

11:119.ar: إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَ رَبُّكَۚ وَلِذَٰلِكَ خَلَقَهُمۡۗ وَتَمَّتۡ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ لَأَمۡلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ ٱلۡجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجۡمَعِينَ
11:119.en: Save him on whom thy Lord hath mercy; and for that He did create them. And the Word of thy Lord hath been fulfilled: Verily I shall fill hell with the jinn and mankind together

49:13.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرࣲ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ شُعُوبࣰ ا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ أَكۡرَمَكُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتۡقَىٰكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرࣱ‏
49:13.en: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct. Lo! Allah is Knower, Aware

10:32.ar: فَذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمُ ٱلۡحَقُّۖ فَمَاذَا بَعۡدَ ٱلۡحَقِّ إِلَّا ٱلضَّلَٰلُۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُصۡرَفُونَ
10:32.en: Such then is Allah, your rightful Lord. After the Truth what is there saving error? How then are ye turned away

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

2:29.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَسَوَّىٰهُنَّ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲۚ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
2:29.en: He it is Who created for you all that is in the earth. Then turned He to the heaven, and fashioned it as seven heavens. And He is knower of all things

14:32.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ رِزۡقࣰ ا لَّكُمۡۖ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ لِتَجۡرِيَ فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِأَمۡرِهِۦۖ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرَ
14:32.en: Allah is He Who created the heavens and the earth, and causeth water to descend from the sky, thereby producing fruits as food for you, and maketh the ships to be of service unto you, that they may run upon the sea at His command, and hath made of service unto you the rivers

14:33.ar: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ دَآئِبَيۡنِۖ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ
14:33.en: And maketh the sun and the moon, constant in their courses, to be of service unto you, and hath made of service unto you the night and the day

2:129.ar: رَبَّنَا وَٱبۡعَثۡ فِيهِمۡ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِكَ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
2:129.en: Our Lord! And raise up in their midst a messenger from among them who shall recite unto them Thy revelations, and shall instruct them in the Scripture and in wisdom and shall make them grow. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Mighty, Wise

2:151.ar: كَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا فِيكُمۡ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنكُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا وَيُزَكِّيكُمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُم مَّا لَمۡ تَكُونُواْ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:151.en: Even as We have sent unto you a messenger from among you, who reciteth unto you Our revelations and causeth you to grow, and teacheth you the Scripture and wisdom, and teacheth you that which ye knew not

62:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي بَعَثَ فِي ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبۡلُ لَفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
62:2.en: He it is Who hath sent among the unlettered ones a messenger of their own, to recite unto them His revelations and to make them grow, and to teach them the Scripture and wisdom, though heretofore they were indeed in error manifest

3:164.ar: لَقَدۡ مَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ إِذۡ بَعَثَ فِيهِمۡ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنۡ أَنفُسِهِمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبۡلُ لَفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينٍ
3:164.en: Allah verily hath shown grace to the believers by sending unto them a messenger of their own who reciteth unto them His revelations, and causeth them to grow, and teacheth them the Scripture and wisdom; although before (he came to them) they were in flagrant error

17:37.ar: وَلَا تَمۡشِ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مَرَحًاۖ إِنَّكَ لَن تَخۡرِقَ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَلَن تَبۡلُغَ ٱلۡجِبَالَ طُولࣰ ا
17:37.en: And walk not in the earth exultant. Lo! thou canst not rend the earth, nor canst thou stretch to the height of the hills

17:36.ar: وَلَا تَقۡفُ مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌۚ إِنَّ ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَٱلۡبَصَرَ وَٱلۡفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ كَانَ عَنۡهُ مَسۡـُٔولࣰ ا
17:36.en: (O man), follow not that whereof thou hast no knowledge. Lo! the hearing and the sight and the heart - of each of these it will be asked

34:13.ar: يَعۡمَلُونَ لَهُۥ مَا يَشَآءُ مِن مَّحَٰرِيبَ وَتَمَٰثِيلَ وَجِفَانࣲ كَٱلۡجَوَابِ وَقُدُورࣲ رَّاسِيَٰتٍۚ ٱعۡمَلُوٓاْ ءَالَ دَاوُۥدَ شُكۡرࣰ اۚ وَقَلِيلࣱ مِّنۡ عِبَادِيَ ٱلشَّكُورُ
34:13.en: They made for him what he willed: synagogues and statues, basins like wells and boilers built into the ground. Give thanks, O House of David! Few of My bondmen are thankful

20:124.ar: وَمَنۡ أَعۡرَضَ عَن ذِكۡرِي فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ مَعِيشَةࣰ ضَنكࣰ ا وَنَحۡشُرُهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ أَعۡمَىٰ
20:124.en: But he who turneth away from remembrance of Me, his will be a narrow life, and I shall bring him blind to the assembly on the Day of Resurrection

20:125.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرۡتَنِيٓ أَعۡمَىٰ وَقَدۡ كُنتُ بَصِيرࣰ ا
20:125.en: He will say: My Lord! Wherefor hast Thou gathered me (hither) blind, when I was wont to see

20:126.ar: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ أَتَتۡكَ ءَايَٰتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَاۖ وَكَذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُنسَىٰ
20:126.en: He will say: So (it must be). Our revelations came unto thee but thou didst forget them. In like manner thou art forgotten this Day

18:22.ar: سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلَٰثَةࣱ رَّابِعُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ وَيَقُولُونَ خَمۡسَةࣱ سَادِسُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ رَجۡمَۢا بِٱلۡغَيۡبِۖ وَيَقُولُونَ سَبۡعَةࣱ وَثَامِنُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡۚ قُل رَّبِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ بِعِدَّتِهِم مَّا يَعۡلَمُهُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱۗ فَلَا تُمَارِ فِيهِمۡ إِلَّا مِرَآءࣰ ظَٰهِرࣰ ا وَلَا تَسۡتَفۡتِ فِيهِم مِّنۡهُمۡ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:22.en: (Some) will say: They were three, their dog the fourth, and (some) say: Five, their dog the sixth, guessing at random; and (some) say: Seven, and their dog the eighth. Say (O Muhammad): My Lord is Best Aware of their number. None knoweth them save a few. So contend not concerning them except with an outward contending, and ask not any of them to pronounce concerning them

74:31.ar: وَمَا جَعَلۡنَآ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلنَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَٰٓئِكَةࣰۖ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا عِدَّتَهُمۡ إِلَّا فِتۡنَةࣰ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِيَسۡتَيۡقِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَيَزۡدَادَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِيمَٰنࣰ ا وَلَا يَرۡتَابَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَلِيَقُولَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضࣱ وَٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلࣰ اۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَۚ وَمَا هِيَ إِلَّا ذِكۡرَىٰ لِلۡبَشَرِ
74:31.en: We have appointed only angels to be wardens of the Fire, and their number have We made to be a stumbling-block for those who disbelieve; that those to whom the Scripture hath been given may have certainty, and that believers may increase in faith; and that those to whom the Scripture hath been given and believers may not doubt; and that those in whose hearts there is disease, and disbelievers, may say: What meaneth Allah by this similitude? Thus Allah sendeth astray whom He will, and whom He will He guideth. None knoweth the hosts of thy Lord save Him. This is naught else than a Reminder unto mortals

16:91.ar: وَأَوۡفُواْ بِعَهۡدِ ٱللَّهِ إِذَا عَٰهَدتُّمۡ وَلَا تَنقُضُواْ ٱلۡأَيۡمَٰنَ بَعۡدَ تَوۡكِيدِهَا وَقَدۡ جَعَلۡتُمُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ كَفِيلًاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تَفۡعَلُونَ
16:91.en: Fulfil the covenant of Allah when ye have covenanted, and break not your oaths after the asseveration of them, and after ye have made Allah surety over you. Lo! Allah knoweth what ye do

38:29.ar: كِتَٰبٌ أَنزَلۡنَٰهُ إِلَيۡكَ مُبَٰرَكࣱ لِّيَدَّبَّرُوٓاْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
38:29.en: (This is) a Scripture that We have revealed unto thee, full of blessing, that they may ponder its revelations, and that men of understanding may reflect

4:82.ar: أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَۚ وَلَوۡ كَانَ مِنۡ عِندِ غَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِ لَوَجَدُواْ فِيهِ ٱخۡتِلَٰفࣰ ا كَثِيرࣰ ا
4:82.en: Will they not then ponder on the Qur'an? If it had been from other than Allah they would have found therein much incongruity

25:52.ar: فَلَا تُطِعِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ وَجَٰهِدۡهُم بِهِۦ جِهَادࣰ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
25:52.en: So obey not the disbelievers, but strive against them herewith with a great endeavour

28:56.ar: إِنَّكَ لَا تَهۡدِي مَنۡ أَحۡبَبۡتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِٱلۡمُهۡتَدِينَ
28:56.en: Lo! thou (O Muhammad) guidest not whom thou lovest, but Allah guideth whom He will. And He is Best Aware of those who walk aright

93:11.en: Therefor of the bounty of thy Lord be thy discourse

28:49.ar: قُلۡ فَأۡتُواْ بِكِتَٰبࣲ مِّنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ أَهۡدَىٰ مِنۡهُمَآ أَتَّبِعۡهُ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
28:49.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Then bring a scripture from the presence of Allah that giveth clearer guidance than these two (that) I may follow it, if ye are truthful

11:13.ar: أَمۡ يَقُولُونَ ٱفۡتَرَىٰهُۖ قُلۡ فَأۡتُواْ بِعَشۡرِ سُوَرࣲ مِّثۡلِهِۦ مُفۡتَرَيَٰتࣲ وَٱدۡعُواْ مَنِ ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
11:13.en: Or they say: He hath invented it. Say: Then bring ten surahs, the like thereof, invented, and call on everyone ye can beside Allah, if ye are truthful
